1:1.pada_sa: धर्मक्षेत्रे, कुरुक्षेत्रे, समवेताः, युयुत्सवः, मामकाः, पाण्डवाः, च, एव, किम्, अकुर्वत, सञ्जय ॥ १ ॥
1:1.anvaya_sa: सञ्जय, धर्मक्षेत्रे, कुरुक्षेत्रे, समवेताः, युयुत्सवः, मामकाः, च, एव, पाण्डवाः, किम्, अकुर्वत ॥ १ ॥
1:1.pada_iast: dharmakṣetre, kurukṣetre, samavetāḥ, yuyutsavaḥ, māmakāḥ, pāṇḍavāḥ, ca, eva, kim, akurvata, sañjaya || 1 ||
1:1.anvaya_iast: sañjaya, dharmakṣetre, kurukṣetre, samavetāḥ, yuyutsavaḥ, māmakāḥ, ca, eva, pāṇḍavāḥ, kim, akurvata || 1 ||
1:1.translation: Dhritarashtra said: O Sanjaya, assembled on the holy field of Kurukshetra and desiring to fight, what did my sons and the sons of Pandu do?
1:1.explanation: The Gita opens with the blind king Dhritarashtra asking his secretary Sanjaya about the battle. The word "dharma-kṣhetre" (field of dharma) is significant — Kurukshetra is not just a battlefield but a place of righteousness. By calling it "dharma-kshetra," the text foreshadows that the outcome will favor dharma. The king's anxiety is revealed by "māmakāḥ" (my sons) vs "pāṇḍavāḥ" (sons of Pandu) — he separates them, showing his bias.
1:1.word_meanings: dhṛtarāśhtraḥ — King Dhritarashtra; uvācha — said; dharma-kṣhetre — holy land; kuru-kṣhetre — Kurukshetra; samavetāḥ — assembled; yuyutsavaḥ — desiring to fight; māmakāḥ — my sons; pāṇḍavāḥ — sons of Pandu; cha — and; eva — certainly; kim — what; akurvata — did they do; sañjaya — Sanjaya

1:2.pada_sa: दृष्ट्वा, तु, पाण्डवानीकं, व्यूढं, दुर्योधनः, तदा आचार्यम् ,उपसंगम्य, राजा, वचनम्, अब्रवीत् ॥ २ ॥
1:2.anvaya_sa: तदा, राजा, दुर्योधनः, व्यूढं, पाण्डवानीकं, दृष्ट्वा, तु, आचार्यम्, उपसंगम्य, वचनम् , अब्रवीत् ॥ २ ॥
1:2.pada_iast: dṛṣṭvā, tu, pāṇḍavānīkaṃ, vyūḍhaṃ, duryodhanaḥ, tadā ācāryam ,upasaṃgamya, rājā, vacanam, abravīt || 2 ||
1:2.anvaya_iast: tadā, rājā, duryodhanaḥ, vyūḍhaṃ, pāṇḍavānīkaṃ, dṛṣṭvā, tu, ācāryam, upasaṃgamya, vacanam , abravīt || 2 ||
1:2.translation: Sanjaya said: Seeing the army of the Pandavas arranged in military formation, King Duryodhana approached his teacher Dronacharya and spoke these words.
1:2.explanation: Duryodhana's first instinct upon seeing the Pandava army is to run to his teacher Drona — not to strategize, but to seek reassurance. This reveals his insecurity despite having the larger army. The word "vyūḍham" (arranged in formation) indicates the Pandavas are well-organized, which disturbs Duryodhana.
1:2.word_meanings: sañjayaḥ — Sanjaya; uvācha — said; dṛṣhṭvā — seeing; tu — but; pāṇḍava-anīkam — army of Pandavas; vyūḍham — arranged in formation; duryodhanaḥ — King Duryodhana; tadā — then; āchāryam — teacher (Dronacharya); upasaṅgamya — approaching; rājā — king; vachanam — words; abravīt — spoke

1:3.pada_sa: पश्य, एताम्, पाण्डुपुत्राणाम्, आचार्य, महतीं, चमूं, व्यूढाम्, द्रुपदपुत्रेण, तव, शिष्येण, धीमता ॥ ३ ॥
1:3.anvaya_sa: आचार्य, तव, धीमता, शिष्येण, द्रुपदपुत्रेण, व्यूढाम्, पाण्डुपुत्राणाम्, एताम्, महतीम्, चमूम्, पश्य ॥ ३ ॥
1:3.pada_iast: paśya, etām, pāṇḍuputrāṇām, ācārya, mahatīṃ, camūṃ, vyūḍhām, drupadaputreṇa, tava, śiṣyeṇa, dhīmatā || 3 ||
1:3.anvaya_iast: ācārya, tava, dhīmatā, śiṣyeṇa, drupadaputreṇa, vyūḍhām, pāṇḍuputrāṇām, etām, mahatīm, camūm, paśya || 3 ||
1:3.translation: O teacher, (please) see this vast army of the sons of Pandu, arrayed for battle by the son of Drupada, your intelligent disciple.
1:3.word_meanings: पश्य — behold; एताम् — this; पाण्डुपुत्राणाम् — of the sons of Pandu; आचार्य — O Teacher; महतीम् — great; चमूम् — army; व्यूढाम् — arrayed; द्रुपदपुत्रेण — son of Drupada; तव शिष्येण — by your disciple; धीमता — wise.No

1:4.pada_sa: अत्र, शूराः, महेष्वासाः, भीमार्जुनसमाः, युधि, युयुधानः, विराटः, च ,द्रुपदः, च, महारथः ॥ ४ ॥
1:4.anvaya_sa: अत्र, महेष्वासाः, युधि, भीमार्जुनसमाः, शूराः, युयुधानः, च, विराटः, च, महारथः, द्रुपदः ॥ ४ ॥
1:4.pada_iast: atra, śūrāḥ, maheṣvāsāḥ, bhīmārjunasamāḥ, yudhi, yuyudhānaḥ, virāṭaḥ, ca ,drupadaḥ, ca, mahārathaḥ || 4 ||
1:4.anvaya_iast: atra, maheṣvāsāḥ, yudhi, bhīmārjunasamāḥ, śūrāḥ, yuyudhānaḥ, ca, virāṭaḥ, ca, mahārathaḥ, drupadaḥ || 4 ||
1:4.translation: Here are the heroes wielding great bows, who in battle are compeers of Bhima and Arjuna: Yuyudhana (Satyaki) and Virata, and the maharatha (great chariot-rider) Drupada;
1:4.explanation: Technically? maharatha means a warrior who is proficient in the science of war and who is able to fight alone with ten thousand archers.
1:4.word_meanings: अत्र — here; शूराः — heroes; महेष्वासाः — mighty archers; भीमार्जुनसमाः — eal to Bhima and Arjuna; युधि — in battle; युयुधानः — Yuyudhana; विराटः — Virata; च — and; द्रुपदः — Drupada; च — and; महारथः — of the great car.

1:5.pada_sa: धृष्टकेतुः, चेकितानः, काशीराजः, च, वीर्यवान्, पुरुजित्, कुन्तिभोजः, च, शैब्यः, च, नरपुंगवः ॥ ५ ॥
1:5.anvaya_sa: धृष्टकेतुः, चेकितानः, काशीराजः, च, वीर्यवान्, पुरुजित्,  कुन्तिभोजः, च, शैब्यः, च, नरपुंगवः ॥ ५ ॥
1:5.pada_iast: dhṛṣṭaketuḥ, cekitānaḥ, kāśīrājaḥ, ca, vīryavān, purujit, kuntibhojaḥ, ca, śaibyaḥ, ca, narapuṃgavaḥ || 5 ||
1:5.anvaya_iast: dhṛṣṭaketuḥ, cekitānaḥ, kāśīrājaḥ, ca, vīryavān, purujit,  kuntibhojaḥ, ca, śaibyaḥ, ca, narapuṃgavaḥ || 5 ||
1:5.translation: Dhrstaketu, Cekitana, and the valiant king of Kasi (Varanasi); Purujit and Kuntibhoja, and Saibya, the choicest among men;
1:5.word_meanings: धृष्टकेतुः — Dhrishtaketu; चेकितानः — Chekitana; काशिराजः — king of Kasi; च — and; वीर्यवान् — valiant; पुरुजित् — Purujit; कुन्तिभोजः — Kuntibhoja; च — and; शैब्यः — son of Sibi; च — and; नरपुङ्गवः — the best of men.No

1:6.pada_sa: युधामन्युः, च, विक्रान्तः, उत्तमौजाः, च, वीर्यवान्, सौभद्रः, द्रौपदेयाः, च, सर्वे, एव, महारथाः ॥ ६ ॥
1:6.anvaya_sa: युधामन्युः,च, विक्रान्तः, उत्तमौजाः, च, वीर्यवान्, सौभद्रः, द्रौपदेयाः, च, सर्वे, एव, महारथाः ॥ ६ ॥
1:6.pada_iast: yudhāmanyuḥ, ca, vikrāntaḥ, uttamaujāḥ, ca, vīryavān, saubhadraḥ, draupadeyāḥ, ca, sarve, eva, mahārathāḥ || 6 ||
1:6.anvaya_iast: yudhāmanyuḥ,ca, vikrāntaḥ, uttamaujāḥ, ca, vīryavān, saubhadraḥ, draupadeyāḥ, ca, sarve, eva, mahārathāḥ || 6 ||
1:6.translation: And the chivalrous Yudhamanyu, and the valiant Uttamaujas; son of Subhadra (Abhimanyu) and the sons of Draupadi  all (of whom) are, verily, maharathas.

sa: अस्माकं तु विशिष्टा ये तान्निबोध द्विजोत्तम
नायका मम सैन्यस्य संज्ञार्थं तान्ब्रवीमि ते
iast: asmākaṁ tu viśiṣhṭā ye tānnibodha dwijottama
nāyakā mama sainyasya sanjñārthaṁ tānbravīmi te

1:7.pada_sa: अस्माकम्, तु, विशिष्टाः, ये, तान्, निबोध, द्विजोत्तम, नायकाः, मम, सैन्यस्य, संज्ञार्थम्, तान्, बवीमि, ते ॥ ७ ॥

1:7.anvaya_iast: dvijottama, asmākaṃ, tu, ye, viśiṣṭāḥ, tān, nibodha, te, saṃjñārthaṃ, mama, sainyasya, nāyakāḥ, tān, bravīmi || 7 ||
1:7.translation: But, O best among the Brahmanas, please be appraised of those who are foremost among us, the ?nders of my army. I speak of them to you by way of example.
1:7.word_meanings: अस्माकम् — ours; तु — also; विशिष्टाः — the best; ये — who (those); तान् — those; निबोध — know (thou); द्विजोत्तम (O) — best among the twicorn ones; नायकाः — the leaders; मम — my; सैन्यस्य — of the army; संज्ञार्थम् — for information; तान् — them; ब्रवीमि — speak; ते — to thee.No

1:8.pada_sa: भवान्, भीष्मः, च, कर्णः, च, कृपः, च, समितिञ्जयः, अश्वत्थामा, विकर्णः, च, सौमदत्तिः, जयद्रथः ॥ ८ ॥
1:8.anvaya_sa: भवान्, भीष्मः, च, कर्णः, च, समितिंजयः, कृपः, च, अश्वत्थामा, विकर्णः, च, सौमदत्तिः, जयद्रथः ॥ ८ ॥
1:8.pada_iast: bhavān, bhīṣmaḥ, ca, karṇaḥ, ca, kṛpaḥ, ca, samitiñjayaḥ, aśvatthāmā, vikarṇaḥ, ca, saumadattiḥ, jayadrathaḥ || 8 ||
1:8.anvaya_iast: bhavān, bhīṣmaḥ, ca, karṇaḥ, ca, samitiṃjayaḥ, kṛpaḥ, ca, aśvatthāmā, vikarṇaḥ, ca, saumadattiḥ, jayadrathaḥ || 8 ||
1:8.translation: (They are:) Your venerable self, Bhisma and Karna, and Krpa who is ever victorious in battle; Asvatthama, Vikarna, Saumadatti and Jayadratha.
1:8.word_meanings: भवान् — yourself; भीष्मः — Bhishma; च — and; कर्णः — Karna; च — and; कृपः — Kripa; च — and; समितिञ्जयः — victorious in war; अश्वत्थामा — Asvatthama; the — son of Dronacharya; विकर्णः — Vikarna; च — and; सौमदत्तिः — the son of Somadatta; तथा — thus; एव — even; च — and.No

sa: अन्ये च बहवः शूरा मदर्थे त्यक्तजीविताः
iast: anye ca bahavaḥ śūrā madarthe tyaktajīvitāḥ

1:9.pada_sa: अन्ये, च, बहवः, शूराः, मदर्थे, त्यक्तजीविताः,नानाशस्त्रप्रहरणाः, सर्वे, युद्धविशारदाः ॥ ९ ॥
1:9.anvaya_sa: अन्ये, च, बहवः, शूराः, नानाशस्त्रप्रहरणाः, मदर्थे, त्यक्तजीविताः, सर्वे, युद्धविशारदाः ॥ ९ ॥
1:9.pada_iast: anye, ca, bahavaḥ, śūrāḥ, madarthe, tyaktajīvitāḥ,nānāśastrapraharaṇāḥ, sarve, yuddhaviśāradāḥ || 9 ||
1:9.anvaya_iast: anye, ca, bahavaḥ, śūrāḥ, nānāśastrapraharaṇāḥ, madarthe, tyaktajīvitāḥ, sarve, yuddhaviśāradāḥ || 9 ||
1:9.translation: There are many heroes who have dedicated their lives for my sake, who possess various kinds of weapons and missiles, (and) all of whom are skilled in battle.
1:9.word_meanings: अन्ये — others; च — and; बहवः — many; शूराः — heroes; मदर्थे — for my sake; त्यक्तजीविताः — who are ready to give up their lives; नानाशस्त्रप्रहरणाः — armed with various weapons and missiles; सर्वे — all; युद्धविशारदाः — wellskilled in battle.No

1:10.pada_sa: अपर्याप्तं, तत्, अस्माकं, बलं, भीष्माभिरक्षितं, पर्याप्तं, तु, इदम्, एतेषां, बलं, भीमाभिरक्षितम् ॥ १० ॥
1:10.anvaya_sa: भीष्माभिरक्षितम्, अस्माकम्, तत्, बलम्, अपर्याप्तम्, तु, भीमाभिरक्षितम्, एतेषाम्, इदं, बलम्, पर्याप्तम् ॥ १० ॥
1:10.pada_iast: aparyāptaṃ, tat, asmākaṃ, balaṃ, bhīṣmābhirakṣitaṃ, paryāptaṃ, tu, idam, eteṣāṃ, balaṃ, bhīmābhirakṣitam || 10 ||
1:10.anvaya_iast: bhīṣmābhirakṣitam, asmākam, tat, balam, aparyāptam, tu, bhīmābhirakṣitam, eteṣām, idaṃ, balam, paryāptam || 10 ||
1:10.translation: Therefore, our army under the complete protection of Bhisma and others is unlimited. But this army of these (enemies), under the protection of Bhima and others is limited.
1:10.explanation: The verse is differently interpreted by different commentators. Sridhara Swami takes the word aparyaptam to mean insufficient. Ananda Giri takes it to mean unlimited.
1:10.word_meanings: अपर्याप्तम् — insufficient; तत् — that; अस्माकम् — ours; बलम् — army; भीष्माभिरक्षितम् — marshalled by Bhishma; पर्याप्तम् — sufficient; तु — while; इदम् — this; एतेषाम् — their; बलम् — army; भीमाभिरक्षितम् — marshalled by Bhima.

1:11.pada_sa: अयनेषु, च, सर्वेषु, यथाभागम्, अवस्थिताः, भीष्मम्, एव, अभिरक्षन्तु, भवन्तः, सर्वे, एव, हि ॥ ११ ॥
1:11.anvaya_sa: च, सर्वेषु, अयनेषु, यथाभागम्, अवस्थिताः, भवन्तः, सर्वे, एव, हि, भीष्मम्, एव, अभिरक्षन्तु ॥ ११ ॥
1:11.pada_iast: ayaneṣu, ca, sarveṣu, yathābhāgam, avasthitāḥ, bhīṣmam, eva, abhirakṣantu, bhavantaḥ, sarve, eva, hi || 11 ||
1:11.anvaya_iast: ca, sarveṣu, ayaneṣu, yathābhāgam, avasthitāḥ, bhavantaḥ, sarve, eva, hi, bhīṣmam, eva, abhirakṣantu || 11 ||
1:11.translation: However, venerable sirs, all of you without exception, while occupying all the positions in the different directions as alloted (to you respectively), please fully protect Bhisma in particular.

1:12.anvaya_iast: kuruvṛddhaḥ, pratāpavān, pitāmahaḥ, tasya, harṣaṃ, sañjanayan, uccaiḥ, siṃhanādaṃ, vinadya, śaṅkhaṃ, dadhmau || 12 ||
1:12.translation: The valiant grandfather, the eldest of the Kurus, loudly sounding a lion-roar, blew the conch to raise his (Duryodhana's) spirits.

1:28.translation: O Krishna, seeing my own kinsmen arrayed here, eager to fight, my limbs fail me and my mouth is parching.
1:28.explanation: Arjuna's breakdown begins physically — his body rebels before his mind does. "Sīdanti mama gātrāṇi" (my limbs are failing) and "mukhaṁ ca pariśuṣyati" (my mouth is drying up) are classic symptoms of extreme anxiety. The Gita acknowledges that spiritual crises manifest in the body first.

1:35.pada_sa: एतान्, न, हन्तुम्, इच्छामि, घ्नतः, अपि, मधुसूदन, अपि, त्रैलोक्यराज्यस्य, हेतोः, किं, नु, महीकृते ॥ ३५ ॥
1:35.anvaya_sa: यद्यपि, लोभोपहतचेतसः, एते, कुलक्षयकृतं, दोषं, च, मित्रद्रोहे, पातकं, न, पश्यन्ति ॥ ३८ ॥
1:35.pada_iast: etān, na, hantum, icchāmi, ghnataḥ, api, madhusūdana, api, trailokyarājyasya, hetoḥ, kiṃ, nu, mahīkṛte || 35 ||
1:35.anvaya_iast: yadyapi, lobhopahatacetasaḥ, ete, kulakṣayakṛtaṃ, doṣaṃ, ca, mitradrohe, pātakaṃ, na, paśyanti || 38 ||
1:35.translation: O Madhusudana, even if I am killed, I do not want to kill these even for the sake of a kingdom extending over the three worlds; what to speak of doing so for the earth!
1:35.word_meanings: एतान् — these; न — not; हन्तुम् — to kill; इच्छामि (I) — wish; घ्नतःअपि — even if they kill me; मधुसूदन — O Madhusudana (the slayer of Madhu; a — demon); अपि — even; त्रैलोक्यराज्यस्य — dominion over the three worlds; हेतोः — for the sake of; किम् — how; नु — then; महीकृते — for the sake of the earth.No

iast: nihatya dhārtarāṣhṭrān naḥ kā prītiḥ syāj janārdana

overrides.पापमेवाश्रयेदस्मान्हत्वैतानाततायिनः: पापम् एव आश्रयेत् अस्मान् हत्वा एतान् आततायिनः

1:36.pada_sa: निहत्य, धार्तराष्ट्रान्, नः, का, प्रीतिः, स्यात्, जनार्दन, पापम्, एव, आश्रयेत्, अस्मान्, हत्वा, एतान्, आततायिनः ॥ ३६ ॥
1:36.anvaya_sa: जनार्दन, कुलक्षयकृतं, दोषं, प्रपश्यद्भिः, अस्माभिः, अस्मात्, पापात्, निवर्तितुं, कथं, न, ज्ञेयम् ॥ ३९ ॥
1:36.pada_iast: nihatya, dhārtarāṣṭrān, naḥ, kā, prītiḥ, syāt, janārdana, pāpam, eva, āśrayet, asmān, hatvā, etān, ātatāyinaḥ || 36 ||
1:36.anvaya_iast: janārdana, kulakṣayakṛtaṃ, doṣaṃ, prapaśyadbhiḥ, asmābhiḥ, asmāt, pāpāt, nivartituṃ, kathaṃ, na, jñeyam || 39 ||
1:36.translation: O Janardana, what happiness shall we derive by killing the sons of Dhrtarastra? Sin alone will accrue to us by killing these felons.
1:36.explanation: Janardana means one who is worshipped by all for prosperity and salvation -- Krishna.He who sets fire to the house of another? who gives poision? who runs with sword to kill? who has plundered wealth and lands? and who has taken hold of the wife of somody else is an atatayi. Duryodhana had done all these evil actions.
1:36.word_meanings: निहत्य — having slain; धार्तराष्ट्रान् — sons of Dhritarashtra; नः — to us; का — what; प्रीतिः — pleasure; स्यात् — may be; जनार्दन — O Janardana; पापम् — sin; एव — only; आश्रयेत् — would take hold; अस्मान् — to us; हत्वा — having killed; एतान् — these; आततायिनः — felons.

sa: स्वजनं हि कथं हत्वा सुखिनः स्याम माधव
iast: tasmān nārhā vayaṁ hantuṁ dhārtarāṣhṭrān sa-bāndhavān
sva-janaṁ hi kathaṁ hatvā sukhinaḥ syāma mādhava

1:37.pada_sa: तस्मात्, न, अर्हाः, वयं, हन्तुं, धार्तराष्ट्रान्, स्वबान्धवान्, स्वजनं, हि, कथं, हत्वा, सुखिनः, स्याम, माधव ॥ ३७ ॥
1:37.anvaya_sa: कुलक्षये, सनातनाः, कुलधर्माः, प्रणश्यन्ति, धर्मे, नष्टे, कृत्स्नं, कुलम्, अधर्मः, उत, अभिभवति ॥ ४० ॥
1:37.pada_iast: tasmāt, na, arhāḥ, vayaṃ, hantuṃ, dhārtarāṣṭrān, svabāndhavān, svajanaṃ, hi, kathaṃ, hatvā, sukhinaḥ, syāma, mādhava || 37 ||
1:37.anvaya_iast: kulakṣaye, sanātanāḥ, kuladharmāḥ, praṇaśyanti, dharme, naṣṭe, kṛtsnaṃ, kulam, adharmaḥ, uta, abhibhavati || 40 ||
1:37.translation: Therefore, it is not proper for us to kill the sons of Dhrtarastra who are our own relatives. For, O Madhava, how can we be happy by killing our kinsmen?
1:37.word_meanings: तस्मात् — therefore; न (are) — not; अर्हाः — justified; वयम् — we; हन्तुम् — to kill; धार्तराष्ट्रान् — the sons of Dhritarashtra; स्वबान्धवान् — our relatives; स्वजनम् — kinsmen; हि — indeed; कथम् — how; हत्वा — having killed; सुखिनः — happy; स्याम — may (we) be; माधव — O Madhava.No

iast: yady apy ete na paśyanti lobhopahata-cetasaḥ

1:38.pada_sa: यद्यपि, एते, न, पश्यन्ति, लोभोपहतचेतसः, कुलक्षयकृतं, दोषं, मित्रद्रोहे, च, पातकम् ॥ ३८ ॥
1:38.anvaya_sa: कृष्ण, अधर्माभिभवात्, कुलस्त्रियः, प्रदुष्यन्ति, वार्ष्णेय, स्त्रीषु, दुष्टासु, वर्णसङ्करः, जायते ॥ ४१ ॥
1:38.pada_iast: yadyapi, ete, na, paśyanti, lobhopahatacetasaḥ, kulakṣayakṛtaṃ, doṣaṃ, mitradrohe, ca, pātakam || 38 ||
1:38.anvaya_iast: kṛṣṇa, adharmābhibhavāt, kulastriyaḥ, praduṣyanti, vārṣṇeya, strīṣu, duṣṭāsu, varṇasaṅkaraḥ, jāyate || 41 ||
1:38.translation: 1.39  O Janardana, although these people, whose hearts have become perverted by greed, do not see the evil arising from destroying the family and sin in hostility towards, friends, yet how can we who clearly see the evil arising from destroying the family remain unaware of (the need of) abstaining from this sin?
1:38.word_meanings: यद्यपि — though; एते — these; न — not; पश्यन्ति — see; लोभोपहतचेतसः — with intelligence overpowered by greed; कुलक्षयकृतम् — in the destruction of families; दोषम् — evil; मित्रद्रोहे — in hostility to friends; च — and; पातकम् — sin.No

iast: kathaṁ na jñeyam asmābhiḥ pāpād asmān nivartitum

1:39.pada_sa: कथं, न, ज्ञेयम्, अस्माभिः, पापात्, अस्मान्, निवर्तितुं, कुलक्षयकृतं, दोषं, प्रपश्यद्भिः, जनार्दन ॥ ३९ ॥
1:39.anvaya_sa: सङ्करः, कुलघ्नानां, च, कुलस्य, नरकाय, एव, लुप्तपिण्डोदकक्रियाः, एषां, पितरः, हि, पतन्ति ॥ ४२ ॥
1:39.pada_iast: kathaṃ, na, jñeyam, asmābhiḥ, pāpāt, asmān, nivartituṃ, kulakṣayakṛtaṃ, doṣaṃ, prapaśyadbhiḥ, janārdana || 39 ||
1:39.anvaya_iast: saṅkaraḥ, kulaghnānāṃ, ca, kulasya, narakāya, eva, luptapiṇḍodakakriyāḥ, eṣāṃ, pitaraḥ, hi, patanti || 42 ||
1:39.translation: 1.39 O Janardana, although these people, whose hearts have become perverted by greed, do not see the evil arising from destroying the family and sin in hostility towards, friends, yet how can we who clearly see the evil arising from destroying the family remain unaware of (the need of) abstaining from this sin?
1:39.explanation: Ignorance of law is no excuse but wanton sinful conduct is a grave crime? unworthy of us? who are wiser.
1:39.word_meanings: कथम् — why; न — not; ज्ञेयम् — should be learnt; अस्माभिः — by us; पापात् — from sin; अस्मात् — this; निवर्तितुम् — to turn away; कुलक्षयकृतम् — in the destruction of families; दोषम् — evil; प्रपश्यद्भिः — clearly seeing; जनार्दन — O Janardana.

iast: dharme naṣhṭe kulaṁ kṛitsnam adharmo ’bhibhavaty uta

1:40.pada_sa: कुलक्षये, प्रणश्यन्ति, कुलधर्माः, सनातनाः, धर्मे, नष्टे, कुलं, कृत्स्नम्, अधर्मः, अभिभवति, उत ॥ ४० ॥
1:40.anvaya_sa: एतैः, वर्णसङ्करकारकैः, दोषैः, कुलघ्नानां, शाश्वताः, कुलधर्माः, च, जातिधर्माः, उत्साद्यन्ते ॥ ४३ ॥
1:40.pada_iast: kulakṣaye, praṇaśyanti, kuladharmāḥ, sanātanāḥ, dharme, naṣṭe, kulaṃ, kṛtsnam, adharmaḥ, abhibhavati, uta || 40 ||
1:40.anvaya_iast: etaiḥ, varṇasaṅkarakārakaiḥ, doṣaiḥ, kulaghnānāṃ, śāśvatāḥ, kuladharmāḥ, ca, jātidharmāḥ, utsādyante || 43 ||
1:40.translation: From the ruin of the family are totally destroyed the traditional rites and duties of the family. When rites and duties are destroyed, vice overpowers the entire family also.
1:40.explanation: Dharma -- the duties and ceremonies practised by the family in accordance with the injunctions of the scriptures.
1:40.word_meanings: कुलक्षये — in the destruction of a family; प्रणश्यन्ति — perish; कुलधर्माः — family religious rites; सनातनाः — immemorial; धर्मे — spirituality; नष्टे — being destroyed; कुलम् कृत्स्नम् — the whole family; अधर्मः — impiety; अभिभवति — overcomes; उत — indeed.

1:41.pada_sa: अधर्माभिभवात्, कृष्ण, प्रदुष्यन्ति, कुलस्त्रियः, स्त्रीषु, दुष्टासु, वार्ष्णेय, जायते, वर्णसङ्करः ॥ ४१ ॥
1:41.anvaya_sa: जनार्दन, उत्सन्नकुलधर्माणां, मनुष्याणाम्, अनियतं, नरके, वासः, भवति, इति, अनुशुश्रुम ॥ ४४ ॥
1:41.pada_iast: adharmābhibhavāt, kṛṣṇa, praduṣyanti, kulastriyaḥ, strīṣu, duṣṭāsu, vārṣṇeya, jāyate, varṇasaṅkaraḥ || 41 ||
1:41.anvaya_iast: janārdana, utsannakuladharmāṇāṃ, manuṣyāṇām, aniyataṃ, narake, vāsaḥ, bhavati, iti, anuśuśruma || 44 ||
1:41.translation: O Krsna, when vice predominates, the women of the family become corrupt. O descendent of the Vrsnis, when women become corrupted, it results in the intermingling of castes.
1:41.word_meanings: अधर्माभिभवात् — from the prevalence of impiety; कृष्ण — O Krishna; प्रदुष्यन्ति — become corrupt; कुलस्त्रियः — the women of the family; स्त्रीषु — in women; दुष्टासु (being) — corrupt; वार्ष्णेय — O Varshneya; जायते — arises; वर्णसङ्करः — casteadmixture.No

1:42.pada_sa: सङ्करः, नरकाय, एव, कुलघ्नानां, कुलस्य, च, पतन्ति, पितरः, हि, एषां, लुप्तपिण्डोदकक्रियाः ॥ ४२ ॥
1:42.anvaya_sa: अहो, बत, वयं, महत्पापं, कर्तुं, व्यवस्थिताः, यत्, राज्यसुखलोभेन, स्वजनं, हन्तुं, उद्यताः ॥ ४५ ॥
1:42.pada_iast: saṅkaraḥ, narakāya, eva, kulaghnānāṃ, kulasya, ca, patanti, pitaraḥ, hi, eṣāṃ, luptapiṇḍodakakriyāḥ || 42 ||
1:42.anvaya_iast: aho, bata, vayaṃ, mahatpāpaṃ, kartuṃ, vyavasthitāḥ, yat, rājyasukhalobhena, svajanaṃ, hantuṃ, udyatāḥ || 45 ||
1:42.translation: And the intermingling in the family leads the ruiners of the family verily into hell. The forefathers of these fall down (into hell) because of being deprived of the offerings of rice-balls and water.
1:42.word_meanings: सङ्करः — confusion of castes; नरकाय — for the hell; एव — also; कुलघ्नानाम् — of the slayers of the family; कुलस्य — of the family; च — and; पतन्ति — fall; पितरः — the forefathers; हि — verily; एषां — their; लुप्तपिण्डोदकक्रियाः — deprived of the offerings of ricall and water.No

1:43.pada_sa: दोषैः, एतैः, कुलघ्नानां, वर्णसङ्करकारकैः, उत्साद्यन्ते, जातिधर्माः, कुलधर्माः, च,  शाश्वताः ॥ ४३ ॥
1:43.anvaya_sa: यदि, माम्, अशस्त्रम्, अप्रतीकारं, शस्त्रपाणयः, धार्तराष्ट्राः, रणे, हन्युः, तत्, मे, क्षेमतरं, भवेत् ॥ ४६ ॥
1:43.pada_iast: doṣaiḥ, etaiḥ, kulaghnānāṃ, varṇasaṅkarakārakaiḥ, utsādyante, jātidharmāḥ, kuladharmāḥ, ca,  śāśvatāḥ || 43 ||
1:43.anvaya_iast: yadi, mām, aśastram, apratīkāraṃ, śastrapāṇayaḥ, dhārtarāṣṭrāḥ, raṇe, hanyuḥ, tat, me, kṣemataraṃ, bhavet || 46 ||
1:43.translation: Due to these misdeeds of the ruiners of the family, which cause intermingling of castes, the traditional rites and duties of the castes and families become destroyed.
1:43.word_meanings: दोषैः — by evil deeds; एतैः (by) — these; कुलघ्नानाम् — of the family destroyers; वर्णसङ्करकारकैः — causing intermingling of castes; उत्साद्यन्ते — are destroyed; जातिधर्माः — religious rites of the caste; कुलधर्माः — family religious rites; च — and; शाश्वताः — eternal.No

1:44.pada_sa: उत्सन्नकुलधर्माणां, मनुष्याणां, जनार्दन, नरके, अनियतं, वासः, भवति, इति, अनुशुश्रुम ॥ ४४ ॥
1:44.anvaya_sa: संख्ये, शोकसंविग्नमानसः, अर्जुनः, एवम्, उक्त्वा, सशरं, चापं, विसृज्य, रथोपस्थे, उपाविशत् ॥ ४७ ॥
1:44.pada_iast: utsannakuladharmāṇāṃ, manuṣyāṇāṃ, janārdana, narake, aniyataṃ, vāsaḥ, bhavati, iti, anuśuśruma || 44 ||
1:44.anvaya_iast: saṃkhye, śokasaṃvignamānasaḥ, arjunaḥ, evam, uktvā, saśaraṃ, cāpaṃ, visṛjya, rathopasthe, upāviśat || 47 ||
1:44.translation: O Janardana, we have heard that living in hell becomes inevitable for those persons whose family duties get destroyed.
1:44.word_meanings: उत्सन्नकुलधर्माणाम् — whose family religious practices are destroyed; मनुष्याणाम् — of the men; जनार्दन — O Janardana; नरके — in hell; अनियतं — for unknown period; वासः — dwelling; भवति — is; इति — thus; अनुशुश्रुम — we have heard.No

sa: अहो बत महत्पापं कर्तुं व्यवसिता वयम्
iast: aho bata mahat pāpaṁ kartuṁ vyavasitā vayam

1:45.pada_sa: अहो, बत, महत्, पापं, कर्तुं, व्यवसिताः, वयं, यत्, राज्यसुखलोभेन, हन्तुं, स्वजनं, उद्यताः ॥ ४५ ॥
1:45.pada_iast: aho, bata, mahat, pāpaṃ, kartuṃ, vyavasitāḥ, vayaṃ, yat, rājyasukhalobhena, hantuṃ, svajanaṃ, udyatāḥ || 45 ||
1:45.translation: What a pity that we have resolved to commit a great sin by being eager to kill our own kith and kin, out of greed for the pleasures of a kingdom!
1:45.word_meanings: अहो बत — alas; महत् — great; पापम् — sin; कर्तुम् — to do; व्यवसिताः — prepared; वयम् — we; यत् — that; राज्यसुखलोभेन — by the greed of pleasure of kingdom; हन्तुम् — to kill; स्वजनम् — kinsmen; उद्यताः — prepared.No

iast: dhārtarāṣhṭrā raṇe hanyus tan me kṣhemataraṁ bhavet

1:46.pada_sa: यदि, माम्, अप्रतीकारं, अशस्त्रं, शस्त्रपाणयः, धार्तराष्ट्राः, रणे, हन्युः, तत्, मे, क्षेमतरं, भवेत् ॥ ४६ ॥
1:46.anvaya_sa: तथा, कृपया, आविष्टम्, अश्रुपूर्णाकुलेक्षणं, विषीदन्तं, तं, मधुसूदनः, इदं, वाक्यम्, उवाच ॥ १ ॥
1:46.pada_iast: yadi, mām, apratīkāraṃ, aśastraṃ, śastrapāṇayaḥ, dhārtarāṣṭrāḥ, raṇe, hanyuḥ, tat, me, kṣemataraṃ, bhavet || 46 ||
1:46.anvaya_iast: tathā, kṛpayā, āviṣṭam, aśrupūrṇākulekṣaṇaṃ, viṣīdantaṃ, taṃ, madhusūdanaḥ, idaṃ, vākyam, uvāca || 1 ||
1:46.translation: If, in this battle, the sons of Dhrtarastra armed with weapons kill me who am non-resistant and unarmed, that will be more beneficial to me.
1:46.word_meanings: यदि — if; माम् — me; अप्रतीकारम् — unresisting; अशस्त्रम् — unarmed; शस्त्रपाणयः — with weapons in hand; धार्तराष्ट्राः — the sons of Dhritarashtra; रणे — in the battle हन्युः should slay; तत् — that; मे — of me; क्षेमतरम् — better; भवेत् — would be.No

1:47.pada_sa: एवम्, उक्त्वा, अर्जुनः, सङ्‍ख्ये, रथोपस्थे, उपाविशत्, विसॄज्य, सशरं, चापं, शोकसंविग्नमानसः ॥ ४७ ॥
1:47.anvaya_sa: अर्जुन, त्वा, विषमे, इदं, अनार्यजुष्टम्, अस्वर्ग्यम्, अकीर्तिकरम्, कश्मलं, कुतः, समुपस्थितं ॥ २ ॥
1:47.pada_iast: evam, uktvā, arjunaḥ, saṅ‍khye, rathopasthe, upāviśat, visṝjya, saśaraṃ, cāpaṃ, śokasaṃvignamānasaḥ || 47 ||
1:47.anvaya_iast: arjuna, tvā, viṣame, idaṃ, anāryajuṣṭam, asvargyam, akīrtikaram, kaśmalaṃ, kutaḥ, samupasthitaṃ || 2 ||
1:47.translation: Sanjaya said: Having spoken thus on the battlefield, Arjuna cast aside his bow and arrows, and sat down on the chariot, his mind overwhelmed with grief.
1:47.explanation: This is the climactic verse of Chapter 1. Arjuna — the greatest warrior of his time — collapses. He doesn't just put down his weapons; he "casts them aside" (visṛjya), an act of complete renunciation. The word "śhoka-saṁvigna-mānasaḥ" (mind overwhelmed with grief) describes a total psychological breakdown. This sets up the entire teaching of the Gita.
1:47.word_meanings: sañjayaḥ — Sanjaya; uvācha — said; evam — thus; uktvā — having said; arjunaḥ — Arjuna; saṅkhye — on the battlefield; ratha-upasthe — on the chariot; upāviśhat — sat down; visṛjya — casting aside; sa-śharam — with arrows; chāpam — bow; śhoka — grief; saṁvigna — overwhelmed; mānasaḥ — mind

2:1.pada_sa: तं, तथा, कृपया, आविष्टम्, अश्रुपूर्णाकुलेक्षणं, विषीदन्तम्, इदं, वाक्यम्, उवाच, मधुसूदनः ॥ १ ॥
2:1.anvaya_sa: पार्थ, क्लैब्यं, मा स्म गमः, एतत्, त्वयि, न उपपद्यते, परन्तप, क्षुद्रं, हृदयदौर्बल्यं, त्यक्त्वा, उत्तिष्ठ  ॥ ३ ॥
2:1.pada_iast: taṃ, tathā, kṛpayā, āviṣṭam, aśrupūrṇākulekṣaṇaṃ, viṣīdantam, idaṃ, vākyam, uvāca, madhusūdanaḥ || 1 ||
2:1.anvaya_iast: pārtha, klaibyaṃ, mā sma gamaḥ, etat, tvayi, na upapadyate, parantapa, kṣudraṃ, hṛdayadaurbalyaṃ, tyaktvā, uttiṣṭha  || 3 ||
2:1.translation: Sanjaya said  To him who had been thus filled with pity, whose eyes were filled with tears and showed distress, and who was sorrowing, Madhusudana uttered these words:
2:1.explanation: . Sanjaya said  To him (Arjuna) who was thus possessed by compassion, whose eyes were confused and filled with tears and who was sinking in despondency, Madhusudana told this [following] sentence.
2:1.word_meanings: तम् — to him; तथा — thus; कृपया — with pity; आविष्टम् — overcome; अश्रुपूर्णाकुलेक्षणम् — with eyes filled with tears and agitated; विषीदन्तम् — despondent; इदम् — this; वाक्यम् — speech; उवाच — spoke; मघुसूदनः — Madhusudana.No commentary.

2:2.pada_sa: कुतः, त्वा, कष्मलम्, इदं, विषमे, समुपस्थितम्, अनार्यजुष्टम्, अस्वर्ग्यम्, अकीर्तिकरम्, अर्जुन ॥ २ ॥
2:2.anvaya_sa: मधुसूदन, अहं, संख्ये, भीष्मं, च, द्रोणं, कथं, इषुभिः, प्रतियोत्स्यामि, (यतः) अरिसूदन, (तौ) पूजार्हौ ॥ ४ ॥
2:2.pada_iast: kutaḥ, tvā, kaṣmalam, idaṃ, viṣame, samupasthitam, anāryajuṣṭam, asvargyam, akīrtikaram, arjuna || 2 ||
2:2.anvaya_iast: madhusūdana, ahaṃ, saṃkhye, bhīṣmaṃ, ca, droṇaṃ, kathaṃ, iṣubhiḥ, pratiyotsyāmi, (yataḥ) arisūdana, (tau) pūjārhau || 4 ||
2:2.translation: The Blessed Lord said  O Arjuna, in this perilous place, whence has come to you this impurity entertained by unenlightened persons, which does not lead to heaven and which brings infamy?
2:2.explanation: . The Bhagavat said  O Arjuna !   At a critical moment,  whence did this sinful act come to you which is practised by men of ignoble (low) birth and which is leading to the hell and is inglorious ?
2:2.word_meanings: कुतः — whence; त्वा — upon thee; कश्मलम् — dejection; इदम् — this; विषमे — in perilous strait; समुपस्थितम् — comes; अनार्यजुष्टम् — unworthy (unaryanlike); अस्वर्ग्यम् — heavenexcluding; अकीर्तिकरम् — disgraceful; अर्जुन — O Arjuna.No commentary.

iast: klaibyaṁ mā sma gamaḥ pārtha naitat tvayyupapadyate

2:3.anvaya_sa: महानुभावान्, गुरून्, अहत्वा, इह, लोके, भैक्ष्यम्, अपि, भोक्तुं, श्रेयः, हि, गुरून्, हत्वा, इह, रुधिरप्रदिग्धान्, अर्थकामान्, भोगान्, एव, तु, भुञ्जीय ॥ ५ ॥
2:3.pada_iast: klaibyaṃ, mā, sma, gamaḥ, pārtha, na, etat, tvayi, upapadyate, kṣudraṃ, hṛdayadaurbalyaṃ, tyaktvā, uttiṣṭha, parantapa || 3 ||
2:3.anvaya_iast: mahānubhāvān, gurūn, ahatvā, iha, loke, bhaikṣyam, api, bhoktuṃ, śreyaḥ, hi, gurūn, hatvā, iha, rudhirapradigdhān, arthakāmān, bhogān, eva, tu, bhuñjīya || 5 ||
2:3.translation: O Partha, yield not to unmanliness. This does not befit you. O scorcher of foes, arise, giving up the petty weakness of the heart.
2:3.explanation: . Stoop not to unmanliness,  O son of Kunti !   It does not befit you.  Shirking off the petty weakness of heart,  arise,  O scorcher of the foes !
2:3.word_meanings: क्लैब्यम् — impotence; मा स्म गमः — do not get; पार्थ — O Partha; न — not; एतत् — this; त्वयि — in thee; उपपद्यते — is fitting; क्षुद्रम् — mean; हृदयदौर्बल्यम् — weakness of the heart; त्यक्त्वा — having abandoned; उत्तिष्ठ — stand up; परन्तप — O scorcher of the foes.No commentary.

sa: कथं भीष्ममहं सङ्ख्ये द्रोणं च मधुसूदन
iast: kathaṁ bhīṣhmam ahaṁ sankhye droṇaṁ ca madhusūdana

2:4.anvaya_sa: एतत्, च, न, विद्मः, नः, कतरत्, गरीयः, यद्वा, जयेम, यदि वा, नः, जयेयुः, यान्, हत्वा, न जिजीविषामः, ते, एव, धार्तराष्ट्राः, प्रमुखे, अवस्थिताः ॥ ६ ॥
2:4.pada_iast: kathaṃ, bhīṣmam, ahaṃ, saṅkhye, droṇaṃ, ca, madhudūdana, iṣubhiḥ, pratiyotsyāmi, pūjārhau, arisūdana || 4 ||
2:4.anvaya_iast: etat, ca, na, vidmaḥ, naḥ, katarat, garīyaḥ, yadvā, jayema, yadi vā, naḥ, jayeyuḥ, yān, hatvā, na jijīviṣāmaḥ, te, eva, dhārtarāṣṭrāḥ, pramukhe, avasthitāḥ || 6 ||
2:4.translation: Arjuna said  O Madhusudana, O destroyer of enemies, how can I fight with arrows in battle against Bhisma and Drona who are worthy of adoration?
2:4.explanation: . Arjuna said  How shall I with arrows fight in battle against Bhisma and Drona,  both being worthy of reverence ?   O slayer of  Mandhu,  O slayer of foes !

2:5.pada_sa: गुरुन्, अहत्वा, हि, महानुभावान्, श्रेयः, भोक्तुं, भैक्षम्, अपि, इह, लोके, हत्वा, अर्थकामान्, तु, गुरून्, इह, एव, भुञ्जीय, भोगान्, रुधिरप्रदिग्धान् ॥ ५ ॥
2:5.anvaya_sa: कार्पण्यदोषोपहतस्वभावः, धर्मासंमूढचेताः, त्वां, पृच्छामि, यत्, निश्चितं, श्रेयः, स्यात्, तत्, मे, ब्रूहि, अहं, ते, शिष्यः, त्वां, प्रपन्नं, मां, शाधि ॥ ७ ॥
2:5.pada_iast: gurun, ahatvā, hi, mahānubhāvān, śreyaḥ, bhoktuṃ, bhaikṣam, api, iha, loke, hatvā, arthakāmān, tu, gurūn, iha, eva, bhuñjīya, bhogān, rudhirapradigdhān || 5 ||
2:5.anvaya_iast: kārpaṇyadoṣopahatasvabhāvaḥ, dharmāsaṃmūḍhacetāḥ, tvāṃ, pṛcchāmi, yat, niścitaṃ, śreyaḥ, syāt, tat, me, brūhi, ahaṃ, te, śiṣyaḥ, tvāṃ, prapannaṃ, māṃ, śādhi || 7 ||
2:5.translation: Rather than killing the noble-minded elders, it is better in this world to live even on alms. But by killing the elders we shall only be enjoying here the pleasures of wealth and desireable things drenched in blood.
2:5.explanation: . It is good indeed even to go about begging in this world without killing the elders of great dignity;  but with greed for wealth,  I would not enjoy,  by killing my elders,  the blood-stained objects of pleasures.
2:5.word_meanings: गुरून् — the Gurus (teachers); अहत्वा — instead of slaying; हि — indeed; महानुभावान् — most noble; श्रेयः — better; भोक्तुम् — to eat; भैक्ष्यम् — alms; अपि — even; इह — here; लोके — in the world; हत्वा — having slain; अर्थकामान् — desirous of wealth; तु — indeed; गुरून् — Gurus; इह — here; एव — also; भुञ्जीय — enjoy; भोगान् — enjoyments; रुधिरप्रदिग्धान् — stained with blood.No commentary.

sa: यद्वा जयेम यदि वा नो जयेयुः
iast: yadvā jayema yadi vā no jayeyuḥ

2:6.anvaya_sa: हि, भूमौ, असपत्नम्, ऋद्धं, राज्यं, च, सुराणां, आधिपत्यं, अवाप्य, अपि, न, प्रपश्यामि, यत्, मम, इन्द्रियाणां, उच्छोषणं, शोकम्, अपनुद्यात् ॥ ८ ॥
2:6.pada_iast: na, ca, etad, vidmaḥ, katarat, naḥ, garīyaḥ, yadvā, jayema, yadi, vā, naḥ, jayeyuḥ, yān, eva, hatvā, na, jijīviṣāmaḥ, te, avasthitāḥ, pramukhe, dhārtarāṣṭrāḥ || 6 ||
2:6.anvaya_iast: hi, bhūmau, asapatnam, ṛddhaṃ, rājyaṃ, ca, surāṇāṃ, ādhipatyaṃ, avāpya, api, na, prapaśyāmi, yat, mama, indriyāṇāṃ, ucchoṣaṇaṃ, śokam, apanudyāt || 8 ||
2:6.translation: We do not know this as well as to which is the better for us, (and) whether we shall win, or whether they shall coner us. Those very sons of Dhrtarastra, by killing whom we do not wish to live, stand in confrontation.
2:6.explanation: . Whether we should coner [in the battle],  or they  should coner us-we do not know this viz.,  'which [of  those two] is better for us'.  [For],  having killed whom, we would not wish to live at all,  the same persons stand before us as Dhrtarastra's men.
2:6.word_meanings: न — not; च — and; एतत् — this; विद्मः (we) — know; कतरत् — which; नः — for us; गरीयः — better; यत् — that; वा — or; जयेम — we should coner; यदि — if; वा — or; नः — us; जयेयुः — they should coner; यान् — whom; एव — even; हत्वा — having slain; न — not; जिजीविषामः — we wish to live; ते — those; अवस्थिताः (are) — standing; प्रमुखे — in face; धार्तराष्ट्राः — sons of Dhritarashtra.No commentary.

iast: yac chhreyaḥ syān niśhchitaṁ brūhi tan me
śhiṣhyas te ’haṁ śhādhi māṁ tvāṁ prapannam

2:7.pada_sa: कार्पण्यदोषोपहतस्वभावः, पृच्छामि, त्वां, धर्मासंमूढचेताः, यत्, श्रेयः, स्यात्, निश्चितं, ब्रूहि, तत्, मे, शिष्यः, ते, अहं, शाधि, मां, त्वां, प्रपन्नम् ॥ ७ ॥
2:7.anvaya_sa: परन्तप, गुडाकेशः, हृषीकेशम्, एवम्, उक्त्वा, गोविन्दं, न योत्स्ये, इति, ह, उक्त्वा, तूष्णीं, बभूव ॥ ९ ॥
2:7.pada_iast: kārpaṇyadoṣopahatasvabhāvaḥ, pṛcchāmi, tvāṃ, dharmāsaṃmūḍhacetāḥ, yat, śreyaḥ, syāt, niścitaṃ, brūhi, tat, me, śiṣyaḥ, te, ahaṃ, śādhi, māṃ, tvāṃ, prapannam || 7 ||
2:7.anvaya_iast: parantapa, guḍākeśaḥ, hṛṣīkeśam, evam, uktvā, govindaṃ, na yotsye, iti, ha, uktvā, tūṣṇīṃ, babhūva || 9 ||
2:7.translation: My nature is weighed down by weakness and confusion about my duty. Tell me decisively what is best for me. I am your disciple, surrendered to you — please instruct me.
2:7.explanation: This is the pivotal verse where Arjuna formally becomes a student. Three things happen: (1) he admits his weakness — "kārpaṇya-doṣhopahata"; (2) he admits confusion — "dharma-sammūḍha"; (3) he surrenders — "śhiṣhyas te'haṁ" (I am your student). This surrender triggers the entire teaching of the Gita.
2:7.word_meanings: kārpaṇya — weakness; doṣha — defect; upahata — afflicted; svabhāvaḥ — nature; pṛichchhāmi — I ask; tvām — you; dharma — duty; sammūḍha — confused; chetāḥ — mind; yat — what; śhreyaḥ — best; syāt — may be; niśhchitam — decisively; brūhi — tell; tat — that; me — to me; śhiṣhyaḥ — disciple; te — your; aham — I; śhādhi — instruct; mām — me; tvām — unto you; prapannam — surrendered

2:8.pada_sa: न, हि, प्रपश्यामि, मम, अपनुद्यात्, यत्, शोकम्, उच्छोषणम्, इन्द्रियाणाम्, अवाप्य, भूमौ, असपत्नम्, ऋद्धं, राज्यं, सुराणाम्, अपि, च, आधिपत्यम्  ॥ ८ ॥
2:8.anvaya_sa: भारत, हृषीकेशः, उभ्योः, सेनयोः, मध्ये, तं, विषीदन्तं, प्रहसन् इव, इदं, वचः, उवाच ॥ १० ॥
2:8.pada_iast: na, hi, prapaśyāmi, mama, apanudyāt, yat, śokam, ucchoṣaṇam, indriyāṇām, avāpya, bhūmau, asapatnam, ṛddhaṃ, rājyaṃ, surāṇām, api, ca, ādhipatyam  || 8 ||
2:8.anvaya_iast: bhārata, hṛṣīkeśaḥ, ubhyoḥ, senayoḥ, madhye, taṃ, viṣīdantaṃ, prahasan iva, idaṃ, vacaḥ, uvāca || 10 ||
2:8.translation: Because, I do not see that which can, even after aciring on this earth a prosperous kingdom free from enemies and even sovereignty over the gods, remove my sorrow (which is) blasting the senses.
2:8.explanation: . I do not clearly see what would drive out my grief,  the scorcher of my sense-organs,  even after achieving,  a prosperous and unrivalled kingship in this earth and also the overlordship of the gods  [in the heaven].
2:8.word_meanings: न हि — not; प्रपश्यामि — I see; मम — my; अपनुद्यात् — would remove; यत् — that; शोकम् — grief; उच्छोषणम् — drying up; इन्द्रियाणाम् — of my senses; अवाप्य — having obtained; भूमौ — on the earth; असपत्नम् — unrivalled; ऋद्धम् — prosperous; राज्यम् — dominion; सुराणाम् — over the gods; अपि — even; च — and; आधिपत्यम् — lordship.No commentary.

iast: na yotsya iti govindam uktvā tūṣhṇīṁ babhūva ha

2:9.anvaya_sa: त्वम्, अशोच्यान्, अन्वशोचः, च, प्रज्ञावादान्, भाषसे, पण्डिताः, गतासून्, च, अगतासून्, न अनुशोचन्ति ॥ ११ ॥

2:9.translation: Sanjaya said  Having spoken thus to Hrsikesa (Krsna), Gudakesa (Arjuna), the afflictor of foes, verily became silent, telling Govinda, 'I shall not fight.' fight.'
2:9.explanation: . Sanjaya said   O scorcher of foes (O Dhrtarastra) !  Having spoken to Hrsikesa (the master of sense-organs),  Govinda (Krsna)  in this manner,  and having declared  'I will not fight',  Gudakesa (Arjuna),  became silent !
2:9.word_meanings: एवम् — thus; उक्त्वा — having spoken; हृषीकेशम् — to Hrishikesha; गुडाकेशः — Arjuna (the coneror of sleep); परन्तप — destroyer of foes; न योत्स्ये — I will not fight; इति — thus; गोविन्दम् — to Govinda; उक्त्वा — having said; तूष्णीम् — silent; बभूव ह — became.No commentary.

2:10.pada_sa: तम्, उवाच, हृषीकेशः, प्रहसन्, इव, भारत, सेनयोः, उभयोः, मध्ये, विषीदन्तम्, इदं, वचः ॥ १० ॥
2:10.anvaya_sa: न, तु, एव, अहं, जातु, न आसं, त्वं, न (असीः), एमे, जनाधिपाः, न (आसन्), च, न, एव, अतः, परं, वयं, सर्वे, न भविष्यामः ॥ १२ ॥
2:10.pada_iast: tam, uvāca, hṛṣīkeśaḥ, prahasan, iva, bhārata, senayoḥ, ubhayoḥ, madhye, viṣīdantam, idaṃ, vacaḥ || 10 ||
2:10.anvaya_iast: na, tu, eva, ahaṃ, jātu, na āsaṃ, tvaṃ, na (asīḥ), eme, janādhipāḥ, na (āsan), ca, na, eva, ataḥ, paraṃ, vayaṃ, sarve, na bhaviṣyāmaḥ || 12 ||
2:10.translation: O descendant of Bharata, to him who was sorrowing between the two armies, Hrsikesa, mocking as it were, said these words:
2:10.explanation: . O descendant of Bharata  (O Dhrtarastra) !  Hrsikesa,  as if  [he was]  smiling, spoke to him who was sinking in despondency in between two armies.
2:10.word_meanings: तम् — to him; उवाच — spoke; हृषीकेशः — Hrishikesha; प्रहसन् — smiling; इव — as it were; भारत — O Bharata; सेनयोः — of the armies; उभयोः (of) — both; मध्ये — in the middle; विषीदन्तम् — despondent; इदम् — this; वचः — word.No commentary.

2:11.pada_sa: अशोच्यान्, अन्वशोचः, त्वं, प्रज्ञावादान्, च, भाषसे, गतासून्, अगतासून्, च, न, अनुशोचन्ति, पण्डिताः ॥ ११ ॥
2:11.anvaya_sa: यथा, देहिनः, अस्मिन्, देहे, कौमारं, यौवनंं, जरा, तथा, देहान्तरप्राप्तिः, तत्र, धीरः, न मुह्यति  ॥ १३ ॥
2:11.pada_iast: aśocyān, anvaśocaḥ, tvaṃ, prajñāvādān, ca, bhāṣase, gatāsūn, agatāsūn, ca, na, anuśocanti, paṇḍitāḥ || 11 ||
2:11.anvaya_iast: yathā, dehinaḥ, asmin, dehe, kaumāraṃ, yauvanaṃṃ, jarā, tathā, dehāntaraprāptiḥ, tatra, dhīraḥ, na muhyati  || 13 ||
2:11.translation: The Supreme Lord said: While speaking learned words, you are mourning for what is not worthy of grief. Those who are wise lament neither for the living nor for the dead.
2:11.explanation: This is Krishna's first teaching verse. He immediately challenges Arjuna: you speak like a philosopher but grieve like the ignorant. The word "paṇḍitāḥ" (the truly wise) is key — real wisdom is not intellectual knowledge but the understanding that the soul is eternal.
2:11.word_meanings: śhrī-bhagavān — the Supreme Lord; uvācha — said; aśhochyān — not worthy of grief; anvaśhochaḥ — you grieve; tvam — you; prajñā-vādān — wise words; cha — and; bhāṣhase — speak; gata-āsūn — the dead; agata-āsūn — the living; cha — and; na — not; anuśhochanti — lament; paṇḍitāḥ — the wise

sa: न त्वेवाहं जातु नासं न त्वं नेमे जनाधिपाः
न चैव न भविष्यामः सर्वे वयमतः परम्
iast: na tvevāhaṁ jātu nāsaṁ na tvaṁ neme janādhipāḥ
na caiva na bhaviṣhyāmaḥ sarve vayamataḥ param

2:12.pada_sa: न, तु, एव, अहं, जातु, न, आसम्, न, त्वं, न, इमे, जनाधिपाः, न, च, एव, न, भविष्यामः, सर्वे, वयम्, अतः, परम्  ॥ १२ ॥
2:12.anvaya_sa: कौन्तेय, शीतोष्णसुखदुःखदाः, मात्रास्पर्शाः, तु, आगमापायिनः, अनित्याः, भारत, तान्, तितिक्षस्व ॥ १४ ॥
2:12.pada_iast: na, tu, eva, ahaṃ, jātu, na, āsam, na, tvaṃ, na, ime, janādhipāḥ, na, ca, eva, na, bhaviṣyāmaḥ, sarve, vayam, ataḥ, param  || 12 ||
2:12.anvaya_iast: kaunteya, śītoṣṇasukhaduḥkhadāḥ, mātrāsparśāḥ, tu, āgamāpāyinaḥ, anityāḥ, bhārata, tān, titikṣasva || 14 ||
2:12.translation: But certainly (it is) not (a fact) that I did not exist at any time; nor you, nor these rulers of men. And surely it is not that we all shall cease to exist after this.
2:12.explanation: -- Lord Krishna speaks here of the immortality of the Soul or the imperishable nature of the Self (Atman). The Soul exists in the three periods of time (past? present and future). Man continues to exist even after the death of the physical body. There is life beyond.
2:12.word_meanings: न — not; तु — indeed; एव — also; अहम् — I; जातु — at any time; न — not; आसम् — was; न — not; त्वम् — thou; न — not; इमे — these; जनाधिपाः — rulers of men; न — not; च — and; एव — also; न — not; भविष्यामः — shall be; सर्वे — all; वयम् — we; अतः — from this time; परम् — after.

iast: dehino ’smin yathā dehe kaumāraṁ yauvanaṁ jarā
tathā dehāntara-prāptir dhīras tatra na muhyati

2:13.pada_sa: देहिनः, अस्मिन्, यथा, देहे, कौमारं, यौवनं, जरा, तथा, देहान्तरप्राप्तिः, धीरः, तत्र, न, मुह्यति ॥ १३ ॥
2:13.anvaya_sa: हि, पुरुषर्षभ, समदुःखसुखं, यं, धीरं, पुरुषं, एते, न, व्यथयन्ति, सः, अमृतत्वाय, कल्पते ॥ १५ ॥
2:13.pada_iast: dehinaḥ, asmin, yathā, dehe, kaumāraṃ, yauvanaṃ, jarā, tathā, dehāntaraprāptiḥ, dhīraḥ, tatra, na, muhyati || 13 ||
2:13.anvaya_iast: hi, puruṣarṣabha, samaduḥkhasukhaṃ, yaṃ, dhīraṃ, puruṣaṃ, ete, na, vyathayanti, saḥ, amṛtatvāya, kalpate || 15 ||
2:13.translation: Just as the embodied soul continuously passes from childhood to youth to old age, similarly at death the soul passes into another body. The wise are not deluded by this.
2:13.explanation: Krishna uses a simple analogy everyone can understand: you've already "died" many times — the child you were is gone, the teenager is gone. Each stage felt like you, yet the body changed completely. Death is just one more such transition. The word "dhīraḥ" (the steady-minded) suggests this understanding brings calm, not grief.
2:13.word_meanings: dehinaḥ — of the embodied; asmin — in this; yathā — as; dehe — in the body; kaumāram — childhood; yauvanam — youth; jarā — old age; tathā — similarly; deha-antara — another body; prāptiḥ — attainment; dhīraḥ — the wise; tatra — thereupon; na — not; muhyati — is deluded

2:14.pada_sa: मत्रास्पर्शाः, तु, कौन्तेय,  शीतोष्णसुखदुःखदाः, आगमापायिनः, अनित्याः, तान्, तितिक्षस्व, भारत ॥ १४ ॥
2:14.anvaya_sa: असतः, भावः, न विद्यते, तु, सतः, अभावः, न विद्यते, अनयोः, उभयोः, अपि, अन्तः, तत्वदर्शिभिः, दृष्टः ॥ १६ ॥
2:14.pada_iast: matrāsparśāḥ, tu, kaunteya,  śītoṣṇasukhaduḥkhadāḥ, āgamāpāyinaḥ, anityāḥ, tān, titikṣasva, bhārata || 14 ||
2:14.anvaya_iast: asataḥ, bhāvaḥ, na vidyate, tu, sataḥ, abhāvaḥ, na vidyate, anayoḥ, ubhayoḥ, api, antaḥ, tatvadarśibhiḥ, dṛṣṭaḥ || 16 ||
2:14.translation: The contact of the senses with their objects gives rise to cold and heat, pleasure and pain. They come and go, they are temporary — endure them bravely, O Arjuna.
2:14.explanation: Krishna introduces a foundational concept: all sensory experiences are temporary. The key insight is "āgamāpāyinaḥ" (they come and go) and "anityāḥ" (not permanent). This is not suppression — it's understanding that no emotional state lasts forever. The instruction "titikṣhasva" means to develop equanimity.
2:14.word_meanings: mātrā-sparśhāḥ — contact of senses; tu — indeed; kaunteya — O son of Kunti; śhīta — cold; uṣhṇa — heat; sukha — pleasure; duḥkha — pain; dāḥ — giving; āgama — come; apāyinaḥ — go; anityāḥ — temporary; tān — them; titikṣhasva — tolerate; bhārata — O descendant of Bharat

sa: यं हि न व्यथयन्त्येते पुरुषं पुरुषर्षभ
iast: yaṁ hi na vyathayantyete puruṣhaṁ puruṣharṣhabha

2:15.pada_sa: यं, हि, न, व्यथयन्ति, एते, पुरुषं, पुरुषर्षभ,  समदुःखसुखं, धीरं, सः, अमृतत्वाय, कल्पते ॥ १५ ॥
2:15.anvaya_sa: अविनाशि, तु, तद्विद्धि, येन, इदं, सर्वम्, ततं, अस्य, अव्ययस्य, विनाशं, कर्तुं, कश्चित्, न अर्हति ॥ १७ ॥
2:15.pada_iast: yaṃ, hi, na, vyathayanti, ete, puruṣaṃ, puruṣarṣabha,  samaduḥkhasukhaṃ, dhīraṃ, saḥ, amṛtatvāya, kalpate || 15 ||
2:15.anvaya_iast: avināśi, tu, tadviddhi, yena, idaṃ, sarvam, tataṃ, asya, avyayasya, vināśaṃ, kartuṃ, kaścit, na arhati || 17 ||
2:15.translation: O (Arjuna, who are) foremost among men, verily, the person whom these do not torment, the wise man to whom sorrow and happhiness are the same  he is fit for Immortality.
2:15.explanation: -- Dehadhyasa or identification of the Self with the body is the cause of pleasure and pain. The more you are able to identify yourself with the immortal? allpervading Self? the less will you be affected by the pairs of opposites (Dvandvas? pleasure and pain? etc.)Titiksha or the power of endurance develops the willpower. Calm endurance in pleasure and pain? and heat and cold is one of the alifications of an aspirant on the path of Jnana Yoga. It is one of the Shatsampat or sixfold virtues. It is a condition of right knowledge. Titiksha by itself cannot give you Moksha or liberation? but still? when coupled with discrimination and dispassion? it becomes a means to the attainment of Immortality or knowledge of the Self. (Cf.XVII.53)
2:15.word_meanings: यम् — whom; हि — surely; न व्यथयन्ति — afflict not; एते — these; पुरुषम् — man; पुरुषर्षभ — chief among men; समदुःखसुखम् — same in pleasure and pain; धीरम् — firm man; सः — he; अमृतत्वाय — for immortality; कल्पते — is fit.

sa: नासतो विद्यते भावो नाभावो विद्यते सतः
iast: nāsato vidyate bhāvo nābhāvo vidyate sataḥ

2:16.pada_sa: न, असतः, विद्यते, भावः, न, अभावः, विद्यते, सतः, उभयोः, अपि, दृष्टः, अन्तः, तु, अनयोः, तत्त्वदर्शिभिः ॥ १६ ॥
2:16.anvaya_sa: अनाशिनः, अप्रमेयस्य, नित्यस्य, शरीरिणः, इमे, देहाः, अन्तवन्तः, उक्ताः, तस्मात्, भारत, युध्यस्व ॥ १८ ॥
2:16.pada_iast: na, asataḥ, vidyate, bhāvaḥ, na, abhāvaḥ, vidyate, sataḥ, ubhayoḥ, api, dṛṣṭaḥ, antaḥ, tu, anayoḥ, tattvadarśibhiḥ || 16 ||
2:16.anvaya_iast: anāśinaḥ, aprameyasya, nityasya, śarīriṇaḥ, ime, dehāḥ, antavantaḥ, uktāḥ, tasmāt, bhārata, yudhyasva || 18 ||
2:16.translation: Of the unreal there is no being; the real has no nonexistence. But the nature of both these, indeed, has been realized by the seers of Truth.
2:16.explanation: -- The changeless? homogeneous Atman or the Self always exists. It is the only solid Reality. This phenomenal world of names and forms is ever changing. Hence it is unreal. The sage or the Jivanmukta is fully aware that the Self always exists and that this world is like a mirage. Through his Jnanachakshus or the eye of intuition? he directly cognises the Self. This world vanishes for him like the snake in the rope? after it has been seen that only the rope exists. He rejects the names and forms and takes the underlying Essence in all the names and forms? viz.? AstiBhatiPriya or Satchidananda or ExistenceKnowledgeBliss Absolute. Hence he is a Tattvadarshi or a knower of the Truth or the Essence.What is changing must be unreal. What is constant or permanent must be real.
2:16.word_meanings: न — not; असतः — of the unreal; विद्यते — is; भावः — being; न — not; अभावः — nonbeing; विद्यते — is; सतः — of the real; उभयोः — of the two; अपि — also; दृष्टः (has — been) seen; अन्तः — the final truth; तु — indeed; अनयोः — of these; तत्त्वदर्शिभिः — by the knowers of the Truth.

sa: अविनाशि तु तद्विद्धि येन सर्वमिदं ततम्
iast: avināśhi tu tadviddhi yena sarvam idaṁ tatam
vināśham avyayasyāsya na kaśhchit kartum arhati

2:17.pada_sa: अविनाशि, तु, तद्विद्धि, येन, सर्वम्, इदं, ततं, विनाशम्, अव्ययस्य, अस्य, न, कश्चित्, कर्तुम्, अर्हति ॥ १७ ॥
2:17.anvaya_sa: यः, एनं, हन्तारं, वेत्ति, च, यः, एनं, हतं, मन्यते, तौ, उभौ, न, विजानीतः, अयं, न हन्ति, न हन्यते ॥ १९ ॥
2:17.pada_iast: avināśi, tu, tadviddhi, yena, sarvam, idaṃ, tataṃ, vināśam, avyayasya, asya, na, kaścit, kartum, arhati || 17 ||
2:17.anvaya_iast: yaḥ, enaṃ, hantāraṃ, vetti, ca, yaḥ, enaṃ, hataṃ, manyate, tau, ubhau, na, vijānītaḥ, ayaṃ, na hanti, na hanyate || 19 ||
2:17.translation: But know That to be indestructible by which all this is pervaded. None can bring about the destruction of this Immutable.
2:17.explanation: By Swami Sivananda2.17 अविनाशि indestructible? तु indeed? तत् That? विद्धि know (thou)? येन by which? सर्वम् all? इदम् this? ततम् is pervaded? विनाशम् destruction? अव्ययस्य अस्य of this Imperishable? न not? कश्चित् anyone? कर्तुम् to do? अर्हति is able.Commentary -- Brahman or Atman pervades all the objects like ether. Even if the pot is broken? the ether that is within and without the pot cannot be destroyed. Even so? if the bodies and all other objects perish? Brahman or the Self that pervades them cannot perish. It is the living Truth? Sat.Brahman has no parts. There cannot be either increase or diminution in Brahman. People are ruined by loss of wealth. But Brahman does not suffer any loss in that way. It is inexhaustible. Therefore? none can bring about the disappearance or destruction of the Self. It always exists. It is always allfull and selfcontained. It is Existence Absolute. It is immutable.

2:18.pada_sa: अन्तवन्तः, इमे, देहाः, नित्यस्य, उक्ताः, शरीरिणः, अनाशिनः, अप्रमेयस्य, तस्मात्, युध्यस्व, भारत ॥ १८ ॥
2:18.anvaya_sa: अयं, कदाचित्, न जायते, वा, न म्रियते, वा, (अयं) न, भूत्वा, भूयः, भविता, अयम्, अजः, नित्यः, शाश्वतः, पुराणः, शरीरे, हन्यमाने, न हन्यते ॥ २० ॥
2:18.pada_iast: antavantaḥ, ime, dehāḥ, nityasya, uktāḥ, śarīriṇaḥ, anāśinaḥ, aprameyasya, tasmāt, yudhyasva, bhārata || 18 ||
2:18.anvaya_iast: ayaṃ, kadācit, na jāyate, vā, na mriyate, vā, (ayaṃ) na, bhūtvā, bhūyaḥ, bhavitā, ayam, ajaḥ, nityaḥ, śāśvataḥ, purāṇaḥ, śarīre, hanyamāne, na hanyate || 20 ||
2:18.translation: These destructible bodies are said to belong to the everlasting, indestructible, indeterminable, embodied One. Therefore, O descendant of Bharata, join the battle.
2:18.explanation: -- Lord Krishna explains to Arjuna the nature of the allpervading? immortal Self in a variety of ways and thus induces him to fight by removing his delusion? grief and despondency which are born of ignorance.
2:18.word_meanings: अन्तवन्तः — having an end; इमे — these; देहाः — bodies; नित्यस्य — of the everlasting; उक्ताः — are said; शरीरिणः — of the embodied; अनाशिनः — of the indestructible; अप्रमेयस्य — of the immesaurable; तस्मात् — therefore; युध्यस्व — fight; भारत — O Bharata.

sa: य एनं वेत्ति हन्तारं यश्चैनं मन्यते हतम्
उभौ तौ न विजानीतो नायं हन्ति न हन्यते
iast: ya enaṁ vetti hantāraṁ yaśh chainaṁ manyate hatam
ubhau tau na vijānīto nāyaṁ hanti na hanyate

2:19.pada_sa: य, एवं, वेत्ति, हन्तारं, यः, च, एनं, मन्यते, हतम्, अभौ, तौ, न, विजानीतः, न, अयं, हन्ति, न, हन्यते ॥ १९ ॥
2:19.anvaya_sa: पार्थ, यः, एनम्, अविनाशिनं, नित्यम्, अजम्, अव्ययं, वेद, सः, पुरुषः, कथं, कं, घातयति, कं, हन्ति ॥ २१ ॥
2:19.pada_iast: ya, evaṃ, vetti, hantāraṃ, yaḥ, ca, enaṃ, manyate, hatam, abhau, tau, na, vijānītaḥ, na, ayaṃ, hanti, na, hanyate || 19 ||
2:19.anvaya_iast: pārtha, yaḥ, enam, avināśinaṃ, nityam, ajam, avyayaṃ, veda, saḥ, puruṣaḥ, kathaṃ, kaṃ, ghātayati, kaṃ, hanti || 21 ||
2:19.translation: He who thinks of this One as the killer, and he who thinks of this One as the killed  both of them do not know. This One does not kill, nor is It killed.
2:19.explanation: -- The Self is nondoer (Akarta) and as It is immutable? It is neither the agent nor the object of the act of slaying. He who thinks I slay or I am slain with the body or the Ahamkara (ego)? he does not really comprehend the true nature of the Self. The Self is indestructible. It exists in the three periods of time. It is Sat (Existence). When the body is destroyed? the Self is not destroyed. The body has to undergo change in any case. It is inevitable. But the Self is not at all affected by it. Verses 19? 20? 21? 23 and 24 speak of the immortality of the Self or Atman. (Cf.XVIII.17)
2:19.word_meanings: यः — he who; एनम् — this (Self); वेत्ति — knows; हन्तारम् — slayer; यः — he who; च — and; एनम् — this; मन्यते — thinks; हतम् — slain; उभौ — both; तौ — those; न — not; विजानीतः — know; न — not; अयम् — this; हन्ति — slays; न — not; हन्यते — is slain.

sa: न्नायं भूत्वा भविता वा न भूयः
iast: nāyaṁ bhūtvā bhavitā vā na bhūyaḥ

2:20.pada_sa: न, जायते, म्रियते, वा, कदाचित्, न, अयं, भूत्वा, भविता, वा, न, भूयः, अजः, नित्यः, शाश्वतः, अयं, पुराणः, न, हन्यते, हन्यमाने, शरीरे ॥ २० ॥
2:20.anvaya_sa: यथा, नरः, जीर्णानि, वासांसि, विहाय, अपराणि, नवानि, गृह्णाति, तथा, देही, जीर्णानि, शरीराणि, विहाय, अन्यानि, नवानि, संयाति ॥ २२ ॥
2:20.pada_iast: na, jāyate, mriyate, vā, kadācit, na, ayaṃ, bhūtvā, bhavitā, vā, na, bhūyaḥ, ajaḥ, nityaḥ, śāśvataḥ, ayaṃ, purāṇaḥ, na, hanyate, hanyamāne, śarīre || 20 ||
2:20.anvaya_iast: yathā, naraḥ, jīrṇāni, vāsāṃsi, vihāya, aparāṇi, navāni, gṛhṇāti, tathā, dehī, jīrṇāni, śarīrāṇi, vihāya, anyāni, navāni, saṃyāti || 22 ||
2:20.translation: The soul is never born nor does it ever die; nor having once existed, does it cease to be. The soul is unborn, eternal, ever-existing, and primeval. It is not slain when the body is slain.
2:20.explanation: This is one of the most powerful declarations in the Gita. Krishna stacks six negations to describe the soul: not born, not dying, not ceasing, unborn (ajaḥ), eternal (nityaḥ), primeval (purāṇaḥ). The final line is devastating in its simplicity — even when the body is destroyed, the soul remains untouched.

iast: vedāvināśhinaṁ nityaṁ ya enam ajam avyayam
kathaṁ sa puruṣhaḥ pārtha kaṁ ghātayati hanti kam

2:21.anvaya_sa: एनं, शस्त्राणि, न छिन्दन्ति, एनं, पावकः, न दहति, एनम्, आपः, न क्लेदयन्ति, च, मारुतः, न शोषयति  ॥ २३ ॥

2:21.translation: O Partha, he who knows this One as indestructible, eternal, birthless and undecaying, how and whom does that person kill, or whom does he cause to be killed! [This is not a estion but only an emphatic denial.-Tr.]
2:21.explanation: The enlightened sage who knows the immutable and indestructible Self through direct cognition or spiritual Anubhava (experience) cannot do the act of slaying. He cannot cause another to slay also.
2:21.word_meanings: वेद — knows; अविनाशिनम् — indestructible; नित्यम् — eternal; यः — who; एनम् — this (Self); अजम् — unborn; अव्ययम् — inexhaustible; कथम् — how; सः — he (that); पुरुषः — man; पार्थ — O Partha (son of Pritha); कम् — whom; घातयति — causes to be slain; हन्ति — kills; कम् — whom.

2:22.pada_iast: vāsāṃsi, jīrṇāni, yathā, vihāya, navāni, gṛhṇāti, naraḥ, aparāṇi, tathā, śarīrāṇi, vihāya, jīrṇāni, anyāni, saṃyāti, navāni, dehī || 22 ||
2:22.anvaya_iast: ayam, acchedyaḥ, ayam, adāhyaḥ, akledyaḥ, ca, aśoṣyaḥ, ayam, eva, nityaḥ, sarvagataḥ, acalaḥ, sthāṇuḥ, sanātanaḥ || 24 ||
2:22.translation: As after rejecting wornout clothes a man takes up other new ones, likewise after rejecting wornout bodies the embodied one unites with other new ones.
2:22.explanation: . Just as rejecting the tattered garments, a man takes other new ones,  in the same way,  rejecting the decayed bodies,  the embodied (Self) rightly proceeds to other new ones.

sa: नैनं छिन्दन्ति शस्त्राणि नैनं दहति पावकः
न चैनं क्लेदयन्त्यापो न शोषयति मारुतः
iast: nainaṁ chhindanti śhastrāṇi nainaṁ dahati pāvakaḥ
na chainaṁ kledayantyāpo na śhoṣhayati mārutaḥ

2:23.pada_sa: न, एनं, छिन्दन्ति, शस्त्राणि, न, एनं, दहति, पावकः, न, च, एनं, क्लेदयन्ति, आपः, न, शोषयति, मारुतः ॥ २३ ॥
2:23.anvaya_sa: अयम्, अव्यक्तः, अयम्, अचिन्त्यः, अयम्, अविकार्यः, उच्यते, तस्मात्, एनम्, एवं, विदित्वा, अनुशोचितुं, न अर्हसि ॥ २५ ॥
2:23.pada_iast: na, enaṃ, chindanti, śastrāṇi, na, enaṃ, dahati, pāvakaḥ, na, ca, enaṃ, kledayanti, āpaḥ, na, śoṣayati, mārutaḥ || 23 ||
2:23.anvaya_iast: ayam, avyaktaḥ, ayam, acintyaḥ, ayam, avikāryaḥ, ucyate, tasmāt, enam, evaṃ, viditvā, anuśocituṃ, na arhasi || 25 ||
2:23.translation: Weapons do not cut It, fire does not burn It, water does not moisten It, and air does not dry It.
2:23.explanation: The Self is indivisible. It has no parts. It is extremely subtle. It is infinite. Therefore? sword cannot cut It fire cannot burn It water cannot wet It wind cannot dry It.
2:23.word_meanings: न — not; एनम् — this (Self); छिन्दन्ति — cut; शस्त्राणि — weapons; न — not; एनम् — this; दहति — burns; पावकः — fire; न — not; ,च — and; एनम् — this; क्लेदयन्ति — wet; आपः — waters; न — not; शोषयति — dries; मारुतः — wind.

overrides.अच्छेद्योऽयमदाह्योऽयमक्लेद्योऽशोष्य: अच्छेद्यः अयम् अदाह्यः अयम् अक्लेद्यः अशोष्यः

2:24.pada_sa: अच्छेद्यः, अयम्, अदाह्यः, अयम्, अक्लेद्यः, अशोष्यः, एव, च, नित्यः, सर्वगतः, स्थाणुः, अचलः, अयं, सनातनः ॥ २४ ॥
2:24.anvaya_sa: अथ, च, त्वम्, एनं, नित्यजातं, वा, नित्यं, मृतं, मन्यसे, तथापि, महाबाहो, एवं, शोचितुं, न अर्हसि ॥ २६ ॥
2:24.pada_iast: acchedyaḥ, ayam, adāhyaḥ, ayam, akledyaḥ, aśoṣyaḥ, eva, ca, nityaḥ, sarvagataḥ, sthāṇuḥ, acalaḥ, ayaṃ, sanātanaḥ || 24 ||
2:24.anvaya_iast: atha, ca, tvam, enaṃ, nityajātaṃ, vā, nityaṃ, mṛtaṃ, manyase, tathāpi, mahābāho, evaṃ, śocituṃ, na arhasi || 26 ||
2:24.translation: It cannot be cut, It cannot be burnt, cannot be moistened, and surely cannot be dried up. It is eternal, omnipresent, stationary, unmoving and changeless.
2:24.explanation: The Self is very subtle. It is beyond the reach of speech and mind. It is very difficult to understand this subtle Self. So Lord Krishna explains the nature of the immortal Self in a variety of ways with various illustrations and examples? so that It can be grasped by the people.Sword cannot cut this Self. It is eternal. Because It is eternal? It is allpervading. Because It is allpervading? It is stable like a stature. Because It is stable? It is immovable. It is everlasting. Therefore? It is not produced out of any cause. It is not new. It is ancient.
2:24.word_meanings: अच्छेद्यः — cannot be cut; अयम् — this (Self); अदाह्यः — cannot be burnt; अयम् — this; अक्लेद्यः — cannot be wetted; अशोष्यः — cannot be died; एव — also; च — and; नित्यः — eternal; सर्वगतः — allpervading; स्थाणुः — stable; अचलः — immovable; अयम् — this; सनातनः — ancient.

2:25.pada_sa: अव्यक्तः, अयम्, अचिन्त्यः, अयम्, अविकार्यः, अयम्, उच्यते, तस्माद्, एवं, विदित्वा, एनं, न, अनुशोचितुम्, अर्हसि ॥ २५ ॥
2:25.anvaya_sa: हि, जातस्य, ध्रुवः, मृत्युः, च, मृतस्य, ध्रुवं, जन्म, तस्मात्, त्वम्, अपरिहार्ये, अर्थे, शोचितुं, न अर्हसि ॥ २७ ॥
2:25.pada_iast: avyaktaḥ, ayam, acintyaḥ, ayam, avikāryaḥ, ayam, ucyate, tasmād, evaṃ, viditvā, enaṃ, na, anuśocitum, arhasi || 25 ||
2:25.anvaya_iast: hi, jātasya, dhruvaḥ, mṛtyuḥ, ca, mṛtasya, dhruvaṃ, janma, tasmāt, tvam, aparihārye, arthe, śocituṃ, na arhasi || 27 ||
2:25.translation: It is said that This is unmanifest; This is inconceivable; This is unchangeable. Therefore, having known This thus, you ougth not to grieve.
2:25.explanation: The Self is not an object of perception. It can hardly be seen by the physical eyes. Therefore? the Self is unmanifested. That which is seen by the eyes becomes an object of thought. As the Self cannot be perceived by the eyes? It is unthinkable. Milk when mixed with buttermilk changes its form. The Self cannot change Its form like milk. Hence? It is changeless and immutable. Therefore? thus understanding the Self? thou shouldst not mourn. Thou shouldst not think also that thou art their slayer and that they are killed by thee.
2:25.word_meanings: अव्यक्तः — unmanifested; अयम् — this (Self); अचिन्त्यः — unthinkable; अयम् — this; अविकार्यः — unchangeable; अयम् — this; उच्यते — is said; तस्मात् — therefore; एवम् — thus; विदित्वा — having known; एनम् — this; न — not; अनुशोचितुम् — to grieve; अर्हसि (thou) — oughtest.

sa: अथ चैनं नित्यजातं नित्यं वा मन्यसे मृतम्
iast: atha chainaṁ nitya-jātaṁ nityaṁ vā manyase mṛitam
tathāpi tvaṁ mahā-bāho naivaṁ śhochitum arhasi

2:26.pada_sa: अथ, च, एनं, नित्यजातं, नित्यं, वा, मन्यसे, मृतं, तथा, अपि, त्वं, महाबाहो, न, एवं, शोचितुम्, अर्हसि ॥ २६ ॥
2:26.anvaya_sa: भारत, भूतानि, अव्यक्तादीनि, अव्यक्तनिधनानि, व्यक्तमध्यानि, एव, तत्र, का, परिदेवना ॥ २८ ॥
2:26.pada_iast: atha, ca, enaṃ, nityajātaṃ, nityaṃ, vā, manyase, mṛtaṃ, tathā, api, tvaṃ, mahābāho, na, evaṃ, śocitum, arhasi || 26 ||
2:26.anvaya_iast: bhārata, bhūtāni, avyaktādīni, avyaktanidhanāni, vyaktamadhyāni, eva, tatra, kā, paridevanā || 28 ||
2:26.translation: On the other hand, if you think this One is born continually or dies constantly, even then, O mighty-armed one, you ought not to grieve thus.
2:26.explanation: Lord Krishna here? for the sake of argument? takes up the popular supposition. Granting that the Self is again and again born whenever a body comes into being? and again and again dies whenever the body dies? O mightyarmed (O Arjuna of great valour and strength)? thou shouldst not grieve thus? because birth is inevitable to want is dead and death is inevitable to what is born. This is the inexorable or unrelenting Law of Nature.
2:26.word_meanings: अथ — now; च — and; एनम् — this (Self); नित्यजातम् — constantly born; नित्यम् — constantly; वा — or; मन्यसे — thinkest; मृतम् — dead; तथापि — even then; त्वम् — thou; महाबाहो — mightyarmed; न — not; एवम् — thus; शोचितुम् — to grieve; अर्हसि (thou) — oughtest.

sa: जातस्य हि ध्रुवो मृत्युर्ध्रुवं जन्म मृतस्य च
iast: jātasya hi dhruvo mṛityur dhruvaṁ janma mṛitasya ca
tasmād aparihārye ’rthe na tvaṁ śhochitum arhasi

2:27.pada_sa: जातस्य, हि, ध्रुवः, मृत्युः, ध्रुवं, जन्म, मृतस्य, च, तस्मात्, अपरिहार्ये, अर्थे, न, त्वं, शोचितुम्, अर्हसि ॥ २७ ॥
2:27.anvaya_sa: कश्चित्, एनम्, आश्चर्यवत्, पश्यति, च, तथा, एव, अन्यः, अश्चर्यवत्, वदति, च, अन्यः, एनम्, अश्चर्यवत्, शृणोति, च, कश्चित्, श्रुत्वा, अपि, एनं, न एव वेद ॥ २९ ॥
2:27.pada_iast: jātasya, hi, dhruvaḥ, mṛtyuḥ, dhruvaṃ, janma, mṛtasya, ca, tasmāt, aparihārye, arthe, na, tvaṃ, śocitum, arhasi || 27 ||
2:27.anvaya_iast: kaścit, enam, āścaryavat, paśyati, ca, tathā, eva, anyaḥ, aścaryavat, vadati, ca, anyaḥ, enam, aścaryavat, śṛṇoti, ca, kaścit, śrutvā, api, enaṃ, na eva veda || 29 ||
2:27.translation: For death of anyone born is certain, and of the dead (re-) birth is a certainly. Therefore you ought not to grieve over an inevitable fact.
2:27.explanation: Birth is sure to happen to that which is dead death is sure to happen to what which is born. Birth and death are certainly unavoidable. Therefore? you should not grieve over an inevitable matter.
2:27.word_meanings: जातस्य — of the born; हि — for; ध्रुवः — certain; मृत्युः — death; ध्रुवम् — certain; जन्म — birth; मृतस्य — of the dead; च — and; तस्मात् — therefore; अपरिहार्ये — inevritable; अर्थे — in matter; न — not; त्वम् — thou; शोचितुम् — to grieve; अर्हसि (thou) — oughtest.

2:28.pada_sa: अव्यक्तादीनि, भूतानि, व्यक्तमध्यानि, भारत, अव्यक्तनिधनानि, एव, तत्र, का, परिदेवना ॥ २८ ॥
2:28.anvaya_sa: भारत, अयं, देही, सर्वस्य, देहे, नित्यम्, अवध्यः, तस्मात्, सर्वाणि, भूतानि, त्वं, शोचितुं, न अर्हसि ॥ ३० ॥
2:28.pada_iast: avyaktādīni, bhūtāni, vyaktamadhyāni, bhārata, avyaktanidhanāni, eva, tatra, kā, paridevanā || 28 ||
2:28.anvaya_iast: bhārata, ayaṃ, dehī, sarvasya, dehe, nityam, avadhyaḥ, tasmāt, sarvāṇi, bhūtāni, tvaṃ, śocituṃ, na arhasi || 30 ||
2:28.translation: O descendant of Bharata, all beings remain unmanifest in the beginning;; they become manifest in the middle. After death they certainly become unmanifest. What lamentation can there be with regard to them?
2:28.explanation: The physical body is a combination of the five elements. It is seen by the physical eyes only after the five elements have entered into such combination. After death? the body disintegrates and the five elements go back to their source it cannot be seen. Therefore? the body can be seen only in the middle state. The relationship as son? friend? teacher? father? mother? wife? brother and sister is formed through the body on account of attachment and Moha (delusion). Just as planks unite and separate in a river? just as pilgrims unite and separate in a public inn? so also fathers? mothers? sons and brothers unite and separate in this world. This world is a very big public inn. People unite and separate.There is no pot in the beginning and in the end. Even if you see the pot in the middle? you should think and feel that it is illusory and does not really exist. So also there is no body in the beginning and in the end. That which does not exist in the beginning and in the end must be illusory in the middle also. You must think and feel that the body does not really exist in the middle as well.He who thus understands the nature of the body and all human relationships based on it? will not grieve.
2:28.word_meanings: अव्यक्तादीनि — unmanifested in the beginning; भूतानि — beings; व्यक्तमध्यानि — manifested in their middle state; भारत — O Bharata; अव्यक्तनिधनानि — unmanifested again in the end; एव — also; तत्र — there; का — what; परिदेवना — grief.

iast: śhrutvāpy enaṁ veda na chaiva kaśhchit

2:29.pada_sa: अश्चर्यवत्, पश्यति, कश्चित्, एनम्, आश्चर्यवत्, वदति, तथा, एव, च, अन्यः, आशर्यवत्, च, एनम्, अन्यः, शृणोति, श्रुत्वा, अपि, एनं, वेद, न, च, एव, कश्चित्  ॥ २९ ॥
2:29.anvaya_sa: च, स्वधर्मम्, अवेक्ष्य, अपि, विकम्पितुं, न अर्हसि, हि, धर्म्यात्, युद्धात्, अन्यत्, श्रेयः, क्षत्रियस्य, न, विद्यते ॥ ३० ॥
2:29.pada_iast: aścaryavat, paśyati, kaścit, enam, āścaryavat, vadati, tathā, eva, ca, anyaḥ, āśaryavat, ca, enam, anyaḥ, śṛṇoti, śrutvā, api, enaṃ, veda, na, ca, eva, kaścit  || 29 ||
2:29.anvaya_iast: ca, svadharmam, avekṣya, api, vikampituṃ, na arhasi, hi, dharmyāt, yuddhāt, anyat, śreyaḥ, kṣatriyasya, na, vidyate || 30 ||
2:29.translation: Someone visualizes It as a wonder; and similarly indeed, someone else talks of It as a wonder; and someone else hears of It as a wonder. And some one else, indeed, does not realize It even after hearing about It.
2:29.explanation: The verse may also be interpreted in this manner. He that sees? hears and speaks of the Self is a wonderful man. Such a man is very rare. He is one among many thousands. Thus the Self is very hard to understand.
2:29.word_meanings: आश्चर्यवत् — as a wonder; पश्यति — sees; कश्चित् — sone one; एनम् — this (Self); आश्चर्यवत् — as a wonder; वदति — speaks of; तथा — so; एव — also; च — and; अन्यः — another; आश्चर्यवत् — as a wonder; च — and; एनम् — this; अन्यः — another; श्रृणोति — hears; श्रुत्वा — having heard; अपि — even; एनम् — this; वेद — knows; न — not; च — and; एव — also; कश्चित् — any one.

iast: dehī nityam avadhyo ’yaṁ dehe sarvasya bhārata
tasmāt sarvāṇi bhūtāni na tvaṁ śhochitum arhasi

2:30.pada_sa: देही, नित्यम्, अवध्यः, अयं, देहे, सर्वस्य, भारत, तस्मात्, सर्वाणि, भूतनि, न, त्वं, शोचितुम्, अर्हसि ॥ ३० ॥
2:30.anvaya_sa: पार्थ, यदृच्छया, उपपन्नम्, च, अपावृतं, स्वर्गाद्वारं, ईदृशं, युद्धं, सुखिनः, क्षत्रियाः, लभन्ते ॥ ३२ ॥
2:30.pada_iast: dehī, nityam, avadhyaḥ, ayaṃ, dehe, sarvasya, bhārata, tasmāt, sarvāṇi, bhūtani, na, tvaṃ, śocitum, arhasi || 30 ||
2:30.anvaya_iast: pārtha, yadṛcchayā, upapannam, ca, apāvṛtaṃ, svargādvāraṃ, īdṛśaṃ, yuddhaṃ, sukhinaḥ, kṣatriyāḥ, labhante || 32 ||
2:30.translation: O descendant of Bharata, this embodied Self existing in everyone's body can never be killed. Therefore you ought not to grieve for all (these) beings.
2:30.explanation: The body of any creature may be destroyed but the Self cannot be killed. Therefore you should not grieve regarding any creature whatever? Bhishma or anybody else.
2:30.word_meanings: देही — indweller; नित्यम् — always; अवध्यः — indestructible; अयम् — this; देहे — in the body; सर्वस्य — of all; भारत — O Bharata; तस्मात् — therefore; सर्वाणि (for) — all; भूतानि — creatures; न — not; त्वम् — thou; शोचितुम् — to grieve; अर्हसि (thou) — shouldst.

iast: swa-dharmam api chāvekṣhya na vikampitum arhasi
dharmyāddhi yuddhāch chhreyo ’nyat kṣhatriyasya na vidyate

2:31.pada_sa: स्वधर्मम्, अपि, च, अवेक्ष्य, न, विकम्पितुम्, अर्हसि, धर्म्यात्, हि, युद्धात्, श्रेयः, अन्यत्, क्षत्रियस्य, न, विद्यते ॥ ३१ ॥
2:31.anvaya_sa: अथ, चेत्, त्वं, इमं, धर्म्यं, संग्रामं, न, करिष्यसि, ततः, स्वधर्मं, च, कीर्तिं, हित्वा, पापम्, अवाप्स्यसि ॥ ३३ ॥
2:31.pada_iast: svadharmam, api, ca, avekṣya, na, vikampitum, arhasi, dharmyāt, hi, yuddhāt, śreyaḥ, anyat, kṣatriyasya, na, vidyate || 31 ||
2:31.anvaya_iast: atha, cet, tvaṃ, imaṃ, dharmyaṃ, saṃgrāmaṃ, na, kariṣyasi, tataḥ, svadharmaṃ, ca, kīrtiṃ, hitvā, pāpam, avāpsyasi || 33 ||
2:31.translation: Even considering your own duty you should not waver, since there is nothing else better for a Ksatriya than a righteous battle.
2:31.explanation: Lord Krishna now gives to Arjuna wordly reasons for fighting. Up to this time? He talked to Arjuna on the immortality of the Self and gave him philosophical reasons. Now He says to Arjuna? O Arjuna Fighting is a Kshatriyas own duty. You ought not to swerve from that duty. To a Kshatriyta (one born in the warrior or ruling class) nothing is more welcome than a righteous war. A warrior should fight.
2:31.word_meanings: स्वधर्मम् — own duty; अपि — also; च — and; अवेक्ष्य — looking at; न — not; विकम्पितुम् — to waver; अर्हसि (thou) — oughtest; धर्म्यात् — than righteous; हि — indeed; युद्धात् — than war; श्रेयः — higher; अन्यत् — other; क्षत्रियस्य — of a Kshatriya; न — not; विद्यते — is.

iast: sukhinaḥ kṣhatriyāḥ pārtha labhante yuddham īdṛiśham

2:32.pada_sa: यदृच्छया, च, उपपन्नं, स्वर्गद्वारम्, अपावृतम्, सुखिनः, क्षत्रियाः, पार्थ, लभन्ते, युद्धम्, ईदृशम् ॥ ३२ ॥
2:32.anvaya_sa: च, भूतानि, ते, अव्ययाम्, अकीर्तिम्, अपि, कथयिष्यन्ति, च, अकीर्तिः, संभावितस्य, मरणात्, अतिरिच्यते ॥ ३४ ॥
2:32.pada_iast: yadṛcchayā, ca, upapannaṃ, svargadvāram, apāvṛtam, sukhinaḥ, kṣatriyāḥ, pārtha, labhante, yuddham, īdṛśam || 32 ||
2:32.anvaya_iast: ca, bhūtāni, te, avyayām, akīrtim, api, kathayiṣyanti, ca, akīrtiḥ, saṃbhāvitasya, maraṇāt, atiricyate || 34 ||
2:32.translation: O son of Partha, happy are the Ksatriyas who come across this kind of a battle, which presents itself unsought for and which is an open gate to heaven.
2:32.explanation: The scriptures declare that if a Kshatriya dies for a righteous cause on the battlefield? he at once goes to heaven.
2:32.word_meanings: यदृच्छया — of itself; च — and; उपपन्नम् — come; स्वर्गद्वारम् — the gate of heaven; अपावृतम् — opened; सुखिनः — happy; क्षत्रियाः — Kshatriyas; पार्थ — O Partha; लभन्ते — obtain; युद्धम् — battle; ईदृशम् — such.

sa: अथ चेत्त्वमिमं धर्म्यं सङ्ग्रामं न करिष्यसि
ततः स्वधर्मं कीर्तिं च हित्वा पापमवाप्स्यसि
iast: atha chet tvam imaṁ dharmyaṁ saṅgrāmaṁ na kariṣhyasi
tataḥ sva-dharmaṁ kīrtiṁ cha hitvā pāpam avāpsyasi

2:33.pada_sa: अथ, चेत्, त्वम्, इमं, धर्म्यं, सङ्ग्रामं, न, करिष्यसि, ततः, स्वधर्मं, कीर्तिं, च, हित्वा, पापम्, अवाप्स्यसि ॥ ३३ ॥
2:33.anvaya_sa: च, येषां, त्वं, बहुमतः, भूत्वा, लाघवं, यास्यसि, महारथाः, त्वां, भयात्, रणात्, उपरतं, मंस्यन्ते ॥ ३५ ॥
2:33.pada_iast: atha, cet, tvam, imaṃ, dharmyaṃ, saṅgrāmaṃ, na, kariṣyasi, tataḥ, svadharmaṃ, kīrtiṃ, ca, hitvā, pāpam, avāpsyasi || 33 ||
2:33.anvaya_iast: ca, yeṣāṃ, tvaṃ, bahumataḥ, bhūtvā, lāghavaṃ, yāsyasi, mahārathāḥ, tvāṃ, bhayāt, raṇāt, uparataṃ, maṃsyante || 35 ||
2:33.translation: On the other hand, if you will not fight this righteous battle, then, forsaking your own duty and fame, you will incur sin.
2:33.explanation: The Lord reminds Arjuna of the fame he had already earned and which he would now lose if he refused to fight. Arjuna had acired great fame by fighting with Lord Siva. Arjuna proceeded on a pilgrimage to the Himalayas. He fought with Siva Who appeared in the guise of a mountaineer (Kirata) and got from Him the Pasupatastra? a celestial weapon.
2:33.word_meanings: अथ चेत् — but if; त्वम् — thou; इमम् — this; धर्म्यम् — righteous; संग्रामम् — warfare; न — not; करिष्यसि — will do; स्वधर्मम् — own duty; कीर्तिम् — fame; च — and; हित्वा — having abandoned; पापम् — sin; अवाप्स्यसि — shall incur.

2:34.pada_sa: अकीर्तिं, च, अपि, भूतानि, कथयिष्यन्ति, ते, अव्ययं, सम्भावितस्य, च, अकीर्तिः, मरणात्, अतिरिच्यते  ॥ ३४ ॥
2:34.anvaya_sa: च, तव, अहिताः, तव, सामर्थ्यं, निन्दन्तः, बहून्, अवाच्यवादान्, वदिष्यन्ति, नु, ततः, दुःखतरंं, किम् ॥ ३६ ॥
2:34.pada_iast: akīrtiṃ, ca, api, bhūtāni, kathayiṣyanti, te, avyayaṃ, sambhāvitasya, ca, akīrtiḥ, maraṇāt, atiricyate  || 34 ||
2:34.anvaya_iast: ca, tava, ahitāḥ, tava, sāmarthyaṃ, nindantaḥ, bahūn, avācyavādān, vadiṣyanti, nu, tataḥ, duḥkhataraṃṃ, kim || 36 ||
2:34.translation: People also will speak of your unending infamy. And to an honoured person infamy is worse than death.
2:34.explanation: The world also will ever recount thy infamy which will survive thee for a long time. Death is really preferable to disgrace to one who has been honoured as a great hero and mighty warrior with noble alities.
2:34.word_meanings: अकीर्तिम् — dishonour; च — and; अपि — also; भूतानि — beings; कथयिष्यन्ति — will tell; ते — thy; अव्ययाम् — everlasting; संभावितस्य — of the honoured; च — and; अकीर्तिः — dishonour; मरणात् — than death; अतिरिच्यते — exceeds.

sa: येषां च त्वं बहुमतो भूत्वा यास्यसि लाघवम्
iast: bhayād raṇād uparataṁ mansyante tvāṁ mahā-rathāḥ
yeṣhāṁ cha tvaṁ bahu-mato bhūtvā yāsyasi lāghavam

2:35.pada_sa: भयात्, रणात्, उपरतं, मंस्यन्ते, त्वां, महारथाः, येषां, च, त्वं, बहुमतः, भूत्वा, यास्यसि, लाघवम् ॥ ३५ ॥
2:35.anvaya_sa: वा, हतः, स्वर्गं, प्राप्स्यसि, वा, जित्वा, महीं, भोक्ष्यसे, तस्मात्, कौन्तेय, युद्धाय, कृतनिश्चयः, उत्तिष्ठ ॥ ३७ ॥
2:35.pada_iast: bhayāt, raṇāt, uparataṃ, maṃsyante, tvāṃ, mahārathāḥ, yeṣāṃ, ca, tvaṃ, bahumataḥ, bhūtvā, yāsyasi, lāghavam || 35 ||
2:35.anvaya_iast: vā, hataḥ, svargaṃ, prāpsyasi, vā, jitvā, mahīṃ, bhokṣyase, tasmāt, kaunteya, yuddhāya, kṛtaniścayaḥ, uttiṣṭha || 37 ||
2:35.translation: The great chariot-riders will think of you as having desisted from the fight out of fear; and you will into disgrace before them to whom you had been estimable.
2:35.explanation: Duryodhana and others will certainly think that you have fled from the battle from fear of Karna and others? but not through compassion and reverence for elders and teachers. Duryodhana and others who have shown great esteem to you on account of your chivalry? bravery and other noble alities? will think very lightly of you and treat you with contempt.
2:35.word_meanings: भयात् — from fear; रणात् — from the battle; उपरतम् — withdrawn; मंस्यन्ते — will think; त्वाम् — thee; महारथाः — the great carwarriors; येषाम् — of whom; च — and; त्वम् — thou; बहुमतः — much thought of; भूत्वा — having been; यास्यसि — will receive; लाघवम् — lightness.

sa: निन्दन्तस्तव सामर्थ्यं ततो दुःखतरं नु किम्
iast: nindantastava sāmarthyaṁ tato duḥkhataraṁ nu kim

2:36.pada_sa: अवाच्यवादान्, च, बहून्, वदिष्यन्ति, तव, आहिताः, निन्दन्तः, तव, सामर्थ्यं, ततः, दुःखतरं, नु, किम् ॥ ३६ ॥
2:36.anvaya_sa: सुखदुःखे, लाभालाभौ, जयाजयौ, समे, कृत्वा, ततः, युद्धाय, युज्यस्व, एवं, पापं, न अवाप्स्यसि ॥ ३८ ॥
2:36.pada_iast: avācyavādān, ca, bahūn, vadiṣyanti, tava, āhitāḥ, nindantaḥ, tava, sāmarthyaṃ, tataḥ, duḥkhataraṃ, nu, kim || 36 ||
2:36.anvaya_iast: sukhaduḥkhe, lābhālābhau, jayājayau, same, kṛtvā, tataḥ, yuddhāya, yujyasva, evaṃ, pāpaṃ, na avāpsyasi || 38 ||
2:36.translation: And your enemies will speak many indecent words while denigrating your might. What can be more painful than that?
2:36.explanation: There is really no pain more unbearable and tormenting that that of slander thus incurred.
2:36.word_meanings: अवाच्यवादान् — words that are improper to be spoken; च — and; बहून् — many; वदिष्यन्ति — will say; तव — thy; अहिताः — enemies; निन्दन्तः — cavilling; तव — thy; सामर्थ्यम् — power; ततः — than this; दुःखतरम् — more painful; नु — indeed; किम् — what.

sa: हतो वा प्राप्स्यसि स्वर्गं जित्वा वा भोक्ष्यसे महीम्
iast: hato vā prāpsyasi swargaṁ jitvā vā bhokṣhyase mahīm

2:37.pada_sa: हतः, वा, प्राप्स्यसि, स्वर्गं, जित्वा, वा, भोक्ष्यसे, महीं, तस्मात्, उत्तिष्ठ, कौन्तेय, युद्धाय, कृतनिश्चयः ॥ ३७ ॥
2:37.anvaya_sa: पार्थ, एषा, बुद्धिः, ते, सांख्ये, अभिहिता, तु, इमां, योगे, शृणु, यया, बुद्ध्या, युक्तः, कर्मबन्धं, प्रहास्यसि ॥ ३९ ॥
2:37.pada_iast: hataḥ, vā, prāpsyasi, svargaṃ, jitvā, vā, bhokṣyase, mahīṃ, tasmāt, uttiṣṭha, kaunteya, yuddhāya, kṛtaniścayaḥ || 37 ||
2:37.anvaya_iast: pārtha, eṣā, buddhiḥ, te, sāṃkhye, abhihitā, tu, imāṃ, yoge, śṛṇu, yayā, buddhyā, yuktaḥ, karmabandhaṃ, prahāsyasi || 39 ||
2:37.translation: Either by being killed you will attain heaven, or by winning you will enjoy the earth. Therefore, O Arjuna, rise up with determination for fighting.
2:37.explanation: In either case you will be benefited. Therefore? stand up with the firm resolution I will coner the enemy or die.
2:37.word_meanings: हतः — slain; वा — or; प्राप्स्यसि (thou) — wilt obtain; स्वर्गम् — heaven; जित्वा — having conered; वा — or; भोक्ष्यसे (thou) — wilt enjoy; महीम् — the earth; तस्मात् — therefore; उत्तिष्ठ — stand up; कौन्तेय — O son of Kunti; युद्धाय — for fight; कृतनिश्चयः — resolved.

iast: tato yuddhāya yujyasva naivaṁ pāpam avāpsyasi

2:38.pada_sa: सुखदुःखे, समे, कृत्वा, लाभालाभौ, जयाजयौ, ततः, युद्धाय, युज्यस्व, न, एवं, पापम्, अवाप्स्यसि ॥ ३८ ॥
2:38.anvaya_sa: इह, अभिक्रमनाशः, न अस्ति, प्रत्यवायः, न विद्यते, अस्य, धर्मस्य, सवल्पम्, अपि, महतः, भयात्, त्रायते ॥ ४० ॥
2:38.pada_iast: sukhaduḥkhe, same, kṛtvā, lābhālābhau, jayājayau, tataḥ, yuddhāya, yujyasva, na, evaṃ, pāpam, avāpsyasi || 38 ||
2:38.anvaya_iast: iha, abhikramanāśaḥ, na asti, pratyavāyaḥ, na vidyate, asya, dharmasya, savalpam, api, mahataḥ, bhayāt, trāyate || 40 ||
2:38.translation: Treating happiness and sorrow, gain and loss, and conest and defeat with eanimity, then engage in battle. Thus you will not incur sin.
2:38.explanation: This is the Yoga of eanimity or the doctrine of poise in action. If anyone does any action with the above mental attitude or balanced state of mind he will not reap the fruits of his action. Such an action will lead to the purification of his heart and freedom from birth and death. One has to develop such a balanced state of mind through continous struggle and vigilant efforts.
2:38.word_meanings: सुखदुःखे — pleasure and pain; समे — same; कृत्वा — having made; लाभालाभौ — gain and loss; जयाजयौ — victory and defeat; ततः — then; युद्धाय — for battle; युज्यस्व — engage thou; न — not; एवम् — thus; पापम् — sin; अवाप्स्यसि — shalt incur.

sa: एषा तेऽभिहिता साङ्ख्ये बुद्धिर्योगे त्विमां शृणु
बुद्ध्या युक्तो यया पार्थ कर्मबन्धं प्रहास्यसि
iast: eṣhā te ’bhihitā sānkhye buddhir yoge tvimāṁ śhṛiṇu
buddhyā yukto yayā pārtha karma-bandhaṁ prahāsyasi

2:39.pada_sa: एषा, ते, अभिहिता, साङ्‍ख्ये, बुद्धिः, योगे, तु, इमां, शृणु, बुद्ध्या, युक्तः, यया, पार्थ, कर्मबन्धं, प्रहास्यसि ॥ ३९ ॥
2:39.anvaya_sa: कुरुनन्दन, इह, व्ययसायात्मिका, बुद्धिः, एका हि, च, अव्यववसायिनां, बुद्धयः, बहुशाखाः, अनन्ताः ॥ ४१ ॥
2:39.pada_iast: eṣā, te, abhihitā, sāṅ‍khye, buddhiḥ, yoge, tu, imāṃ, śṛṇu, buddhyā, yuktaḥ, yayā, pārtha, karmabandhaṃ, prahāsyasi || 39 ||
2:39.anvaya_iast: kurunandana, iha, vyayasāyātmikā, buddhiḥ, ekā hi, ca, avyavavasāyināṃ, buddhayaḥ, bahuśākhāḥ, anantāḥ || 41 ||
2:39.translation: O Partha, this wisdom has been imparted to you from the standpoint of Self-realization. But listen to this (wisdom) from the standpoint of Yoga, endowed with which wisdom you will get rid of the bondage of action.
2:39.explanation: Lord Krishna taught Jnana (knowledge) to Arjuna till now. (Sankhya Yoga is the path of Vedanta or Jnana Yoga? which treats of the nature of the Atman or the Self and the methods to attain Selfrealisation. It is not the Sankhya philosophy of sage Kapila.) He is now giving to teach Arjuna the technie or secret of Karma Yoga endowed with which he (or anybody else) can break through the bonds of Karma. The Karma Yogi should perform work without expectation of fruits of his actions? without the idea of agency (or the notin I do this)? without attachment? after annihilating or going beyond all the pairs of opposites such as heat and cold? gain and loss? victoyr and defeat? etc. Dharma and Adharma? or merit and demerit will not touch that Karma Yogi who works without attachment and egoism. The Karma Yogi consecrates all his works and their fruits as offerings unto the Lord (Isvararpanam) and thus obtains the grace of the Lord (Isvaraprasada).
2:39.word_meanings: एषा — this; ते — to thee; अभिहिता (is) — declared; सांख्ये — in Sankhya; बुद्धिः — wisdom; योगे — in the Yoga; तु — indeed; इमाम् — this; श्रृणु — hear; बुद्ध्या — with wisdom; युक्तः — endowed with; यया — which; पार्थ — O Partha; कर्मबन्धम् — bondage of Karma; प्रहास्यसि (thou) — shalt cast off.

iast: svalpam apyasya dharmasya trāyate mahato bhayāt

2:40.pada_sa: न, इह, अभिक्रमनाशः, अस्ति, प्रत्यवायः, न, विद्यते, स्वल्पम्, अपि, अस्य, धर्मस्य, त्रायते, महतः, भयात् ॥ ४० ॥
2:40.anvaya_sa: पार्थ, कामात्मानः, वेवादरताः, स्वर्गपराः, अन्यत्, न अस्ति, इति, वादिनः, अविपश्चितः, जन्मकर्मफलप्रदां, भोगैश्वर्यगतिं प्रति, क्रियाविशेषबहुलां, इमां, यां, पुष्पितां, वाचं, प्रवदन्ति ॥४२-४३ ॥
