2:40.pada_iast: na, iha, abhikramanāśaḥ, asti, pratyavāyaḥ, na, vidyate, svalpam, api, asya, dharmasya, trāyate, mahataḥ, bhayāt || 40 ||
2:40.anvaya_iast: pārtha, kāmātmānaḥ, vevādaratāḥ, svargaparāḥ, anyat, na asti, iti, vādinaḥ, avipaścitaḥ, janmakarmaphalapradāṃ, bhogaiśvaryagatiṃ prati, kriyāviśeṣabahulāṃ, imāṃ, yāṃ, puṣpitāṃ, vācaṃ, pravadanti ||42-43 ||
2:40.translation: Here there is no waste of an attempt; nor is there (any) harm. Even a little of this righteousness saves (one) from great fear.
2:40.explanation: If a religious ceremony is left uncompleted? it is a wastage as the performer cannot realise the fruits. But it is not so in the case of Karma Yoga because every action causes immediate purification of the heart.In agriculture there is uncertainty. The farmer may till the land? plough and sow the seed but he may not get a crop if there is no rain. This is not so in Karma Yoga. There is no uncertainty at all. Further? there is no chance of any harm coming out of it. In the case of medical treatment great harm will result from the doctors injudicious treatment if he uses a wrong medicine. But it is not so in the case of Karma Yoga. Anything done? however little it may be? in this path of Yoga? the Yoga of action? saves one from great fear of being caught in the wheel of birth and death. Lord Krishna here extols Karma Yoga in order to create interest in Arjuna in this Yoga.
2:40.word_meanings: न — not; इह — in this; अभिक्रमनाशः — loss of effort; अस्ति — is; प्रत्यवायः — production of contrary results; न — not; विद्यते — is; स्वल्पम् — very little; अपि — even; अस्य — of this; धर्मस्य — duty; त्रायते — protects; महतः (from) — great; भयात् — fear.

2:41.pada_sa: व्ययसायात्मिका, बुद्धिः, एका, इह, कुरुनन्दन, बहुशाखाः, हि, अनन्ताः, च, बुद्धयः, अव्यवसायिनाम्  ॥ ४१ ॥
2:41.anvaya_sa: तया, अपहृतचेतसां, भोगश्वैर्यप्रसक्तानां, समाधौ, व्ययसायात्मिका, बुद्धिः, न विधीयते ॥ ४४ ॥
2:41.pada_iast: vyayasāyātmikā, buddhiḥ, ekā, iha, kurunandana, bahuśākhāḥ, hi, anantāḥ, ca, buddhayaḥ, avyavasāyinām  || 41 ||
2:41.anvaya_iast: tayā, apahṛtacetasāṃ, bhogaśvairyaprasaktānāṃ, samādhau, vyayasāyātmikā, buddhiḥ, na vidhīyate || 44 ||
2:41.translation: O scion of the Kuru dynasty, in this there is a single, one-pointed conviction. The thoughts of the irresolute ones have many branches indeed, and are innumerable.
2:41.explanation: Here? in this path to Bliss there is only one thought of a resolute nature there is singleminded determination. This single thought arises from the right source of knowledge. The student of Yoga collects all the dissipated rays of the mind. He gathers all of them through discrimination? dispassion and concentration. He is free from wavering or vacillation of the mind.The worldlyminded man who is suck in the mire of Samsara has no singleminded determination. He entertains countless thoughts. His mind is always unsteady and vacillating.If thoughts cease? Samsara also ceases. Mind generates endless thoughts and this world comes into being. Thoughts? and names and forms are inseparable. If the thoughts are controlled? the mind is controlled and the Yogi is liberated.
2:41.word_meanings: व्यवसायात्मिका — onepointed; बुद्धिः — determination; एका — single; इह — here; कुरुनन्दन — O joy of the Kurus; बहुशाखाः — manybranched; हि — indeed; अनन्ताः — endless; च — and; बुद्धयः — thoughts; अव्यवसायिनाम् — of the irresoulte.

2:42.pada_sa: याम्, इमां, पुष्पितां, वाचं, प्रवदन्ति, अविपश्चितः, वेदवादरताः, पार्थ, न, अन्यत्, अस्ति, इति, वादिनः ॥ ४२ ॥
2:42.anvaya_sa: अर्जुन, वेदाः, त्रैगुण्यविषयाः, निस्त्रैगुण्यः, निर्द्वन्द्वः, नित्यः, सत्त्वस्थः, निर्योगक्षेमः, आत्मवान्, भव ॥ ४५ ॥
2:42.pada_iast: yām, imāṃ, puṣpitāṃ, vācaṃ, pravadanti, avipaścitaḥ, vedavādaratāḥ, pārtha, na, anyat, asti, iti, vādinaḥ || 42 ||
2:42.anvaya_iast: arjuna, vedāḥ, traiguṇyaviṣayāḥ, nistraiguṇyaḥ, nirdvandvaḥ, nityaḥ, sattvasthaḥ, niryogakṣemaḥ, ātmavān, bhava || 45 ||
2:42.translation: -2.43  O son of Prtha, those undiscerning people who utter this flowery talk  which promises birth as a result of rites and duties, and is full of various special rites meant for the attainment of enjoyment and affluence , they remain engrossed in the utterances of the Vedas and declare that nothing else exists; their minds are full of desires and they have heaven as the goal.
2:42.explanation: Unwise people who are lacking in discrimination lay great stress upon the Karma Kanda or the ritualistic portion of the Vedas? which lays down specific rules for specific actions for,the attainment of specific fruits and ectol these actions and rewards unduly. They are highly enamoured of such Vedic passages which prescribe ways for the attainment of heavenly enjoyments. They say that there is nothing else beyond the sensual enjoyments in Svarga (heaven) which can be obtained by performing the rites of the Karma Kanda of the Vedas.There are two main divisions of the Vedas -- Karma Kanda (the section dealing with action) and Jnana Kanda (the section dealing with knowledge). The Karma Kanda comprises the Brahmanas and the Samhitas. This is the authority for the Purvamimamsa school founded by Jaimini. The followers of this school deal with rituals and prescribe many of them for attaining enjoyments and power here and happiness in heaven. They regard this as the ultimate object of human existence. Ordinary people are attracted by their panegyrics. The Jnana Kanda comprises the Aranyakas and the Upanishads which deal with the nature of Brahman or the Supreme Self.Life in heaven is also transitory. After the fruits of the good actions are exhausted? one has to come back to this earthplane. Liberatio or Moksha can only be attained by knowledge of the Self but not by performing a thousand and one sacrifices.Lord Krishna assigns a comparatively inferior position to the doctrine of the Mimamsakas of performing Vedic sacrifices for obtaining heaven? power and lordship in this world as they cannot give us final liberation.
2:42.word_meanings: याम — which; इमाम् — this; पुष्पिताम् — flowery; वाचम् — speech; प्रवदन्ति — utter; अविपश्चितः — the unwise; वेदवादरताः — takign pleasure in the eulogising words of the Vedas; पार्थ — O Partha; न — not; अन्यत् — other; अस्ति — is; इति — thus; वादिनः — saying.

2:43.pada_sa: कामात्मानः, स्वर्गपराः, जन्मकर्मफलप्रदाम्, क्रियाविशेषबहुलां, भोगैश्वर्यगतिं, प्रति ॥ ४३ ॥
2:43.anvaya_sa: सर्वतः, संप्लुतोदके, उदपाने, यावान्, अर्थः, विजानतः, ब्राह्मणस्य, सर्वेषु, वेदेषु, तावान्  ॥ ४६ ॥
2:43.pada_iast: kāmātmānaḥ, svargaparāḥ, janmakarmaphalapradām, kriyāviśeṣabahulāṃ, bhogaiśvaryagatiṃ, prati || 43 ||
2:43.anvaya_iast: sarvataḥ, saṃplutodake, udapāne, yāvān, arthaḥ, vijānataḥ, brāhmaṇasya, sarveṣu, vedeṣu, tāvān  || 46 ||
2:43.translation: -2.43 O son of Prtha, those undiscerning people who utter this flowery talk  which promises birth as a result of rites and duties, and is full of various special rites meant for the attainment of enjoyment and affluence , they remain engrossed in the utterances of the Vedas and declare that nothing else exists; their minds are full of desires and they have heaven as the goal.
2:43.explanation: . - 2.43. O son of  Prtha !  Those, whose very nature is desire,  whose goal is heaven,  who esteem only the Vedic declaration [of fruits],  who declare that there is nothing else,  who proclaim this flowery speech about the paths to the lordship of the objects of enjoyment-[the paths]  that are full of different actionsand who desire action alone as a fruit of their birth-they are men without insight.
2:43.word_meanings: कामात्मानः — full of desires; स्वर्गपराः — with heaven as their highest goal; जन्मकर्मफलप्रदाम् — leading to (new) births as the result of their works; क्रियाविशेषबहुलाम् — exuberant with various specifi actions; भोगैश्वर्यगतिम् प्रति — for the attainment of pleasure and lordship.No commentary.

2:44.pada_sa: भोगैश्वर्यप्रसक्तानां, तया, अपहृतचेतसां, व्यवसायात्मिका, बुद्धिः, समाधौ, न, विधीयते ॥ ४४ ॥
2:44.anvaya_sa: ते, कर्मणि, एव, अधिकारः, फलेषु, कदाचन, मा, कर्मफलहेतुः, मा, भूः, ते, अकर्मणि, सङ्गः, मा अस्तु ॥ ४७ ॥
2:44.pada_iast: bhogaiśvaryaprasaktānāṃ, tayā, apahṛtacetasāṃ, vyavasāyātmikā, buddhiḥ, samādhau, na, vidhīyate || 44 ||
2:44.anvaya_iast: te, karmaṇi, eva, adhikāraḥ, phaleṣu, kadācana, mā, karmaphalahetuḥ, mā, bhūḥ, te, akarmaṇi, saṅgaḥ, mā astu || 47 ||
2:44.translation: One-pointed conviction does not become established in the minds of those who delight in enjoyment and affluence, and whose intellects are carried away by that (speech).
2:44.explanation: Those who cling to pleasure and power cannot have steadiness of mind. They cannot concentrate or meditate. They are ever busy in planning projects for the acisition of wealth and power. Their minds are ever restless. They have no poised understanding.
2:44.word_meanings: भोगैश्वर्यप्रसक्तानाम् — of the people deeply attached to pleasure and lordship; तया — by that; अपहृतचेतसाम् — whose minds are drawn away; व्यवसायात्मिका — determinate; बुद्धिः — reason; समाधौ — in Samadhi; न — not; विधीयते — is fixed.

2:45.pada_sa: त्रैगुण्यविषयाः, वेदाः, निस्त्रैगुण्यः, भव, अर्जुन, निर्द्वन्द्वः, नित्यसत्त्वस्थः, निर्योगक्षेमः, आत्मवान्  ॥ ४५ ॥
2:45.anvaya_sa: धनञ्जय, सङ्गं, त्यक्त्वा, सिद्ध्यसिद्ध्योः, समः, भूत्वा, योगस्थः, कर्माणि, कुरु, समत्वं, योगः, उच्यते ॥ ४८ ॥
2:45.pada_iast: traiguṇyaviṣayāḥ, vedāḥ, nistraiguṇyaḥ, bhava, arjuna, nirdvandvaḥ, nityasattvasthaḥ, niryogakṣemaḥ, ātmavān  || 45 ||
2:45.anvaya_iast: dhanañjaya, saṅgaṃ, tyaktvā, siddhyasiddhyoḥ, samaḥ, bhūtvā, yogasthaḥ, karmāṇi, kuru, samatvaṃ, yogaḥ, ucyate || 48 ||
2:45.translation: O Arjuna, the Vedas [Meaning only the portion dealing with rites and duties (karma-kanda).] have the three alities as their object. You become free from worldliness, free from the pairs of duality, ever-poised in the ality of sattva, without (desire for) acisition and protection, and self-collected.
2:45.explanation: Guna means attribute or ality. It is substance as well as ality. Nature (Prakriti) is made up of three Gunas? viz.? Sattva (purity? light or harmony)? Rajas (passion or motion) and Tamas (darkness or inertia). The pairs of opposites are heat and cold? pleasure and pain? gain and loss? victory and defeat? honour and dishonour? praise and censure. He who is anxious about new acuqisitions or about the preservation of his old possessions cannot have peace of mind. He is ever restless. He cannot concentrate or meditate on the Self. He cannot practise virtue. Therefore? Lord Krishna advises Arjuna that he should be free from the thought of acisition and preservation of things. (Cf.IX.20?21).
2:45.word_meanings: त्रैगुण्यविषयाः — deal with the three attributes; वेदाः — the Vedas; निस्त्रैगुण्यः — without these three attributes; भव — be; अर्जुन — O Arjuna निर्द्वन्द्वः free from the pairs of opposites; नित्यसत्त्वस्थः — ever remaining in the Sattva (goodness); निर्योगक्षेमः — free from (the thought of) acisition and preservation; आत्मवान् — established in the Self.

2:46.pada_sa: यावान्, अर्थः, उदपाने, सर्वतः, सम्प्लुतोदके, तावान्, सर्वेषु, वेदेषु, ब्राह्मणस्य, विजानतः ॥ ४६ ॥
2:46.anvaya_sa: बुद्धियोगात्, कर्म, दूरेण, अवरं, (अतः) धनञ्जय, बुद्धौ, शरणम्, अन्विच्छ, हि, फलहेतवः, कृपणाः ॥ ४९ ॥
2:46.pada_iast: yāvān, arthaḥ, udapāne, sarvataḥ, samplutodake, tāvān, sarveṣu, vedeṣu, brāhmaṇasya, vijānataḥ || 46 ||
2:46.anvaya_iast: buddhiyogāt, karma, dūreṇa, avaraṃ, (ataḥ) dhanañjaya, buddhau, śaraṇam, anviccha, hi, phalahetavaḥ, kṛpaṇāḥ || 49 ||
2:46.translation: A Brahmana with realization has that much utility in all the Vedas as a man has in a well when there is a flood all around.
2:46.explanation: Only for a sage who has realised the Self? the Vedas are of no use? because he is in possession of the infinite knowledge of the Self. This does not? however? mean that the Vedas are useless. They are useful for the neophytes or the aspirants who have just started on the spiritual path.All the transient pleasures derivable from the proper performance of all actions enjoined in the Vedas are comprehended in the infinite bliss of Selfknowledge.
2:46.word_meanings: यावान् — as much; अर्थः — use; उदपाने — in a reservoir; सर्वतः — everywhere; संप्लुतोदके — being flooded; तावान्,so — much (use); सर्वेषु — in all; वेदेषु — in the Vedas; ब्राह्मणस्य — of the Brahmana; विजानतः — of the knowing.

iast: mā karma-phala-hetur bhūr mā te saṅgo ’stvakarmaṇi

2:47.pada_sa: कर्मणि, एव, अधिकारः, ते, मा, फलेषु, कदाचन, मा, कर्मफलहेतुः, भूः, मा, ते, सङ्गः, अस्तु, अकर्मणि ॥ ४७ ॥
2:47.anvaya_sa: बुद्धियुक्तः, सुकृतदुष्कृते, उभे, इह, जहाति, तस्मात्, योगाय, युज्यस्व, योगः, कर्मसु, कौशलम् ॥ ५० ॥
2:47.pada_iast: karmaṇi, eva, adhikāraḥ, te, mā, phaleṣu, kadācana, mā, karmaphalahetuḥ, bhūḥ, mā, te, saṅgaḥ, astu, akarmaṇi || 47 ||
2:47.anvaya_iast: buddhiyuktaḥ, sukṛtaduṣkṛte, ubhe, iha, jahāti, tasmāt, yogāya, yujyasva, yogaḥ, karmasu, kauśalam || 50 ||
2:47.translation: You have a right to perform your duty, but never to the fruits of your actions. Do not consider yourself the cause of the results, and never be attached to inaction.
2:47.explanation: This is arguably the most famous verse of the Gita. Four instructions: (1) your right is to work only; (2) never to the results; (3) don't think you cause results; (4) don't use this as an excuse for inaction. Modern psychology calls this "process focus" vs "outcome focus."
2:47.word_meanings: karmaṇi — in action; eva — only; adhikāraḥ — right; te — your; mā — not; phaleṣhu — in the results; kadāchana — ever; mā — not; karma-phala — result of action; hetuḥ — cause; bhūḥ — be; mā — not; te — your; saṅgaḥ — attachment; astu — be; akarmaṇi — in inaction

sa: योगस्थः कुरु कर्माणि सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा धनञ्जय
सिद्ध्यसिद्ध्योः समो भूत्वा समत्वं योग उच्यते
iast: yoga-sthaḥ kuru karmāṇi saṅgaṁ tyaktvā dhanañjaya
siddhy-asiddhyoḥ samo bhūtvā samatvaṁ yoga uchyate

2:48.pada_sa: योगस्थः, कुरु, कर्माणि, सङ्गं, त्यक्त्वा, धनञ्जय, सिद्ध्यसिद्ध्योः, समः, भूत्वा, समत्वं, योगः, उच्यते ॥ ४८ ॥
2:48.anvaya_sa: हि, बुद्धियुक्ताः, मनीषिणः, कर्मजं, फलं, त्यक्त्वा, जन्मबन्धविनिर्मुक्ताः, अनामयं, पदं, गच्छन्ति ॥ ५१ ॥
2:48.pada_iast: yogasthaḥ, kuru, karmāṇi, saṅgaṃ, tyaktvā, dhanañjaya, siddhyasiddhyoḥ, samaḥ, bhūtvā, samatvaṃ, yogaḥ, ucyate || 48 ||
2:48.anvaya_iast: hi, buddhiyuktāḥ, manīṣiṇaḥ, karmajaṃ, phalaṃ, tyaktvā, janmabandhavinirmuktāḥ, anāmayaṃ, padaṃ, gacchanti || 51 ||
2:48.translation: By being established in Yoga, O Dhananjaya (Arjuna), undertake actions, casting off attachment and remaining eipoised in success and failure. Eanimity is called Yoga.
2:48.explanation: Dwelling in union with the Divine perform actions merely for Gods sake with a balanced mind in success and failure. Eilibrium is Yoga. The attainment of the knowledge of the Self through purity of heart obtained by doing actions without expectation of fruits is success (Siddhi). Failure is the nonattainment of knowledge by doing actions with expectation of fruit. (Cf.III.9IV.14IV.20).
2:48.word_meanings: योगस्थः — steadfast in Yoga; कुरु — perform; कर्माणि — actions; सङ्गम् — attachment; त्यक्त्वा — having abandoned; धनञ्जय — O Dhananjaya; सिद्ध्यसिद्ध्योः — in success and failure; समः — the smae; भूत्वा — having become; समत्वम् — evenness of mind; योगः — Yoga; उच्यते — is called.

2:49.pada_sa: दूरेण, हि, अवरं, कर्म, बुद्धियोगात्, धनञ्जय, बुद्धौ, शरणम्, अन्विच्छ, कृपणाः, फलहेतवः ॥ ४९ ॥
2:49.anvaya_sa: यदा, ते, बुद्धिः, मोहकलितं, व्यतितरिष्यति, तदा, श्रोतव्यस्य, च, श्रुतस्य, निर्वेदं, गन्तासि ॥ ५२ ॥
2:49.pada_iast: dūreṇa, hi, avaraṃ, karma, buddhiyogāt, dhanañjaya, buddhau, śaraṇam, anviccha, kṛpaṇāḥ, phalahetavaḥ || 49 ||
2:49.anvaya_iast: yadā, te, buddhiḥ, mohakalitaṃ, vyatitariṣyati, tadā, śrotavyasya, ca, śrutasya, nirvedaṃ, gantāsi || 52 ||
2:49.translation: O Dhananjaya, indeed, action is ite inferior to the yoga of wisdom. Take resort to wisdom. Those who thirst for rewards are pitiable.
2:49.explanation: Action done with evenness of mind is Yoga of wisdom. The yogi who is established in the Yoga of widdom is not affected by success or failure. He does not seek fruits of his actions. He has poised reason. His reason is rooted in the Self. Action performed by one who expects fruits for his actions? is far inferior to the Yoga of wisdom wherein the seeker does not seek fruits because the former leads to bondage and is the cause of birth and death. (Cf.VIII.18).
2:49.word_meanings: दूरेण — by far; हि — indeed; अवरम् — inferior; कर्म — action or work; बुद्धियोगात् — than the Yoga of wisdom; धनञ्जय — O Dhananjaya; बुद्धौ — in wisdom; शरणम् — refuge; अन्विच्छ — seek; कृपणाः — wretched; फलहेतवः — seekers after fruits.

iast: tasmād yogāya yujyasva yogaḥ karmasu kauśhalam

2:50.pada_sa: बुद्धियुक्तः, जहाति, इह,  उभे, सुकृतदुष्कृते, तस्मात्, योगाय, युज्यस्व, योगः, कर्मसु, कौशलम् ॥ ५० ॥
2:50.anvaya_sa: यदा, ते, श्रुतिविप्रतिपन्ना, बुद्धिः, समाधौ, अचला, निश्चला, स्थास्यति, तदा, योगम्, अवाप्स्यसि ॥ ५३ ॥
2:50.pada_iast: buddhiyuktaḥ, jahāti, iha,  ubhe, sukṛtaduṣkṛte, tasmāt, yogāya, yujyasva, yogaḥ, karmasu, kauśalam || 50 ||
2:50.anvaya_iast: yadā, te, śrutivipratipannā, buddhiḥ, samādhau, acalā, niścalā, sthāsyati, tadā, yogam, avāpsyasi || 53 ||
2:50.translation: Possessed of wisdom, one rejects here both virtue and vice. Therefore devote yourself to (Karma-) yoga. Yoga is skilfulness in action.
2:50.explanation: Work performed with motive towards fruits only can bind a man. It will bring the fruits and the performer of the action will have to take birth again in this mortal world to enjoy them. If work is performed with evennes of mind (the Yoga of wisdom? i.e.? united to pure Buddhi? intelligence or reason) with the mind resting in the Lord? it will not bind him it will not bring any fruit it is no work at all. Actions which are of a binding nature lose that nature when performed with eanimity of mind? or poised reason. The Yogi of poised reason attributes all actions to the Divine Actor within (Isvara or God).
2:50.word_meanings: बुद्धियुक्तः — endowed with wisdom; जहाति — casts off; इह — in this life; उभे — both; सुकृतदुष्कृते — good and evil deeds; तस्मात् — therefore; योगाय — to Yoga; युज्यस्व — devote thyself; योगः — Yoga; कर्मसु — in actions; कौशलम् — skill.

sa: कर्मजं बुद्धियुक्ता हि फलं त्यक्त्वा मनीषिणः
iast: karma-jaṁ buddhi-yuktā hi phalaṁ tyaktvā manīṣhiṇaḥ

2:51.pada_sa: कर्मजं, बुद्धियुक्तं, हि, फलं, त्यक्त्वा, मनीषिणः, जन्मबन्धविनिर्मुक्ताः, पदं, गच्छन्ति, अनामयम् ॥ ५१ ॥
2:51.anvaya_sa: केशव, समाधिस्थस्य, स्थितप्रज्ञस्य, का, भाषा, स्थितधीः, किं, प्रभाषेत, किम्, आसीत, किं, व्रजेत ॥ ५४ ॥
2:51.pada_iast: karmajaṃ, buddhiyuktaṃ, hi, phalaṃ, tyaktvā, manīṣiṇaḥ, janmabandhavinirmuktāḥ, padaṃ, gacchanti, anāmayam || 51 ||
2:51.anvaya_iast: keśava, samādhisthasya, sthitaprajñasya, kā, bhāṣā, sthitadhīḥ, kiṃ, prabhāṣeta, kim, āsīta, kiṃ, vrajeta || 54 ||
2:51.translation: Because, those who are devoted to wisdom, (they) becoming men of Enlightenment by giving up the fruits produced by actions, reach the state beyond evils by having become freed from the bondage of birth.
2:51.explanation: Clinging to the fruits of actions is the cause of rirth. Man takes a body to enjoy them. If anyone performs actions for the sake of God in fulfilment of His purpose without desire for the fruits? he is released from the bonds of birth and attains to the blissful state or the immortal abode.Sages who possess evenness of mind abandon the fruits of their actions and thus escape from good and bad actions.Buddhi referred to in the three verses 49? 50 and 51 may be the wisdom of the Sankhyas? i.e.? the knowledge of the Self or AtmaJnana which dawns when the mind is purified by Karma Yoga.
2:51.word_meanings: कर्मजम् — actionborn; बुद्धियुक्ताः — possessed of knowledsge; हि — indeed; फलम् — the fruit; त्यक्त्वा — having abandoned; मनीषिणः — the wise; जन्मबन्धविनिर्मुक्ताः — freed from the fetters of birth; पदम् — the abode; गच्छन्ति — go; अनामयम् — beyond evil.

sa: तदा गन्तासि निर्वेदं श्रोतव्यस्य श्रुतस्य च
iast: tadā gantāsi nirvedaṁ śhrotavyasya śhrutasya cha

2:52.pada_sa: यदा, ते, मोहकलिलं, बुद्धिः, व्यतितरिष्यति, तदा, गन्तासि, निर्वेदं, श्रोतव्यस्य, श्रुतस्य, च ॥ ५२ ॥
2:52.anvaya_sa: पार्थ, यदा, मनोगतान्, सर्वान्, कामान्, प्रजहाति, तदा, आत्मना, एव, आत्मनि, तुष्टः, स्थितप्रज्ञः, उच्यते ॥ ५५ ॥
2:52.pada_iast: yadā, te, mohakalilaṃ, buddhiḥ, vyatitariṣyati, tadā, gantāsi, nirvedaṃ, śrotavyasya, śrutasya, ca || 52 ||
2:52.anvaya_iast: pārtha, yadā, manogatān, sarvān, kāmān, prajahāti, tadā, ātmanā, eva, ātmani, tuṣṭaḥ, sthitaprajñaḥ, ucyate || 55 ||
2:52.translation: When your mind will go beyond the turbidity of delusion, then you will acire dispassion for what has to be heard and what has been heard.
2:52.explanation: The mire of delusion is the identification of the Self with the notself. The sense of discrimination between the Self and the notSelf is confounded by the mire of delusion and the mind runs towards the sensual objects and the body is takes as the pure Self. When you attain purity of mind? you will attain to indifference regarding things heard and yet to be heard. They will appear to you to be of no use. You will not care a bit for them. You will entertain disgust for them. (Cf.XVI.24).
2:52.word_meanings: यदा — when; ते — thy; मोहकलिलम् — mire of delusion; बुद्धिः — intellect; व्यतितरिष्यति — crosses beyond; तदा — then; गन्तासि — thou shalt attain; निर्वेदम् — to indifference; श्रोतव्यस्य — of what has to be heard; श्रुतस्य — what has been heard; च — and.

2:53.pada_sa: श्रुतिविप्रतिपन्नाः, ते, यदा, स्थास्यति, निश्चला, समाधौ, अचला, बुद्धिः, तदा, योगम्, अवाप्स्यसि ॥ ५३ ॥
2:53.anvaya_sa: दुःखेषु, अनुद्विग्नमनाः, सुखेषु, विगतस्पृहः, वीतरागभयक्रोधः, मुनिः, स्थितधीः, उच्यते ॥ ५६ ॥
2:53.pada_iast: śrutivipratipannāḥ, te, yadā, sthāsyati, niścalā, samādhau, acalā, buddhiḥ, tadā, yogam, avāpsyasi || 53 ||
2:53.anvaya_iast: duḥkheṣu, anudvignamanāḥ, sukheṣu, vigataspṛhaḥ, vītarāgabhayakrodhaḥ, muniḥ, sthitadhīḥ, ucyate || 56 ||
2:53.translation: When your mind that has become bewildered by hearing [S. takes the word sruti in the sense of the Vedas.-Tr.] will become unshakable and steadfast in the Self, then you will attain Yoga that arises from discrimination.
2:53.explanation: When your intellect which is tossed about by the conflict of opinions regarding the Pravritti Marga (the path of action) and the Nivritti Marga (the path of retirement or renunciation) has become immovable without distraction and doubt and firmly established in the Self? then thou shalt attain Selfrealisation or knowledge of the Self (AtmaJnana).
2:53.word_meanings: श्रुतिविप्रतिपन्ना — perplexed by what hast heard; ते — thy; यदा — when; स्थास्यति — shall stand; निश्चला — immovable; समाधौ — in the Self; अचला — steady; बुद्धिः — intellect; तदा — then; योगम् — Selfrealisation; अवाप्स्यसि (thou) — shalt attain.

sa: स्थितधीः किं प्रभाषेत किमासीत व्रजेत किम्
iast: sthita-dhīḥ kiṁ prabhāṣheta kim āsīta vrajeta kim

2:54.pada_sa: स्थितप्रज्ञस्य, का, भाषा, समाधिस्थस्य, केशव, स्थितधीः, किं, प्रभाषेत, किम्, आसीत, व्रजेत, किम् ॥ ५४ ॥
2:54.anvaya_sa: यः, सर्वत्र, अनभिस्नेहः, तत् तत्, शुभाशुभं, प्राप्य, न अभिनन्दति, न द्वेष्टि, तस्य, प्रज्ञा, प्रतिष्ठिता ॥ ५७ ॥
2:54.pada_iast: sthitaprajñasya, kā, bhāṣā, samādhisthasya, keśava, sthitadhīḥ, kiṃ, prabhāṣeta, kim, āsīta, vrajeta, kim || 54 ||
2:54.anvaya_iast: yaḥ, sarvatra, anabhisnehaḥ, tat tat, śubhāśubhaṃ, prāpya, na abhinandati, na dveṣṭi, tasya, prajñā, pratiṣṭhitā || 57 ||
2:54.translation: Arjuna said  O kesava, what is the description of a man of steady wisdom who is Self-absorbed? How does the man of steady wisdom speak? How does he sit? How does he move about?
2:54.explanation: Arjuna wants to know from Lord Krishna the characteristic marks of one who is established in the Self in Samadhi how he speaks? how he sits? how he moves about.The characteristic marks of the sage of steady wisdom and the means of attaining that steady knowledge of the Self are described in the verses from 55 to 72 of this chapter.Steady wisdom is settled knowledge of ones identity with Brahman attained by direct realisation. (Cf.XIV.21? 27).
2:54.word_meanings: स्थितप्रज्ञस्य — of the (sage of) steady wisdom; का — what; भाषा — description; समाधिस्थस्य — of the (man) merged in the superconscious state; केशव — O Kesava; स्थितधीः — the sage of steady wisdom; किम् — what (how); प्रभाषेत — speaks; किम् — what (how); आसीत — sits; व्रजेत — walks; किम् — what (how).

iast: prajahāti yadā kāmān sarvān pārtha mano-gatān

2:55.pada_sa: प्रजहाति, यदा, कामान्, सर्वान्, पार्थ, मनोगतान्, आत्मनि, एव, अत्मना, तुष्टः, स्थितप्रज्ञः, तदा, उच्यते ॥ ५५ ॥
2:55.anvaya_sa: च, कूर्मः, अङ्गानि, इव, अयं, यदा, सर्वशः, इन्द्रियाणि, इन्द्रियार्थेभ्यः, संहरते, तस्य, प्रज्ञा, प्रतिष्ठिता ॥ ५८ ॥
2:55.pada_iast: prajahāti, yadā, kāmān, sarvān, pārtha, manogatān, ātmani, eva, atmanā, tuṣṭaḥ, sthitaprajñaḥ, tadā, ucyate || 55 ||
2:55.anvaya_iast: ca, kūrmaḥ, aṅgāni, iva, ayaṃ, yadā, sarvaśaḥ, indriyāṇi, indriyārthebhyaḥ, saṃharate, tasya, prajñā, pratiṣṭhitā || 58 ||
2:55.translation: The Blessed said  O Partha, when one fully renounces all the desires that have entered the mind, and remains satisfied in the Self alone by the Self, then he is called a man of steady wisdom.
2:55.explanation: In this verse Lord Krishna gives His answer to the first part of Arjunas estion.If anyone gets sugarcandy will he crave for blacksugar Certainly not. If anyone can attain the supreme bliss of the Self? will he thirst for the sensual pleasures No? not at all. The sumtotal of all the pleasures of the world will seem worthless for the sage of steady wisdom who is satisfied in the Self. (Cf.III.17VI.7?8).
2:55.word_meanings: प्रजहाति — casts off; यदा — when; कामान् — desires; सर्वान् — all; पार्थ — O Partha; मनोगतान् — of the mind; आत्मनि — in the Self; एव — only; आत्मना — by the Self; तुष्टः — satisfied; स्थितप्रज्ञः — of steady wisdom; तदा — then; उच्यते (he) — is called.

2:56.pada_sa: दुःखेषु, अनुद्विग्नमनाः, सुखेषु, विगतस्पृहः, वीतरागभयक्रोधः, स्थितधीः, मुनिः, उच्यते ॥ ५६ ॥
2:56.anvaya_sa: निराहारस्य, देहिनः, विषयाः, विनिवर्तन्ते, रसवर्जम्, अस्य, रसः, अपि, परं, दृष्ट्वा, निवर्तते ॥ ५९ ॥
2:56.pada_iast: duḥkheṣu, anudvignamanāḥ, sukheṣu, vigataspṛhaḥ, vītarāgabhayakrodhaḥ, sthitadhīḥ, muniḥ, ucyate || 56 ||
2:56.anvaya_iast: nirāhārasya, dehinaḥ, viṣayāḥ, vinivartante, rasavarjam, asya, rasaḥ, api, paraṃ, dṛṣṭvā, nivartate || 59 ||
2:56.translation: That monk is called a man of steady wisdom when his mind is unperturbed in sorrow, he is free from longing for delights, and has gone beyond attachment, fear and anger.
2:56.explanation: Lord Krishna gives His answer to the second part of Arjunas estion as to the conduct of a sage of steady wisdom in the 56th? 57th and 58th verses.The mind of a sage of steady wisdom is not distressed in calamities. He is not affected by the three afflictions (Taapas) -- Adhyatmika (arising from diseases or disorders in ones own body)? Adhidaivika (arising from thunder? lightning? storm? flood? etc.)? and Adhibhautika (arising from scorpions? cobras? tigers? etc.). When he is placed in an affluent condition he does not long for sensual pleasures. (Cf.IV.10).
2:56.word_meanings: दुःखेषु — in adversity; अनुद्विग्नमनाः — of unshaken mind; सुखेषु — in pleasure; विगतस्पृहः — withut hankering; वीतरागभयक्रोधः — free from attachment; fear — and anger; स्थितधीः — of steady wisdom; मुनिः — sage; उच्यते (he) — is called.

sa: नाभिनन्दति न द्वेष्टि तस्य प्रज्ञा प्रतिष्ठिता
iast: yaḥ sarvatrānabhisnehas tat tat prāpya śhubhāśhubham
nābhinandati na dveṣhṭi tasya prajñā pratiṣhṭhitā

2:57.pada_sa: यः, सर्वत्र, अनभिस्नेहः, तत्, तत्, प्राप्य, शुभाशुभं, न, अभिनन्दति, न, द्वेष्टि, तस्य, प्रज्ञा, पतिष्टिता ॥ ५७ ॥
2:57.anvaya_sa: कौन्तेय, हि, यततः, विपश्चितः, पुरुषस्य, अपि, मनः, प्रमाथीनि, इन्द्रियाणि, प्रसभं, हरन्ति ॥ ६० ॥
2:57.pada_iast: yaḥ, sarvatra, anabhisnehaḥ, tat, tat, prāpya, śubhāśubhaṃ, na, abhinandati, na, dveṣṭi, tasya, prajñā, patiṣṭitā || 57 ||
2:57.anvaya_iast: kaunteya, hi, yatataḥ, vipaścitaḥ, puruṣasya, api, manaḥ, pramāthīni, indriyāṇi, prasabhaṃ, haranti || 60 ||
2:57.translation: The wisdom of that person remains established who has not attachment for anything anywhere, who neither welcomes nor rejects anything whatever good or bad when he comes across it.
2:57.explanation: The sage possesses poised understanding or evenness of mind. He does not rejoice in pleasure nor is he averse to pain that may befall him. He is ite indifferent as he is rooted in the Self. He has no attachment even for his life or body as he identifies himself with Brahman or the Supreme Self. He will not praise anybody when the latter does any good to him nor censure anyone when one does him any harm. This is the answer given by the Lord to Arjunas ery How does a sage of steady wisdom talk
2:57.word_meanings: यः — he who; सर्वत्र — everywhere; अनभिस्नेहः — without attachment; तत् — that; तत् — that; प्राप्य — having obtained; शुभाशुभम् — good and evil; न — not; अभिनन्दति — rejoices; न — not; द्वेष्टि — hates; तस्य — of him; प्रज्ञा — wisdom; प्रतिष्ठिता — is fixed.

2:58.pada_sa: यदा, संहरते, च, अयं, कूर्मः, अङ्गानि, इव, सर्वशः, इन्द्रियाणि, इन्द्रियार्थेभ्यः, तस्य, प्रज्ञा, प्रतिष्टिता ॥ ५८ ॥
2:58.anvaya_sa: तानि, सर्वाणि, संयम्य, युक्तः, मत्परः, आसीत, हि, यस्य, इन्द्रियाणि, वशे, तस्य, प्रज्ञा, प्रतिष्ठिता ॥ ६१ ॥
2:58.pada_iast: yadā, saṃharate, ca, ayaṃ, kūrmaḥ, aṅgāni, iva, sarvaśaḥ, indriyāṇi, indriyārthebhyaḥ, tasya, prajñā, pratiṣṭitā || 58 ||
2:58.anvaya_iast: tāni, sarvāṇi, saṃyamya, yuktaḥ, matparaḥ, āsīta, hi, yasya, indriyāṇi, vaśe, tasya, prajñā, pratiṣṭhitā || 61 ||
2:58.translation: And when this one fully withdraws the senses from the objects of the senses, as a tortoise wholly (withdraws) the limbs, then his wisdom remains established.
2:58.explanation: Withdrawal of the senses is Pratyahara or abstraction. The mind has a natural,tendency to run towards external objects. The Yogi again and again withdraws the mind from the objects of the senses and fixes it on the Self. A Yogi who is endowed with the power of Pratyahara can enter into Samadhi even in a crowded place by withdrawing his senses within the twinkling of an eye. He is not disturbed by tumultuous sounds and noises of any description. Even on the battlefield he can rest in his centre? the Self? by withdrawing his senses. He who practises Pratyahara is dead to the world. He will not be affected by the outside vibrations. At any time by mere willing he can bring his senses under his perfect control. They are his obedient servants or instruments.
2:58.word_meanings: यदा — when; संहरते — withdraws; च — and; अयम् — this (Yogi); कूर्मः — tortoise; अङ्गानि — limbs; इव — like; सर्वशः — everywhere; इन्द्रियाणि — the senses; इन्द्रियार्थेभ्यः — from the senseobjects; तस्य — of him; प्रज्ञा — wisdom प्रतिष्ठिता is steadied.

2:59.pada_sa: विषयाः, विनिवर्तन्ते, निराहारस्य, देहिनः, रसवर्जं, रसः, अपि, अस्य, परं, दृष्ट्वा, निवर्तते ॥ ५९ ॥
2:59.anvaya_sa: विषयान्, ध्यायतः, पुंसः, तेषु, सङ्गः, उपजायते, सङ्गात्, कामः, सञ्जायते, कामात्, क्रोधः, अभिजायते ॥ ६२ ॥
2:59.pada_iast: viṣayāḥ, vinivartante, nirāhārasya, dehinaḥ, rasavarjaṃ, rasaḥ, api, asya, paraṃ, dṛṣṭvā, nivartate || 59 ||
2:59.anvaya_iast: viṣayān, dhyāyataḥ, puṃsaḥ, teṣu, saṅgaḥ, upajāyate, saṅgāt, kāmaḥ, sañjāyate, kāmāt, krodhaḥ, abhijāyate || 62 ||
2:59.translation: The objects recede from an abstinent man, with the exception of the taste (for them). Even the taste of this person falls away after realization the Absolute.
2:59.explanation: Knowledge of the Self alone can destroy in toto the subtle Vasanas (latent tendencies) and all the subtle desires? all subtle attachments and even the longing for objects. By practising severe austerities? by abandoning the sensual objects? the objects of the senses may turn away from the ascetic but the relish or taste or longing for the objects will still remain.
2:59.word_meanings: विषयाः — the objects of senses; विनिवर्तन्ते — turn away; निराहारस्य — abstinent; देहिनः — of the man; रसवर्जम् — leaving the longing; रसः — loving (taste); अपि — even; अस्य — of his; परम् — the Supreme; दृष्ट्वा — having seen; निवर्तते — turns away.

2:60.pada_sa: यततः, हि, अपि, कौन्तेय, पुरुषस्य, विपश्चितः, इन्द्रियाणि, प्रमाथीनि, हरन्ति, प्रसभं, मनः ॥ ६० ॥
2:60.anvaya_sa: क्रोधात्, संमोहः, भवति, संमोहात्, स्मृतिविभ्रमः, स्मृतिभ्रंशात्, बुद्धिनाशः, बुद्धिनाशात्, प्रणश्यति ॥ ६३ ॥
2:60.pada_iast: yatataḥ, hi, api, kaunteya, puruṣasya, vipaścitaḥ, indriyāṇi, pramāthīni, haranti, prasabhaṃ, manaḥ || 60 ||
2:60.anvaya_iast: krodhāt, saṃmohaḥ, bhavati, saṃmohāt, smṛtivibhramaḥ, smṛtibhraṃśāt, buddhināśaḥ, buddhināśāt, praṇaśyati || 63 ||
2:60.translation: For, O son of Kunti, the turbulent organs violently snatch away the mind of an intelligent person, even while he is striving diligently.
2:60.explanation: The aspirant should first bring the senses under his control. The senses are like horses. If you keep the horses under your perfect control you can reach your destinaton safely. Turbulent horses will throw you down on the way. Even so the turbulent senses will hurl you down into the objects of the senses and you cannot reach your spiritual destination? viz.? Param Dhama (the supreme abode) or the abode of eternal peace and immortality or Moksha (final liberation). (Cf.III.33V.14).
2:60.word_meanings: यततः — of the striving; हि — indeed; अपि — even; कौन्तेय — O Kaunteya (son of Kunti); पुरुषस्य — of man; विपश्चितः (of — the) wise; इन्द्रियाणि — the senses; प्रमाथीनि — turbulent; हरन्ति — carry away; प्रसभम् — violently; मनः — the mind.

sa: तानि सर्वाणि संयम्य युक्त आसीत मत्परः
वशे हि यस्येन्द्रियाणि तस्य प्रज्ञा प्रतिष्ठिता
iast: tāni sarvāṇi sanyamya yukta āsīta mat-paraḥ
vaśhe hi yasyendriyāṇi tasya prajñā pratiṣhṭhitā

2:61.pada_sa: तानि, सर्वाणि, संयम्य, युक्तः, आसीत, मत्परः, वशे, हि, यस्य, इन्द्रियाणि, तस्य, प्रज्ञा, प्रतिष्ठिता ॥ ६१ ॥
2:61.anvaya_sa: तु, विधेयात्मा, रागद्वेषवियुक्तैः, आत्मवश्यैः, इन्द्रियैः, विषयान्, चरन्, प्रसादम्, अधिगच्छति ॥ ६४ ॥
2:61.pada_iast: tāni, sarvāṇi, saṃyamya, yuktaḥ, āsīta, matparaḥ, vaśe, hi, yasya, indriyāṇi, tasya, prajñā, pratiṣṭhitā || 61 ||
2:61.anvaya_iast: tu, vidheyātmā, rāgadveṣaviyuktaiḥ, ātmavaśyaiḥ, indriyaiḥ, viṣayān, caran, prasādam, adhigacchati || 64 ||
2:61.translation: Controlling all of them, one should remain concentrated on Me as the supreme. For, the wisdom of one whose organs are under control becomes steadfast.
2:61.explanation: He should control the senses and sit focussed on Me as the Supreme? with a calm mind. The wisdom of the Yogi who thus seated has brought all his senses under subjugation is doubtless ite steady. He is established in the Self. Sri Sankaracharya explains Asita Matparah as He should sit contemplating I am no other than He. (Cf.II.64).
2:61.word_meanings: तानि — them; सर्वाणि — all; संयम्य — having restrained; युक्तः — joined; आसीत — should sit; मत्परः — intent on Me; वशे — under control; हि — indeed; यस्य — whose; इन्द्रियाणि — senses; तस्य — his; प्रज्ञा — wisdom; प्रतिष्ठिता — is settled.

2:62.pada_sa: ध्यायतः, विषयान्, पुंसः, सङ्गः, तेषु, उपजायते, सङ्गात्, सञ्जायते, कामः, कामात्, क्रोधः, अभिजायते ॥ ६२ ॥
2:62.anvaya_sa: प्रसादे, अस्य, सर्वदुःखानां, हानिः, उपजायते, प्रसन्नचेतसः, बुद्धिः, आशु, हि, पर्यवतिष्ठते ॥ ६५ ॥
2:62.pada_iast: dhyāyataḥ, viṣayān, puṃsaḥ, saṅgaḥ, teṣu, upajāyate, saṅgāt, sañjāyate, kāmaḥ, kāmāt, krodhaḥ, abhijāyate || 62 ||
2:62.anvaya_iast: prasāde, asya, sarvaduḥkhānāṃ, hāniḥ, upajāyate, prasannacetasaḥ, buddhiḥ, āśu, hi, paryavatiṣṭhate || 65 ||
2:62.translation: When a person dwells on sense objects, attachment to them arises. From attachment comes desire, and from unfulfilled desire comes anger.
2:62.explanation: Krishna maps the psychology of downfall as a chain reaction: contemplation → attachment → desire → anger. This is remarkably modern — cognitive behavioral therapy describes similar "thought chains." The chain continues in the next verse: anger → delusion → memory loss → loss of intelligence → destruction.
2:62.word_meanings: dhyāyataḥ — contemplating; viṣhayān — sense objects; puṁsaḥ — of a person; saṅgaḥ — attachment; teṣhu — to them; upajāyate — arises; saṅgāt — from attachment; sañjāyate — develops; kāmaḥ — desire; kāmāt — from desire; krodhaḥ — anger; abhijāyate — arises

2:63.pada_sa: क्रोधात्, भवति, संमोहः, संमोहात्, स्मृतिविभ्रमः, स्मृतिभ्रंशात्, बुद्धिनाशः, बुद्धिनाशात्, प्रणश्यति ॥ ६३ ॥
2:63.anvaya_sa: अयुक्तस्य, बुद्धिः, न अस्ति, च, अयुक्तस्य, भावना, न, अभावयतः, शान्तिः, च, न, अशान्तस्य, सुखं, कुतः ॥ ६६ ॥
2:63.pada_iast: krodhāt, bhavati, saṃmohaḥ, saṃmohāt, smṛtivibhramaḥ, smṛtibhraṃśāt, buddhināśaḥ, buddhināśāt, praṇaśyati || 63 ||
2:63.anvaya_iast: ayuktasya, buddhiḥ, na asti, ca, ayuktasya, bhāvanā, na, abhāvayataḥ, śāntiḥ, ca, na, aśāntasya, sukhaṃ, kutaḥ || 66 ||
2:63.translation: From anger follows delusion; from delusion, failure of memory; from failure of memory, the loss of understanding; from the loss of understanding, he perishes.
2:63.explanation: From anger arises delusion. When a man becomes angry he loses his power of discrimination between right and wrong. He will speak and do anything he likes. He will be swept away by the impulse of passion and emotion and will act irrationally.
2:63.word_meanings: क्रोधात् — from anger; भवति — comes; संमोहः — delusion; संमोहात् — from delusion; स्मृतिविभ्रमः — loss of memory; स्मृतिभ्रंशात् — from loss of memory; बुद्धिनाशः — the destruction of discriminatio; बुद्धिनाशात् — from the,destruction of discrimination; प्रणश्यति (he) — perishes.

2:64.pada_sa: रागद्वेषवियुक्तैः, तु, विषयान्, इन्द्रियैः, चरन्, आत्मवश्यैः, विधेयात्मा, प्रसादम्, अधिगच्छति ॥ ६४ ॥
2:64.anvaya_sa: हि, अम्भसि, वायुः, नावम्, इव, चरताम्, इन्द्रियाणां, यत्, मनः, अनुविधीयते, तत्, अस्य, प्रज्ञां, हरति ॥ ६७ ॥
2:64.pada_iast: rāgadveṣaviyuktaiḥ, tu, viṣayān, indriyaiḥ, caran, ātmavaśyaiḥ, vidheyātmā, prasādam, adhigacchati || 64 ||
2:64.anvaya_iast: hi, ambhasi, vāyuḥ, nāvam, iva, caratām, indriyāṇāṃ, yat, manaḥ, anuvidhīyate, tat, asya, prajñāṃ, harati || 67 ||
2:64.translation: But by perceiving objects with the organs that are free from attraction and repulsion, and are under his own control, the self-controlled man attains serenity.
2:64.explanation: The mind and the senses are naturally endowed with the two currents of attraction and repulsion. Therefore? the mind and the senses like certain objects and dislike certain other objects. But the disciplined man moves among senseobjects with the mind and the senses free from attraction and repulsion and mastered by the Self? attains to the peace of the Eternal. The senses and the mind obey his will? as the disciplined self has a very strong will. The disciplined self takes only those objects which are ite necessary for the maintenance of the body without any love or hatred. He never takes those objects which are forbidden by the scriptures.In this verse Lord Krishna gives the answer to Arjunas fourth estion? How does a sage of steady wisdom move about (Cf.III.7.19?25XVIII.9).
2:64.word_meanings: रागद्वेषवियुक्तैः — free from attraction and repulsion; तु — but; विषयान् — objects; इन्द्रियैः — with senses; चरन् — moving (amongst); आत्मवश्यैः — selfrestrained; विधेयात्मा — the selfcontrolled; प्रसादम् — to peace; अधिगच्छति — attains.

2:65.pada_sa: प्रसादे, सर्वदुःखानां, हानिः, अस्य, उपजायते, प्रसन्नचेतसः, हि, अशु, बुद्धिः, पर्यवतिष्ठते ॥ ६५ ॥
2:65.anvaya_sa: तस्मात्, महाबाहो, यस्य, इन्द्रियाणि, सर्वशः, इन्द्रियार्थेभ्यः, निगृहीतानि, तस्य, प्रज्ञा, प्रतिष्ठिता ॥ ६८ ॥
2:65.pada_iast: prasāde, sarvaduḥkhānāṃ, hāniḥ, asya, upajāyate, prasannacetasaḥ, hi, aśu, buddhiḥ, paryavatiṣṭhate || 65 ||
2:65.anvaya_iast: tasmāt, mahābāho, yasya, indriyāṇi, sarvaśaḥ, indriyārthebhyaḥ, nigṛhītāni, tasya, prajñā, pratiṣṭhitā || 68 ||
2:65.translation: When there is serenity, there follows eradication of all his sorrows, because the wisdom of one who has a serene mind soon becomes firmly established.
2:65.explanation: When the mental peace is attained? there is no hankering after senseobjects. The Yogi has perfect mastery over his reason. The intellect abides in the Self. It is ite steady. The miseries of the body and the mind come to an end.
2:65.word_meanings: प्रसादे — in peace; सर्वदुःखानाम् (of) — all pains; हानिः — destruction; अस्य — of him; उपजायते — arises (or happens); प्रसन्नचेतसः — of the tranilminded; हि — because; आशु — soon; बुद्धिः — intellect (or reason); पर्यवतिष्ठते — becomes steady.

iast: na chābhāvayataḥ śhāntir aśhāntasya kutaḥ sukham

2:66.pada_sa: न, अस्ति, बुद्धिः, अयुक्तस्य, न, च, अयुक्तस्य, भावना, न, च, अभावयतः, शान्तिः, अशान्तस्य, कुतः, सुखम् ॥ ६६ ॥
2:66.anvaya_sa: सर्वभूतानां, या, निशा, तस्यां, संयमी, जागर्ति, यस्यां, भूतानि, जाग्रति, पश्यतः, मुनेः, सा, निषा ॥ ६९ ॥
2:66.pada_iast: na, asti, buddhiḥ, ayuktasya, na, ca, ayuktasya, bhāvanā, na, ca, abhāvayataḥ, śāntiḥ, aśāntasya, kutaḥ, sukham || 66 ||
2:66.anvaya_iast: sarvabhūtānāṃ, yā, niśā, tasyāṃ, saṃyamī, jāgarti, yasyāṃ, bhūtāni, jāgrati, paśyataḥ, muneḥ, sā, niṣā || 69 ||
2:66.translation: For the unsteady there is no wisdom, and there is no meditation for the unsteady man. And for an unmeditative man there is no peace. How can there be happiness for one without peace?
2:66.explanation: The man who cannot fix his mind in meditation cannot have knowledge of the Self. The unsteady man cannot practise meditation. He cannot have even intense devotion to Selfknowledge nor can he have burning longing for liberation or Moksha. He who does not practise meditation cannot possess peace of mind. How can the man who has no peace of mind enjoy happinessDesire or Trishna (thirsting for senseobjects) is the enemy of peace. There cannot be an iota or tinge of happiness for a man who is thirsting for sensual objects. The mind will be ever restless? and will be hankering for the objects. Only when this thirsting dies? does man enjoy peace. Only then can he meditate and rest in the Self.
2:66.word_meanings: न — not; अस्ति — is; बुद्धिः — knowledge (of the Self); अयुक्तस्य — of the unsteady; न — not; च — and; अयुक्तस्य — of the unsteady; भावना — meditation; न — not; च — and; अभावयतः — of the unmeditated; शान्तिः — peace; अशान्तस्य — of the peaceless; कुतः — whence; सुखम् — happiness.

iast: tadasya harati prajñāṁ vāyur nāvam ivāmbhasi

2:67.pada_sa: इन्द्रियाणां, हि, चरतां, यत्, मनः, अनुविधीयते, तत्, अस्य, हरति, प्रज्ञां, वायुः, नावम्, इव, अम्भसि ॥ ६७ ॥
2:67.anvaya_sa: यद्वत्, आपूर्यमाणम्, अचलप्रतिष्ठं, समुद्रम्, आपः, प्रविशन्ति, तद्वत्, यं, सर्वे, कामाः, प्रविशन्ति, सः, शान्तिम्, आप्नोति, न कामकामी ॥ ७० ॥
2:67.pada_iast: indriyāṇāṃ, hi, caratāṃ, yat, manaḥ, anuvidhīyate, tat, asya, harati, prajñāṃ, vāyuḥ, nāvam, iva, ambhasi || 67 ||
2:67.anvaya_iast: yadvat, āpūryamāṇam, acalapratiṣṭhaṃ, samudram, āpaḥ, praviśanti, tadvat, yaṃ, sarve, kāmāḥ, praviśanti, saḥ, śāntim, āpnoti, na kāmakāmī || 70 ||
2:67.translation: For, the mind which follows in the wake of the wandering senses, that (mind) carries away his wisdom like the mind (diverting) a boat on the waters.
2:67.explanation: The mind which constantly dwells on the sensual objects and moves in company with the senses destroys altogether the discrimination of the man. Just as the wind carries away a boat from its course? so also the mind carries away the aspirant from his spiritual path and turns,him towards the objects of the senses.
2:67.word_meanings: इन्द्रियाणाम् — senses; हि — for; चरताम् — wandering; यत् — which; मनः — mind; अनुविधीयते — follows; तत् — that; अस्य — his; हरति — carries away; प्रज्ञाम् — discrimination; वायुः — the wind; नावम् — boat; इव — like; अम्भसि — in the water.

2:68.pada_sa: तस्मात्, यस्य, महाबाहो, निगृहीतानि, सर्वशः, इन्द्रियाणि, इन्द्रियार्थेभ्यः, तस्य, प्रज्ञा, प्रतिष्ठिता ॥ ६८ ॥
2:68.anvaya_sa: यः, पुमान्, सर्वान्, कामान्, विहाय, निर्ममः, निरहङ्कारः, निःस्पृहः, चरति, सः, शान्तिम्, अधिगच्छति ॥ ७१ ॥
2:68.pada_iast: tasmāt, yasya, mahābāho, nigṛhītāni, sarvaśaḥ, indriyāṇi, indriyārthebhyaḥ, tasya, prajñā, pratiṣṭhitā || 68 ||
2:68.anvaya_iast: yaḥ, pumān, sarvān, kāmān, vihāya, nirmamaḥ, nirahaṅkāraḥ, niḥspṛhaḥ, carati, saḥ, śāntim, adhigacchati || 71 ||
2:68.translation: Therefore, O mighty-armed one, this wisdom becomes established whose organs in all their varieties are withdrawn from their objects.
2:68.explanation: When the senses are completely controlled? the mind cannot wander wildly in the sensual grooves. It becomes steady like the lamp in a windless place. The Yogi is now established in the Self and his knowledge is steady. (Cf.III.7).
2:68.word_meanings: तस्मात् — therefore; यस्य — whose; महाबाहो — O mightyarmed; निगृहीतानि — restrained; सर्वशः — completely; इन्द्रियाणि — the senses; इन्द्रियार्थेभ्यः — from the senseobjects; तस्य — his; प्रज्ञा — knowledge; प्रतिष्ठिता — is steady.

sa: या निशा सर्वभूतानां तस्यां जागर्ति संयमी
यस्यां जाग्रति भूतानि सा निशा पश्यतो मुनेः
iast: yā niśhā sarva-bhūtānāṁ tasyāṁ jāgarti sanyamī
yasyāṁ jāgrati bhūtāni sā niśhā paśhyato muneḥ

2:69.pada_sa: या, निशा, सर्वभूतानां, तस्यां, जागर्ति, संयमी, यस्यां, जाग्रति, भूतानि, सा, निशा, पश्यतः, मुनेः ॥ ६९ ॥
2:69.anvaya_sa: पार्थ, एषा, ब्राह्मी, स्थितिः, एनां, प्राप्य, न विमुह्यति, अन्तकाले, अपि, अस्यां, स्थित्वा, ब्रह्मनिर्वाणम्, ऋच्चति ॥ ७२ ॥
2:69.pada_iast: yā, niśā, sarvabhūtānāṃ, tasyāṃ, jāgarti, saṃyamī, yasyāṃ, jāgrati, bhūtāni, sā, niśā, paśyataḥ, muneḥ || 69 ||
2:69.anvaya_iast: pārtha, eṣā, brāhmī, sthitiḥ, enāṃ, prāpya, na vimuhyati, antakāle, api, asyāṃ, sthitvā, brahmanirvāṇam, ṛccati || 72 ||
2:69.translation: The self-restrained man keeps awake during that which is night for all creatures. That during which creatures keep awake, it is night to the seeing sage.
2:69.explanation: That which is real for the wordlyminded people is illusion for the sage? and vice versa. The sage lives in the Self. This is day for him. He is unconscious of the wordly phenomena. They are night for him? as it were. The ordinary man is unconscious of his real nature. Life in the spirit is night for him. He is experiencing the objects of sensual enjoyment. This is day for him. The Self is a nonentity for him For a sage this world is a nonentity.The wordlyminded people are in utter darkness as they have no knowledge of the Self. What is darkness for them is all light for the sage. The Self? Atman or Brahman is night for the worldlyminded persons. But the sage is fully awake. He is directly cognising the supreme Reality? the Light of lights. He is full of illumination and AtmaJnana or knowledge of the Self.
2:69.word_meanings: या — which; निशा — night; सर्वभूतानाम् — of all beings; तस्याम् — in that; जागर्ति — wakes; संयमी — the selfcontrolled; यस्याम् — in which; जाग्रति — wake; भूतानि — all beings; सा — that; निशा — night; पश्यतः (of — the) seeing; मुनेः — of the Muni.

2:70.pada_sa: आपूर्यमाणम्, अचलप्रतिष्ठं, समुद्रम्, आपः, प्रविशन्ति, यद्वत्, तद्वत्, कामाः, यं, प्रविशन्ति, सर्वे, सः, शान्तिम्, आप्नोति, न, कामकामी ॥ ७० ॥
2:70.pada_iast: āpūryamāṇam, acalapratiṣṭhaṃ, samudram, āpaḥ, praviśanti, yadvat, tadvat, kāmāḥ, yaṃ, praviśanti, sarve, saḥ, śāntim, āpnoti, na, kāmakāmī || 70 ||
2:70.translation: That man attains peace into whom all desires enter in the same way as the waters flow into a sea that remains unchanged (even) when being filled up from all sides. Not so one who is desirous of objects.
2:70.explanation: Just as the ocean filled with waters from all sides remains unmoved? so also the sage who is resting in his own Svarupa or the Self is not a bit affected though desires of all sorts enter from all sides. The sage attains peace or liberation but not he who longs for objects of sensual enjoyment and entertains various desires. (Cf.XVIII.53?54).
2:70.word_meanings: आपूर्यमाणम् — filled from all sides; अचलप्रतिष्ठम् — based in stillness; समुद्रम् — ocean; आपः — water; प्रविशन्ति — enter; यद्वत् — as; तद्वत् — so; कामाः — desires; यम् — whom; प्रविशन्ति — enter; सर्वे — all; सः — he; शान्तिम् — peace; आप्नोति — attains; न — not; कामकामी — desirer of desires.

iast: vihāya kāmān yaḥ sarvān pumānś carati niḥspṛihaḥ

2:71.pada_sa: विहाय, कामान्, यः, सर्वान्, पुमान्, चरति, निःस्पृहः, निर्ममः, निरहङ्कारः, सः, शान्तिम्, अधिगच्छति ॥ ७१ ॥
2:71.anvaya_sa: जनार्दन, चेत्, कर्मणः, बुद्धिः, ते, ज्यायसी, मता, तत्, केशव, माम्, घोरे, कर्मणि, किं, नियोजयसि ॥ १ ॥
2:71.pada_iast: vihāya, kāmān, yaḥ, sarvān, pumān, carati, niḥspṛhaḥ, nirmamaḥ, nirahaṅkāraḥ, saḥ, śāntim, adhigacchati || 71 ||
2:71.anvaya_iast: janārdana, cet, karmaṇaḥ, buddhiḥ, te, jyāyasī, matā, tat, keśava, mām, ghore, karmaṇi, kiṃ, niyojayasi || 1 ||
2:71.translation: That man attains peace who, after rejecting all desires, moves about free from hankering, without the idea of ('me' and) 'mine', and devoid of pride.
2:71.explanation: That man who lives destitute of longing? abandoning all desires? without the senses of I and mine? who is satisfied with the bare necessities of life? who does not care even for those bare necessities of life? who has no attachment even for the bare necessities of life? attains Moksha or eternal peace. (Cf.II.55).
2:71.word_meanings: विहाय — abandoning; कामान् — desires; यः — that; सर्वान् — all; पुमान् — man; चरति — moves about; निःस्पृहः — free from longing; निर्ममः — devoid of mineness; निरहंकारः — without egoism; सः — he; शान्तिम् — to peace; अधिगच्छति — attains.

sa: एषा ब्राह्मी स्थितिः पार्थ नैनां प्राप्य विमुह्यति
iast: eṣhā brāhmī sthitiḥ pārtha naināṁ prāpya vimuhyati

2:72.pada_sa: एषा, ब्राह्मी, स्थितिः, पार्थ, न, एनां, प्राप्य, विमुह्यति, स्थित्वा, अस्याम्, अन्तकाले, अपि, ब्रह्मनिर्वाणम्, ऋच्छति ॥ ७२ ॥
2:72.anvaya_sa: व्यामिश्रेण, इव, वाक्येन, मे, बुद्धिं, मोहयसि, इव, तत्, एकं, निश्चित्य, वद, येन, अहं, श्रेयः, आप्नुयम्  ॥ २ ॥
2:72.pada_iast: eṣā, brāhmī, sthitiḥ, pārtha, na, enāṃ, prāpya, vimuhyati, sthitvā, asyām, antakāle, api, brahmanirvāṇam, ṛcchati || 72 ||
2:72.anvaya_iast: vyāmiśreṇa, iva, vākyena, me, buddhiṃ, mohayasi, iva, tat, ekaṃ, niścitya, vada, yena, ahaṃ, śreyaḥ, āpnuyam  || 2 ||
2:72.translation: O Partha, this is the state of being established in Brahman. One does not become deluded after attaining this. One attains identification with Brahman by being established in this state even in the closing years of one's life.
2:72.explanation: The state described in the previous verse -- to renounce everything and to live in Brahman -- is the Brahmic state or the state of Brahman. If one attains to this state one is never deluded. He attains Moksha if he stays in that state even at the hour of his death. It is needless to say that he who gets establised in Brahman throughout his life attains to the state of Brahman or,BrahmaNirvana (Cf.VIII.5?6).Maharshi Vidyaranya says in his Panchadasi that Antakala here means the moment at which Avidya or mutual superimposition of the Self and the notSelf ends.Thus in the Upanishads of the glorious Bhagavad Gita? the science of the Eternal? the scripture of Yoga? the dialogue between Sri Krishna and Arjuna? ends the second discourse entitledThe Sankhya Yoga.,
2:72.word_meanings: एषा — this; ब्राह्मी — of Brahmic; स्थितिः — state; पार्थ — O Partha; न — not; एनाम् — this; प्राप्य — having obtained; विमुह्यति — is deluded; स्थित्वा — being established; अस्याम् — in this; अन्तकाले — at the end of life; अपि — even; ब्रह्मनिर्वाणम् — oneness with Brahman; ऋच्छति — attains.

sa: तत्किं कर्मणि घोरे मां नियोजयसि केशव
iast: jyāyasī cet karmaṇas te matā buddhir janārdana
tat kiṁ karmaṇi ghore māṁ niyojayasi keśava

3:1.pada_sa: ज्यायसी, चेत्, कर्मणः, ते, मता, बुद्धिः, जनार्दन, तत्, किं, कर्मणि, घोरे, मां, नियोजयसि, केशव ॥ १ ॥
3:1.anvaya_sa: अनघ, अस्मिन्, लोके, द्विविधा, निष्ठा, मया, पुरा, प्रोक्ता, साङ्ख्यनां, ज्ञानयोगेन, योगिनां, कर्मयोगेन ॥ ३ ॥
3:1.pada_iast: jyāyasī, cet, karmaṇaḥ, te, matā, buddhiḥ, janārdana, tat, kiṃ, karmaṇi, ghore, māṃ, niyojayasi, keśava || 1 ||
3:1.anvaya_iast: anagha, asmin, loke, dvividhā, niṣṭhā, mayā, purā, proktā, sāṅkhyanāṃ, jñānayogena, yogināṃ, karmayogena || 3 ||
3:1.translation: Arjuna said  O Janardana (krsna), if it be Your opinion that wisdom is superior to action, why they do you urge me to horrible aciton, O Kesava ?
3:1.explanation: In verses 49? 50 and 51 of chapter II? Lord Krsihna has spoken very highly about Buddhi Yoga. He again asks Arjuna to fight. That is the reason why Arjuna is perplexed now.
3:1.word_meanings: ज्यायसी — superior; चेत् — if; कर्मणः — than action; ते — by Thee; मता — thought; बुद्धिः — knowledge; जनार्दन — O Janardana; तत् — then; किम् — why; कर्मणि — in action; घोरे — terrible; माम् — me; नियोजयसि — Thou engagest; केशव — O Kesava.

iast: tad ekaṁ vada niścitya yena śreyo ’ham āpnuyām

3:2.pada_sa: व्यामिश्रेण, इव, वाक्येन, बुद्धिं, मोहयसि, इव, मे, तत्, एकं, वद, निश्चित्य, येन, श्रेयः, अहम्, आप्नुयाम्  ॥ २ ॥
3:2.anvaya_sa: पुरुषः, न, कर्मणाम्, अनारम्भात्, नैष्कर्म्यम्, अश्नुते, च, न, संन्यसनात्, एव, सिद्धिं, समधिगच्छति ॥ ४ ॥
3:2.pada_iast: vyāmiśreṇa, iva, vākyena, buddhiṃ, mohayasi, iva, me, tat, ekaṃ, vada, niścitya, yena, śreyaḥ, aham, āpnuyām  || 2 ||
3:2.anvaya_iast: puruṣaḥ, na, karmaṇām, anārambhāt, naiṣkarmyam, aśnute, ca, na, saṃnyasanāt, eva, siddhiṃ, samadhigacchati || 4 ||
3:2.translation: You bewilder my understanding, as it were, by a seemingly conflicting statement! Tell me for certain one of these by which I may attain the highest Good.
3:2.explanation: Arjuna says to Lord Krishna? Tecah me one of the two? knowledge or action? by which I may attain to the highest good or bliss or Moksha. (Cf.V.I).
3:2.word_meanings: व्यामिश्रेण — perplexing; इव — as it were; वाक्येन — with speech; बुद्धिम् — understanding; मोहयसि (Thou) — confusest; इव — as it were; मे — my; तत् — that; एकम् — one; वद — tell; निश्चित्य — for certain; येन — by which; श्रेयः — bliss (the good or the highest); अहम् — I; आप्नुयाम् — may attain.

iast: loke ’smin dvi-vidhā niṣhṭhā purā proktā mayānagha

3:3.pada_sa: लोके, अस्मिन्, द्विविधा, निष्ठा, पुरा, प्रोक्ता, मया, अनघ, ज्ञानयोगेन, साङ्‍ख्यानां, कर्मयोगेन, योगिनाम् ॥ ३ ॥
3:3.anvaya_sa: हि, कश्चित्, जातु, क्षणम्, अपि, अकर्मकृत्, न, तिष्ठति, हि, सर्वः, प्रकृतिजैः, गुणैः, अवशः, कर्म, कार्यते ॥ ५ ॥
3:3.pada_iast: loke, asmin, dvividhā, niṣṭhā, purā, proktā, mayā, anagha, jñānayogena, sāṅ‍khyānāṃ, karmayogena, yoginām || 3 ||
3:3.anvaya_iast: hi, kaścit, jātu, kṣaṇam, api, akarmakṛt, na, tiṣṭhati, hi, sarvaḥ, prakṛtijaiḥ, guṇaiḥ, avaśaḥ, karma, kāryate || 5 ||
3:3.translation: The Blessed Lord said  O unblemished one, two kinds of steadfastness in this world were spoken of by Me in the days of yore-through the Yoga of Knowledge for the men of realization; through the Yoga of Action for the yogis.
3:3.explanation: The path of knowledge of the Sankhyas (Jnana Yoga) was described by Lord Krishna in chapter II? verses 11 to 38 the path of action (Karma Yoga) from 40 to 53.Pura Prokta may also mean In the beginning of creation the twofold path was given by Me to this world.Those who are endowed with the four means and who have sharp? subtle intellect and bold understanding are fit for Jnana Yoga. Those who have a tendency or inclination for wok are fit for Karma Yoga. (The four means are discrimination? dispassion? sixfold virutes? and longing for liberation. The sixfold virtues are control of the mind? control of the senses? fortitude (endurance)? turning away from the objects of the world? faith and tranillity.)It is not possible for a man to practise the two Yogas simultaneously. Karma Yoga is a means to an end. It purifies the heart and prepares the aspirant for the reception of knowledge. The Karma Yogi should take up Jnana Yoga as soon as his heart is purified. Jnana Yoga takes the aspirant directly to the goal without any extraneous help. (Cf.V.5).
3:3.word_meanings: लोके — in world; अस्मिन् — in this; द्विविधा — twofold; निष्ठा — path; पुरा — previously; प्रोक्ता — said; मया — by Me; अनघ — O sinless one; ज्ञानयोगेन — by the path of knowledge; सांख्यानाम् — of the Sankhyas; कर्मयोगेन — by the path of action; योगिनाम् — of the Yogins.

iast: na ca sannyasanād eva siddhiṁ samadhigacchati

3:4.pada_sa: न, कर्मणाम्, अनारम्भात्, नैष्कर्म्यं, पुरुषः, अश्नुते, न, च, संन्यसनात्, एव, सिद्धिं, समधिगच्छति ॥ ४ ॥
3:4.anvaya_sa: यः, विमूढात्मा, कर्मेन्द्रियाणि, संयम्य, इन्द्रियार्थान्, मनसा, स्मरन्, आस्ते, सः, मिथ्याचारः, उच्यते ॥ ६ ॥
3:4.pada_iast: na, karmaṇām, anārambhāt, naiṣkarmyaṃ, puruṣaḥ, aśnute, na, ca, saṃnyasanāt, eva, siddhiṃ, samadhigacchati || 4 ||
3:4.anvaya_iast: yaḥ, vimūḍhātmā, karmendriyāṇi, saṃyamya, indriyārthān, manasā, smaran, āste, saḥ, mithyācāraḥ, ucyate || 6 ||
3:4.translation: A person does not attain freedom from action by abstaining from action; nor does he attain fulfilment merely through renunciation.
3:4.explanation: Actionlessness (Naishkarmyam) and perfection (Siddhi) are synonymous. The sage who has attained to perfection or reached the state of actionlessness rests in his own essential nature as ExistenceKnowledgeBliss Absolute (Satchidananda Svarupa). He has neither necessity nor desire for action as a means to an end. He has perfect satisfaction in the Self.One attains to the state of actionlessness by gaining the knowledge of the Self. If a man simply sits iet by abandoning action you cannot say that he has attained to the state of actionlessness. His mind will be planning? scheming and speculating. Thought is real action. The sage who is free from affirmative thoughts? wishes? and likes and dislikes? who has the knowledge of the Self can be said to have attained to the state of actionlessness.No one can reach perfection or freedom from action or knowledge of the Self by mere renunciation or by simply giving up activities without possessing the knowledge of the Self. (Cf.XVIII.49).
3:4.word_meanings: न — not; कर्मणाम् — of actions; अनारम्भात् — from nonperformance; नैष्कर्म्यम् — actionlessness; पुरुषः — man; अश्नुते — reaches; न — not; च — and; संन्यसनात् — from renunciation; एव — only; सिद्धिम् — perfection; समधिगच्छति — attains.

iast: na hi kaścit kṣaṇam api jātu tiṣṭhaty akarma-kṛt
kāryate hy avaśaḥ karma sarvaḥ prakṛti-jair guṇaiḥ

3:5.pada_sa: न, हि, कश्चित्, क्षणम्, अपि, जातु, तिष्ठति, अकर्मकृत्, कार्यते, हि, अवशः, कर्म, सर्वः, प्रकृतिजैः, र्गुणैः ॥ ५ ॥
3:5.anvaya_sa: तु, अर्जुन, यः, मनसा, इन्द्रियाणि, नियम्य, असक्तः, कर्मेन्द्रियैः, कर्मयोगम्, आरभते, सः, विशिष्यते ॥ ७ ॥
3:5.pada_iast: na, hi, kaścit, kṣaṇam, api, jātu, tiṣṭhati, akarmakṛt, kāryate, hi, avaśaḥ, karma, sarvaḥ, prakṛtijaiḥ, rguṇaiḥ || 5 ||
3:5.anvaya_iast: tu, arjuna, yaḥ, manasā, indriyāṇi, niyamya, asaktaḥ, karmendriyaiḥ, karmayogam, ārabhate, saḥ, viśiṣyate || 7 ||
3:5.translation: Because, no one ever remains even for a moment without doing work. For all are made to work under compulsion by the gunas born of Nature.
3:5.explanation: The Gunas (alities of Nature) are three? viz.? Sattva? Rajas and Tamas. Sattva is harmony or light or purity Rajas is passion or motion Tamas is inertia or darkness. Sattvic actions help a man to attain to Moksha. Rajasic and Tamasic actions bind a man to Samsara.These alities cannot affect a man who has knowledge of the Self. He has crossed over these alities. He has become a Gunatita (one who has transcended the alities of Nature). The ignorant man who has no knowledge of the Self and who is swayed by Avidya or nescience is driven helplessly to action by the Gunas. (Cf.IV.16?XVIII.11).
3:5.word_meanings: नहि — not; कश्चित् — anyone; क्षणम् — a moment; अपि — even; जातु — verily; तिष्ठति — remains; अकर्मकृत् — without performing action; कार्यते — is made to do; हि — for; अवशः — helpless; कर्म — action; सर्वः — all; प्रकृतिजैः — born of Prakriti; गुणैः — by the alities.

sa: कर्मेन्द्रियाणि संयम्य य आस्ते मनसा स्मरन्
iast: karmendriyāṇi sanyamya ya āste manasā smaran

3:6.pada_sa: कर्मेन्द्रियाणि, संयम्य, यः, आस्ते, मनसा, स्मरन्, इन्द्रियार्थान्, विमूढात्मा, मिथ्याचारः, सः, उच्यते ॥ ६ ॥
3:6.anvaya_sa: त्वं, नियतं, कर्म, कुरु, हि, अकर्मणः, कर्म, ज्यायः, च, अकर्मणः, ते, शरीरयात्रा, अपि, न, प्रसिद्ध्येत् ॥ ८ ॥
3:6.pada_iast: karmendriyāṇi, saṃyamya, yaḥ, āste, manasā, smaran, indriyārthān, vimūḍhātmā, mithyācāraḥ, saḥ, ucyate || 6 ||
3:6.anvaya_iast: tvaṃ, niyataṃ, karma, kuru, hi, akarmaṇaḥ, karma, jyāyaḥ, ca, akarmaṇaḥ, te, śarīrayātrā, api, na, prasiddhyet || 8 ||
3:6.translation: One, who after withdrawing the organs of action, sits mentally recollecting the objects of the senses, that one, of deluded mind, is called a hypocrite.
3:6.explanation: The five organs of action? Karma Indriyas? are Vak (organ of speech)? Pani (hands)? Padam (feet)? Upastha (genitals) and Guda (anus). They are born of the Rajasic portion of the five Tanmatras or subtle elements Vak from the Akasa Tanmatra (ether)? Pani from the Vayu Tanmatra (air)? Padam from the Agni Tanmatra (fire)? Upastha from the Apas Tanmatra (water)? and Guda from the Prithivi Tanmatra (earth). That man who? restraining the organs of action? sits revolving in his mind thoughts regarding the objects of the senses is a man of sinful conduct. He is selfdeluded. He is a veritable hypocrite.The organs of action must be controlled. The thoughts should also be controlled. The mind should be firmly fixed on the Lord. Only then will you become a true Yogi. Only then will you attain to Selfrealisation.
3:6.word_meanings: कर्मेन्द्रियाणि — organs of action; संयम्य — restraining; यः — who; आस्ते — sits; मनसा — by the mind; स्मरन् — remembering; इन्द्रियार्थान् — senseobjects; विमूढात्मा — of deluded understanding; मिथ्याचारः — hypocrite; सः — he; उच्यते — is called.

3:7.pada_sa: यः, तु, इद्रियाणि, मनसा, नियम्य, आरभते, अर्जुन, कर्मेन्द्रियैः, कर्मयोगम्, असक्तः, सः, विशिष्यते ॥ ७ ॥
3:7.anvaya_sa: यज्ञार्थात्, कर्मणः, अन्यत्र, अयं, लोकः, कर्मबन्धनः, कौन्तेय, मुक्तसङ्गः, तदर्थं, कर्म, समाचर ॥ ९ ॥
3:7.pada_iast: yaḥ, tu, idriyāṇi, manasā, niyamya, ārabhate, arjuna, karmendriyaiḥ, karmayogam, asaktaḥ, saḥ, viśiṣyate || 7 ||
3:7.anvaya_iast: yajñārthāt, karmaṇaḥ, anyatra, ayaṃ, lokaḥ, karmabandhanaḥ, kaunteya, muktasaṅgaḥ, tadarthaṃ, karma, samācara || 9 ||
3:7.translation: But, O Arjuna, one who engages in Karma-yoga with the organs of action, controlling the organs with the mind and becoming unattached-that one excels.
3:7.explanation: If anyone performs actions with his organs of action (viz.? hands? feet? organ of speech? etc.) controlling the organs of knowledge by the mind? and without expectation of the fruits of the actions and without egoism? he is certainly more worthy than the other who is a hypocrite or a man of false conduct. (Cf.II.64?68IV.21).The five organs of knowledge are the eyes? the ears? the nose? the skin and the sense of taste (tongue).
3:7.word_meanings: यः — whose; तु — but; इन्द्रियाणि — the senses; मनसा — by the mind; नियम्य — controlling; आरभते — commences; अर्जुन — O Arjuna; कर्मेन्द्रियैः — by the organs of action; कर्मयोगम् — Karma Yoga; असक्तः — unattached; सः — he; विशिष्यते — excels.

śarīra-yātrāpi ca te na prasiddhyed akarmaṇaḥ

3:8.pada_sa: नियतं, कुरु, कर्म, त्वं, कर्म, ज्यायः, हि, अकर्मणः, शरीरयात्रा, अपि, च, ते, न, प्रसिध्येत्, अकर्मणः ॥ ८ ॥
3:8.anvaya_sa: प्रजापतिः, पुरा, सहयज्ञाः, प्रजाः, सृष्ट्वा, उवाच, अनेन, प्रसविष्यध्वम्, एषः, वः, इष्टकामधुक्, अस्तु ॥ १० ॥
3:8.pada_iast: niyataṃ, kuru, karma, tvaṃ, karma, jyāyaḥ, hi, akarmaṇaḥ, śarīrayātrā, api, ca, te, na, prasidhyet, akarmaṇaḥ || 8 ||
3:8.anvaya_iast: prajāpatiḥ, purā, sahayajñāḥ, prajāḥ, sṛṣṭvā, uvāca, anena, prasaviṣyadhvam, eṣaḥ, vaḥ, iṣṭakāmadhuk, astu || 10 ||
3:8.translation: You perform the obligatory duties, for action is superior to inaction. And, through inaction, even the maintenance of your body will not be possible.
3:8.explanation: Niyatam Karma is an obligatory duty which one is bound to perform. Thenonperformance of the bounden duties causes demerit. The performance of the obligatory duties is not a means for the attainment of a specific result. The performance does not cause any merit.Living itself involves several natural and unavoidable actions which have to be performed by all. It is ignorance to say? I can live doing nothing.
3:8.word_meanings: नियतम् — bounden (prescribed or obligatory); कुरु — perform; कर्म — action; त्वम् — thou; कर्म — action; ज्यायः — superior; हि — for; अकर्मणः — than inaction; शरीरयात्रा — maintenance of the body; अपि — even; च — and; ते — thy; न — not; प्रसिद्ध्येत् — would be possible; अकर्मणः — by inaction.

3:9.pada_sa: यज्ञार्थात्, कर्मणः, अन्यत्र, लोकः, अयं, कर्मबन्धनः, तदर्थं, कर्म, कौन्तेय, मुक्तसङ्गः, समाचर ॥ ९ ॥
3:9.anvaya_sa: अनेन, देवान्, भावयत, ते, देवाः, वः, भावयन्तु, (एवं) परस्परं, भावयन्तः, परं, श्रेयः, अवाप्स्यथ ॥ ११ ॥
3:9.pada_iast: yajñārthāt, karmaṇaḥ, anyatra, lokaḥ, ayaṃ, karmabandhanaḥ, tadarthaṃ, karma, kaunteya, muktasaṅgaḥ, samācara || 9 ||
3:9.anvaya_iast: anena, devān, bhāvayata, te, devāḥ, vaḥ, bhāvayantu, (evaṃ) parasparaṃ, bhāvayantaḥ, paraṃ, śreyaḥ, avāpsyatha || 11 ||
3:9.translation: This man becomes bound by actions other than that action meant for God. Without being attached, O son of Kunti, you perform actions for Him.
3:9.explanation: Yajna means sacrifice or religious rite or any unselfish action done with a pure motive. It means also Isvara. The Taittiriya Samhita (of the Veda) says Yajna verily is Vishnu (174). If anyone does actions for the sake of the Lord? he is not bound. His heart is purified by performing actions for the sake of the Lord. Where this spirit of unselfishness does not govern the action? it will bind one to Samsara however good or glorious it may be. (Cf.II.48).
3:9.word_meanings: यज्ञार्थात् — for the sake of sacrifice; कर्मणः — of action; अन्यत्र — otherwise; लोकः — the world; अयम् — this; कर्मबन्धनः — bound by action; तदर्थम् — for that sake; कर्म — action; कौन्तेय — O Kaunteya; मुक्तसंगः — free from attachment; समाचार — perform.

3:10.pada_sa: सहयज्ञाः, प्रजाः, सृष्ट्वा, पुरा, उवाच, प्रजापतिः, अनेन, प्रसविष्यध्वम्, एषः, वः, अस्तु, इष्टकामधुक् ॥ १० ॥
3:10.anvaya_sa: यज्ञभाविताः, देवाः, वः, इष्टान्, भोग़ान्, दास्यन्ते, तैः, दत्तान्, यः, एभ्यः, अप्रदाय, हि, भुङ्क्ते, सः, एव, स्तेनः ॥ १२ ॥
3:10.pada_iast: sahayajñāḥ, prajāḥ, sṛṣṭvā, purā, uvāca, prajāpatiḥ, anena, prasaviṣyadhvam, eṣaḥ, vaḥ, astu, iṣṭakāmadhuk || 10 ||
3:10.anvaya_iast: yajñabhāvitāḥ, devāḥ, vaḥ, iṣṭān, bhoग़्ān, dāsyante, taiḥ, dattān, yaḥ, ebhyaḥ, apradāya, hi, bhuṅkte, saḥ, eva, stenaḥ || 12 ||
3:10.translation: In the days of yore, having created the beings together with the sacrifices, Prajapati said: 'By this you multiply. Let this be your yielder of coveted objects of desire.'
3:10.explanation: Prajapati is the Creator or Brahma. Kamadhuk is another name for the cow Kamadhenu. Kamadhenu is the cow of Indra from which everyone can milk whatever one desires. (Cf.VIII.4IX.2427X.25).
3:10.word_meanings: सहयज्ञाः — together with sacrifice; प्रजाः — mankind; सृष्ट्वा — having created; पुरा — in the beginning; उवाच — said; प्रजापतिः — Prajapati; अनेन — by this; प्रसविष्यध्वम् — shall ye propagate; एषः — this; वः — your; अस्तु — let be; इष्टकामधुक् — milch cow of desires.

iast: devān bhāvayatānena te devā bhāvayantu vaḥ

3:11.pada_sa: देवान्, भावयत, अनेन, ते, देवाः, भावयन्तु, वः, परस्परं, भावयन्तः, श्रेयः, परम्, अवाप्स्यथ ॥ ११ ॥
3:11.anvaya_sa: यज्ञशिष्टाशिनः, सन्तः, सर्वकिल्बिषैः, मुच्यन्ते, ये, पापाः, आत्मकारणात्, पचन्ति, ते, तु, अघं, भुञ्जते ॥ १३ ॥
3:11.pada_iast: devān, bhāvayata, anena, te, devāḥ, bhāvayantu, vaḥ, parasparaṃ, bhāvayantaḥ, śreyaḥ, param, avāpsyatha || 11 ||
3:11.anvaya_iast: yajñaśiṣṭāśinaḥ, santaḥ, sarvakilbiṣaiḥ, mucyante, ye, pāpāḥ, ātmakāraṇāt, pacanti, te, tu, aghaṃ, bhuñjate || 13 ||
3:11.translation: 'You nourish the gods with this. Let those gods nourish you. Nourishing one another, you shall attain the supreme Good.'
3:11.explanation: Deva literally means the shining one. By this sacrifice you nourish the gods such as Indra. The gods shall nourish you with rain? etc. the highest good is the attainment of the knowledge of the Self which frees one from the round of births and deaths. The highest good may mean the attainment of heaven also. The fruit depends upon the motive of the aspirant.
3:11.word_meanings: देवान् — the gods; भावयत — nourish (ye); अनेन — with this; ते — those; देवाः — gods; भावयन्तु — may nourish; वः — you; परस्परम् — one another; भावयन्तः — nourishing; श्रेयः — good; परम् — the highest; अवाप्स्यथ — shall attain.

sa: तैर्दत्तानप्रदायैभ्यो यो भुङ्क्ते स्तेन एव सः
iast: iṣṭān bhogān hi vo devā dāsyante yajña-bhāvitāḥ
tair dattān apradāyaibhyo yo bhuṅkte stena eva saḥ

3:12.pada_sa: इष्टान्, भोगान्, हि, वः, देवाः, दास्यन्ते, यज्ञभाविताः, तैः, दत्तान्, अप्रदाय, एभ्यः, यः, भुङ्क्ते, स्तेनः, एव, सः ॥ १२ ॥
3:12.anvaya_sa: भूतानि, अन्नात्, भवन्ति, अन्नसम्भवः, पर्जन्यात्, पर्जन्यः, यज्ञात्, भवति, यज्ञः, कर्मसमुद्भवः ॥ १४ ॥
3:12.pada_iast: iṣṭān, bhogān, hi, vaḥ, devāḥ, dāsyante, yajñabhāvitāḥ, taiḥ, dattān, apradāya, ebhyaḥ, yaḥ, bhuṅkte, stenaḥ, eva, saḥ || 12 ||
3:12.anvaya_iast: bhūtāni, annāt, bhavanti, annasambhavaḥ, parjanyāt, parjanyaḥ, yajñāt, bhavati, yajñaḥ, karmasamudbhavaḥ || 14 ||
3:12.translation: 'Being nourished by sacrifices, the gods will indeed give you the coveted enjoyments. He is certainly a theif who enjoys what have been given by them without offering (these) to them.'
3:12.explanation: When the gods are pleased with you sacrifices? they will bestow on you all the desired objects such as children? cattle? property? etc. He who enjoys what has been given to him by the gods? i.e.? he who gratifies the cravings of his own body and the senses without offering anything to the gods in return is a veritable thief. He is really a dacoit of the property of the gods.
3:12.word_meanings: इष्टान् — desired; भोगान् — objects; हि — so; वः — to you; देवाः — the gods; दास्यन्ते — will give; यज्ञभाविताः — nourished by sacrifice; तैः — by them; दत्तान् — give; अप्रदाय — without offering; एभ्यः — to them; यः — who; भुङ्क्ते — enjoys; स्तेनः — thief; एव — verily; सः — he.

sa: भुञ्जते ते त्वघं पापा ये पचन्त्यात्मकारणात्
iast: bhuñjate te tv aghaṁ pāpā ye pacanty ātma-kāraṇāt

3:13.pada_sa: यज्ञशिष्टाशिनः, सन्तः, मुच्यन्ते, सर्वकिल्बिषैः, भुञ्जते, ते, तु, अघं, पापाः, ये, पचन्ति, आत्मकारणात् ॥ १३ ॥
3:13.anvaya_sa: कर्म, ब्रह्मोद्भवं, विद्धि, ब्रह्म, अक्षरसमुद्भवं, तस्मात्, सर्वगतं, ब्रह्म, नित्यं, यज्ञे, प्रतिष्ठितम् ॥ १५ ॥
3:13.pada_iast: yajñaśiṣṭāśinaḥ, santaḥ, mucyante, sarvakilbiṣaiḥ, bhuñjate, te, tu, aghaṃ, pāpāḥ, ye, pacanti, ātmakāraṇāt || 13 ||
3:13.anvaya_iast: karma, brahmodbhavaṃ, viddhi, brahma, akṣarasamudbhavaṃ, tasmāt, sarvagataṃ, brahma, nityaṃ, yajñe, pratiṣṭhitam || 15 ||
3:13.translation: By becoming partakers of the remembers of sacrifices, they become freed from all sins. But the unholy persons who cook for themselves, they incur sin.
3:13.explanation: Those who? after performing the five great sacrifices? eat the remnants of the food are freed from all the sins committed by these five agents of insect slaughter? viz.? (1) the pestle and mortar? (2) the grinding stone? (3) the fireplace? (4) the place where the waterpot is kept? and (5) the broom. These are the five places where injury to life is daily committed. The sins are washed away by the performance of the five MahaYajnas or great sacrifices which every Dvija(twicorn or the people belonging to the first three castes in Hindu society? especially the Brahmin) ought to perform1. DevaYajna Offering sacrifices to the gods which will satisfy them?2. BrahmaYajna or RishiYajna Teaching and reciting the scriptures which will satisfy Brahman and the Rishis?3. PitriYajna Offering libations of water to ones ancestors which will satisfy the manes?4. NriYajna The feeding of the hungry and the guests? and?5. BhutaYajna The feeding of the subhuman species? such as animals? birds? etc.
3:13.word_meanings: यज्ञशिष्टाशिनः — who eat the remnants of the sacrifice; सन्तः — the righteous; मुच्यन्ते — are freed; सर्वकिल्बिषैः — from all sins; भुञ्जते — eat; ते — those; तु — indeed; अघम् — sin; पापाः — sinful ones; ये — who; पचन्ति — cook; आत्मकारणात् — for their own sake.

3:14.pada_sa: अन्नात्, भवन्ति, भूतानि, पर्जन्यात्, अन्नसम्भवः, यज्ञात्, भवति, पर्जन्यः, यज्ञः, कर्मसमुद्भवः ॥ १४ ॥
3:14.anvaya_sa: पार्थ, यः, इह, एवं, प्रवर्तितं, चक्रं, न, अनुवर्तयति, सः, इन्द्रियारामः, अघायुः, मोघं, जीवति ॥ १६ ॥
3:14.pada_iast: annāt, bhavanti, bhūtāni, parjanyāt, annasambhavaḥ, yajñāt, bhavati, parjanyaḥ, yajñaḥ, karmasamudbhavaḥ || 14 ||
3:14.anvaya_iast: pārtha, yaḥ, iha, evaṃ, pravartitaṃ, cakraṃ, na, anuvartayati, saḥ, indriyārāmaḥ, aghāyuḥ, moghaṃ, jīvati || 16 ||
3:14.translation: From food are born the creatures; the origin of food is from rainfall; rainfall originates from sacrifice; sacrifice has action as its origin.
3:14.explanation: Here Yajna means Apurva or the subtle principle or the unseen form which a sacrifice assumes between the time of its performance and the time when its fruits manifest themselves.
3:14.word_meanings: अन्नात् — from food; भवन्ति — come forth; भूतानि — beings; पर्जन्यात् — from rain; अन्नसम्भवः — production of food; यज्ञात् — from sacrifice; भवति — arises; पर्जन्यः — rain; यज्ञः — sacrifice; कर्मसमुद्भवः — born of action.

iast: tasmāt sarva-gataṁ brahma nityaṁ yajñe pratiṣṭhitam

3:15.pada_sa: कर्म, ब्रह्मोद्भवं, विद्धि, ब्रह्म, अक्षरसमुद्भवम्, तस्मात्, सर्वगतं, ब्रह्म, नित्यं, यज्ञे, प्रतिष्ठितम् ॥ १५ ॥
3:15.anvaya_sa: तु, यः, मानवः, आत्मरतिः, एव, च, आत्मतृप्तः, च, आत्मनि, एव, संतुष्टः, स्यात्, तस्य, कार्यं, न, विद्यते ॥ १७ ॥
3:15.pada_iast: karma, brahmodbhavaṃ, viddhi, brahma, akṣarasamudbhavam, tasmāt, sarvagataṃ, brahma, nityaṃ, yajñe, pratiṣṭhitam || 15 ||
3:15.anvaya_iast: tu, yaḥ, mānavaḥ, ātmaratiḥ, eva, ca, ātmatṛptaḥ, ca, ātmani, eva, saṃtuṣṭaḥ, syāt, tasya, kāryaṃ, na, vidyate || 17 ||
3:15.translation: Know that actin has the veda as its origin; the Vedas has the Immutable as its source. Hence, the all-pervading Veda is for ever based on sacrifice.
3:15.explanation: Brahma may mean Veda. Just as the breath comes out of a man? so also the Veda is the breath of the Imperishable or the Omniscient. The Veda ever rests in the sacrifice? i.e.? it deals chiefly with sacrifices and the ways of their performance. (Cf.IV.24 to 32).Karma Action? Brahmodbhavam arisen from the injunctions of the Vedas.
3:15.word_meanings: कर्म — action; ब्रह्मोद्भवम् — arisen from Brahma; विद्धि — know; ब्रह्म — Brahma; अक्षरसमुद्भवम् — arisen from the Imperishable; तस्मात् — therefore; सर्वगतम् — allpervading; ब्रह्म — Brahma; नित्यम् — ever; यज्ञे — in sacrifice; प्रतिष्ठितम् (is) — established.

iast: aghāyur indriyārāmo moghaṁ pārtha sa jīvati

3:16.pada_sa: एवं, प्रवर्तितं, चक्रं, न, अनुवर्तयति, इह, यः, अघायुः, इन्द्रियारामः, मोघं, पार्थ, सः, जीवति ॥ १६ ॥
3:16.anvaya_sa: इह, तस्य, कृतेन, एव, अर्थः, न, अकृतेन, कश्चन, न, च, अस्य, सर्वभूतेषु, कश्चित्, अर्थव्यपाश्रयः न ॥ १८ ॥
3:16.pada_iast: evaṃ, pravartitaṃ, cakraṃ, na, anuvartayati, iha, yaḥ, aghāyuḥ, indriyārāmaḥ, moghaṃ, pārtha, saḥ, jīvati || 16 ||
3:16.anvaya_iast: iha, tasya, kṛtena, eva, arthaḥ, na, akṛtena, kaścana, na, ca, asya, sarvabhūteṣu, kaścit, arthavyapāśrayaḥ na || 18 ||
3:16.translation: O Partha, he lives in vain who does not follow here the wheel thus set in motion, whose life is sinful, and who indulges in the senses.
3:16.explanation: This is the wheel of action set in motion by the Creator on the basis of the Veda and sacrifice.He who does not follow the wheel by studying the Vedas and performing the sacrifices prescribed therein but who indulges only in sensual pleasures lives in vain. He is wasting his life. He is leading a worthless life indeed.One who does not live in accordance with this law and who is selfish commits sin. He violates the law of the Creator and that is the worst sin.
3:16.word_meanings: एवम् — thus; प्रवर्तितम् — set revolving; चक्रम् — wheel; न — not; अनुवर्तयति — follows; इह — here; यः — who; अघायुः — living in sin; इन्द्रियारामः — rejoicing in the senses; मोघम् — in vain; पार्थ — O Partha; सः — he; जीवति — lives.

sa: आत्मन्येव च सन्तुष्टस्तस्य कार्यं न विद्यते

ātmany eva ca santuṣṭas tasya kāryaṁ na vidyate

3:17.pada_sa: यः, तु, आत्मरतिः, एव, स्यात्, आत्मतृप्तः, च, मानवः, आत्मनि, एव, च, सन्तुष्टः, तस्य, कार्यं, न, विद्यते ॥ १७ ॥
3:17.anvaya_sa: तस्मात्, असक्तः, सततं, कार्यं, कर्म, समाचर, हि, असक्तः, पूरुषः, कर्म, आचरन्, परम्, आप्नोति ॥ १९ ॥
3:17.pada_iast: yaḥ, tu, ātmaratiḥ, eva, syāt, ātmatṛptaḥ, ca, mānavaḥ, ātmani, eva, ca, santuṣṭaḥ, tasya, kāryaṃ, na, vidyate || 17 ||
3:17.anvaya_iast: tasmāt, asaktaḥ, satataṃ, kāryaṃ, karma, samācara, hi, asaktaḥ, pūruṣaḥ, karma, ācaran, param, āpnoti || 19 ||
3:17.translation: But that man who rejoices only in theSelf and is satisfied with the Self, and is contented only in the Self-for him there is no duty to perform.
3:17.explanation: The sage does not depend on external objects for his happiness. He is ite satisfied with the Self. He finds his joy? bliss and contentment within his own Self. For such a sage who has knowledge of the Self? there is nothing to do. He has already done all actions. He has satisfied all his desires. He has complete satisfaction. (Cf.II.55).
3:17.word_meanings: यः — who; तु — but; आत्मरतिः — who rejoices in the Self; एव — only; स्यात् — may be; आत्मतृप्तः — satisfied in the Self; च — and; मानवः — the man; आत्मनि — in the Self; एव — only; च — and; सन्तुष्टः — contented; तस्य — his; कार्यम् — work to be done; न — not; विद्यते — is.

3:18.pada_sa: न, एव, तस्य, कृतेन, अर्थः, न, अकृतेन, इह, कश्चन, न, च, अस्य, सर्वभूतेषु, कश्चित्, अर्थव्यपाश्रयः ॥ १८ ॥
3:18.anvaya_sa: जनकादयः, कर्मणा, इव, संसिद्धिम्, आस्थिताः, हि, लोकसंग्रहं, संपश्यन्, अपि, कर्तुम्, एव, अर्हसि ॥ २० ॥
3:18.pada_iast: na, eva, tasya, kṛtena, arthaḥ, na, akṛtena, iha, kaścana, na, ca, asya, sarvabhūteṣu, kaścit, arthavyapāśrayaḥ || 18 ||
3:18.anvaya_iast: janakādayaḥ, karmaṇā, iva, saṃsiddhim, āsthitāḥ, hi, lokasaṃgrahaṃ, saṃpaśyan, api, kartum, eva, arhasi || 20 ||
3:18.translation: For him there is no concern here at all with performing action; nor any (concern) with nonperformance. Moreover, for him there is no dependence on any object to serve any purpose.
3:18.explanation: The sage who is thus rejoicing in the Self does not gain anything by doing any action. For him really no purpose is served by an action. No evil (Pratyavaya Dosha) can touch him from inaction. He does not lose anything from inaction. He need not depend upon anybody to gain a particular object. He need not exert himself to get the favour of anybody.
3:18.word_meanings: न — not; एव — even; तस्य — of hi; कृतेन — by action; अर्थः — concern; न — not; अकृतेन — by actions not done; इह — here; कश्चन् — any; न — not; च — and; अस्य — of this man; सर्वभूतेषु — in all beings; कश्चित् — any; अर्थव्यपाश्रयः — depending for any object.

iast: tasmād asaktaḥ satataṁ kāryaṁ karma samācara
asakto hy ācaran karma param āpnoti pūruṣaḥ

3:19.pada_sa: तस्मात्, असक्तः, सततं, कार्यं, कर्म, समाचर, असक्तः, हि, आचरन्, कर्म, परम्, आप्नोति, पूरुषः ॥ १९ ॥
3:19.anvaya_sa: श्रेष्ठः, यत्, यत्, आचरति, इतरः, जनः, तत्, तत्, एव, (अनुवर्तते) सः, यत्, प्रमाणं, कुरुते, लोकः, तत्, अनुवर्तते ॥ २१ ॥
3:19.pada_iast: tasmāt, asaktaḥ, satataṃ, kāryaṃ, karma, samācara, asaktaḥ, hi, ācaran, karma, param, āpnoti, pūruṣaḥ || 19 ||
3:19.anvaya_iast: śreṣṭhaḥ, yat, yat, ācarati, itaraḥ, janaḥ, tat, tat, eva, (anuvartate) saḥ, yat, pramāṇaṃ, kurute, lokaḥ, tat, anuvartate || 21 ||
3:19.translation: Therefore, remaining unattached, always perform the obligatory duty, for, by performing (one's) duty without attachment, a person attains the Highest.
3:19.explanation: If you perform actions without attachment? for the sake of the Lord? you will attain to Selfrealisation through purity of heart. (Cf.II.64IV.19?23XVIII.49).
3:19.word_meanings: तस्मात् — therefore; असक्तः — without attachment; सततम् — always; कार्यम् — which should be done; कर्म — action; समाचर — perform; असक्तः — without attachment; हि — because; आचरन् — performing; कर्म — action; परम् — the Supreme; आप्नोति — attains; पूरुषः — man.

3:20.pada_sa: कर्मणा, एव, हि, संसिद्धिं, आस्थिताः, जनकादयः, लोकसंग्रहम्, एव, अपि, सम्पश्यन्, कर्तुम्, अर्हसि ॥ २० ॥
